era-15.note: Plain white field with the black shahada in two lines matches; the reference has no black border and uses calligraphic text (the 2021 variant with Pashto subtext is Flag_of_the_Islamic_Emirate_of_Afghanistan_(with_Pashto_subtext).svg). The drawing adds a thin black border and sets the text in a plain typeface.

era-17.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The Republic of Afghanistan flag from 1974 to 1978 is a HORIZONTAL black-red-green tricolour with the eagle emblem at the upper hoist. The drawing is a vertical tricolour with a text label in the centre, which is the layout of the 1973-1974 flag (Flag_of_Afghanistan_(1973–1974).svg, vertical, monarchy emblem minus the date), so layout and emblem place do not match the eagle flag described in the caption. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1747.note: Black field with a white central emblem matches the 1901-1919 flag in layout; the emblem is a plain white oval where the reference has a mosque with flags. Evidence notes this design is documented only from the 1880s, not for the Durrani period.

era-1919.note: Vertical black-red-green tricolour with a central emblem matches the 1931-1973 flag in layout. The emblem is a plain gold disc (reference: white mosque with flags and wheat), and the card starts in 1919 when the flags were different (black field, then other tricolours to 1931).

era-2001.note: Vertical black-red-green tricolour matches. The central emblem and shahada are replaced by the text label "SHAHADA + EMBLEM"; the reference has a white wreathed mosque emblem with the shahada above it.

era-27.note: White field with black shahada matches the 1997-2001 reference (the 1996-97 flag was plain white). Black border and plain typeface are the differences, as for the 2021 card.

era-27-1.note: Red field with a yellow emblem at the hoist matches the 1978-1980 flag in layout, with the emblem reduced to a yellow rectangle labelled "EMBLEM". The card's dates run to 1992, but from 1980 to 1992 the flag was a black-red-green tricolour with an emblem (Flag_of_Afghanistan_(1980–1987).svg); the drawing shows only the 1978-80 flag.

era-28.note: Horizontal green-white-black tricolour matches. The central emblem is only the text label "EMBLEM"; the reference has a yellow wreathed mosque emblem with the shahada on the white band.

era-1479.note: Red field with a white crescent and star, as in the 1844-1922 Ottoman state flag. The reference crescent is larger with the star at its mouth; ours is smaller and offset. The earlier part of the era (1479-1844) used other Ottoman flags that this drawing does not show.

era-1516.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Wikipedia (citing al-Jilali) says the Regency's main flags were plain red and devoid of any symbol, unlike the Ottoman crescent-and-star flag. The drawing is a red field with a white crescent and star, and the crescent path is degenerate so it renders as a thin sliver and a star. Fix: plain red field. The Commons file for the Dey/Regent is a plain red flag; Flag_of_Regency_of_Algiers.svg is a different green-red design with yellow. (FOTW's contributor disagrees, saying the Ottoman flag flew.) It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1830.note: Vertical blue-white-red tricolour, blue at the hoist, same as the French tricolour reference.

era-1962.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Green and white halves are right, but the crescent path is degenerate (its two arcs coincide) so no crescent shows, only a small star at the dividing line. The reference has a large red crescent on the green side over the boundary with a red star in the white half. Fix: proper crescent and star. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1077bce.note: A text label on a dashed frame; it draws no flag or emblem, which suits a period with none documented. Commons has no flag or banner file for this polity/period (searched Commons file names and the Wikipedia article image lists), so there is nothing to compare against. The card reads FRAGMENTED DYNASTIES.

era-1550bce.note: Sun disk and uraeus stand-in. Ours is a gold disc inside a shield outline with a curved band and two stubs, not a rearing cobra; a uraeus photo on Commons (Walters 22367, found by search, not compared visually) shows a rearing cobra. Caption says reconstructed.

The card reads HYKSOS RULE (NORTH).

era-2055bce.note: Pschent stand-in. The Commons double crown is a white crown rising out of a red crown with a curl; ours is a white disc over a red pointed block on gold, so the white-on-red idea matches but the crown outlines do not. Caption says reconstructed.

era-2181bce.note: A text label on a dashed frame; it draws no flag or emblem, which suits a period with none documented. The card reads REGIONAL GOVERNORS.

era-2686bce.note: Redrawn as the white Hedjet crown the caption names; a reconstruction of the symbol, since no flag survives from the Old Kingdom.

era-305bce.note: The caption calls this a reconstruction of the diadem and eagle device, and the Commons Ptolemaic eagle file (found by Commons search, not compared visually) shows the eagle motif. Ours shows neither: a gold shield-ring on dark blue with a curved band underneath, so the picture does not show the eagle or diadem the caption names. Fine as a stand-in only because the caption says reconstructed.

era-30bce.note: A text label on a dashed frame; it draws no flag or emblem, which suits a period with none documented. Commons has no flag or banner file for this period (searched Commons file names and the Wikipedia article image lists), so there is nothing to compare against. The card reads ROMAN ANNEXATION.

era-3100bce.note: Serekh stand-in. The Commons serekh is a rectangle with palace-facade panelling and a Horus falcon on top; ours keeps the cream panelled rectangle on a brown field but replaces the falcon with a gold blob inside the frame and a small base block. Caption says reconstructed.

era-664bce.note: Reconstructed Pschent stand-in. The Commons double crown is a white bowling-pin crown seated in a red crown with a tall curl; ours is a white disc on a gold column on a maroon field, which keeps the white-over-gold idea but not the crown outline or the red lower crown. Caption says reconstructed.

era-1278.note: Cream panel with translucent red and blue bars standing for the bishop and the count. The caption says schematic; nothing documents a flag for the founding period (FOTW infers the Catalan Quatre Barres from Olle, and neither source describes episcopal or comital heraldry as a flag).

era-1806.note: Redrawn: Vertical yellow-red bicolour, which Flags of the World gives for 1806-1866. Earlier drawing differed from the reference.

era-1866.note: Vertical blue-yellow-red tricolour as the modern flag. The coat of arms (four quarters: mitre and crozier, Foix pales, Catalan bars, two cows) is reduced to a small cream box divided red, yellow and cream, and it shows the modern arms; the sources say the 1866 flag was plain or had a coronet and horizontal stripes (Flag_of_Andorra_(end_of_the_19th_century-c._1930s).svg), arms only from about 1939.

era-1575.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The drawing is a horizontal green-white-red triband with a red box and gold disc at the hoist. The Portuguese flag in the reference is a vertical green and red bicolour (green about two fifths at the hoist) with the arms and armillary sphere on the join. fixSvg draws it with a simplified emblem. Note this is the post-1911 republican flag; the monarchy's blue-and-white flags were used earlier in the 1575-1975 span. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1975.note: The drawing is the Wikimedia Commons file 'Flag of Angola.svg' (Public domain), with scripts, text and external links removed so it embeds in the page; its shapes and colours are the file's own.

era-1516.note: Same Cross of Burgundy drawing as 1776: white with a straight-barred red saltire standing in for the ragged-stave cross of the reference. The field colour varied by period in the sources, and no flag specific to the territory is documented.

era-1776.note: White field with a red saltire (Cross of Burgundy) as in the reference; the reference saltire is made of ragged, knotted staves, ours is two straight bars in a darker brick red. Commons describes this flag as used in the Spanish viceroyalties (New Spain and Peru); use specifically at Rio de la Plata is inferred in the evidence row. The red-and-yellow Spanish flag of 1785 (Flag_of_Spain_(1785–1873,_1875–1931).svg) replaced it at sea.

era-1810.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The Commons drawing of Belgrano's 1812 flag is a two-band flag, white over light blue. Ours is a three-band light blue - white - light blue flag with no sun, which is the later design without the sun, not Belgrano's flag the caption names. fixSvg gives the white-over-sky-blue bicolour. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1816.note: Blue-white-blue with a gold sun on the white band, as in the Commons 1818 flag (the sun was added in 1818, two years after 1816; the caption says so). the sun is a gold disc with eight triangular rays, where the reference Sun of May has a face and about thirty-two alternating straight and wavy rays.

era-1820.note: Ours is the plain sun flag for the whole 1820s-1861 span. Commons shows the sun flag for 1820-1829 (Flag_of_Argentina_(1818–1819,_1820–1829,_1861–2010).svg) but other flags for the rest: a Confederation military flag with the national arms at the centre (c. 1840), a 1840 Rosas-era flag with red marks, and the State of Buenos Aires flag of 1852-61. So for 1829-1861 the single sun flag is not what the references show, and the caption's 'same flag flown by both sides' is contradicted by the evidence row. No fixSvg: no single replacement fits the whole era. The caption now says which period the drawing fits.

era-1861.note: The drawing is the Wikimedia Commons file 'Flag of Argentina.svg' (Public domain), with scripts, text and external links removed so it embeds in the page; its shapes and colours are the file's own.

era-1045.note: Caption calls it a generic representation. Ours is a brown field with a pale ring and dot, which matches no documented flag: the Commons Cilician flags (Catalan Atlas, Book of Knowledge) are red-on-gold lion or cross banners and the Khachen standard is red with a white cross and four gold crosses. Stays schematic; nothing attested is depicted.

era-1375.note: Caption describes it as a partition (Ottoman crescent west, Safavid roundel east), i.e. an invented composite. The Ottoman half (red with a pale crescent) resembles the Commons Ottoman flag in shape and colour; the Safavid half (teal with a gold disc) has no Commons or evidence-row reference (FOTW describes the Iravan khanate flag as dark red and white diagonally with a yellow device). Left schematic as captioned.

era-1828.note: Black-yellow-white horizontal bands match Commons Flag_of_Russia_(1858-1896), the imperial flag. Caveats: ours uses a cream white; the flag covers only 1858-96 of this 1828-1915 span (white-blue-red afterwards); and it is a Russian flag, not an Armenian one; the evidence row found no source tying it to Armenia.

era-1918.note: Red-blue-orange horizontal equal thirds, same as the Commons First Republic file; shades paler in ours only.

era-1920.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Reference (1952-91 flag) is red with a quarter-height blue stripe across the middle and a gold hammer and sickle with a red star in the upper hoist; ours draws a gold plus-shaped cross in the upper hoist and puts the blue stripe near the bottom edge. The earlier Soviet flags (1920-22 plain red, 1922 letters, 1936-52 hammer and sickle with Armenian letters, no blue stripe) are not drawn either. fixSvg draws the 1952 flag; not viewed after drawing, emblem simplified. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1991.note: Red-blue-orange horizontal equal thirds, no emblem, same as Flag_of_Armenia.svg; ours is somewhat paler in each colour but hue and order match.

era-885.note: Redrawn: Dark-red field with a white lion beneath a cross, as the Commons Bagratuni flag. Earlier drawing differed from the reference.

era-1788.note: Union Flag as flown after 1801 (red diagonals of St Patrick, here drawn centred rather than counterchanged). The flag raised in 1788 was the earlier Union Flag without the red diagonals (Flag_of_Great_Britain_(1707–1800).svg), so the drawing is right only for about 1801-1901; the evidence also says nothing shows it was the formal ensign of all six colonies.

era-1901.note: Blue Ensign with the Union Jack canton, a Commonwealth Star under it and five Southern Cross stars in the fly matches in layout. The stars are all five-pointed; the reference has a seven-pointed Commonwealth Star and seven-pointed Cross stars (the original 1901 flag, …(1901–1903).svg, had a six-pointed Federation Star and Cross stars of varied points).

era-1156.note: Same red-white-red design as the reference, but the reference file is dated from 1230: nothing seen shows these colours before 1230, so the 1156-1230 part of this era is projected backwards.

era-1282.note: Same red-white-red design as the reference (the colours of the Bindenschild, documented from 1230); medieval banner proportions are not attested by the reference.

era-1453.note: Red-white-red horizontal triband in the colours of the Austrian arms (Bindenschild). Matches the Commons flag file; the proportions and use of a banner of this exact form in the 15th century are not shown by the reference, which is a modern drawing of the colours.

era-1918.note: Plain red-white-red triband, same as the reference; grid match was complete.

era-1919.note: Plain red-white-red triband, same as the reference; grid match was complete.

era-1938.note: Redrawn after the Commons Flag of Germany (1935–1945): red field, white disc, black swastika turned on its point.

era-1945.note: Same red-white-red triband as the reference file (dated 1230-1934, 1945-2000). The drawing adds a dashed black border as a page device for "sovereignty suspended"; that frame is not part of the flag.

era-1955.note: Red-white-red horizontal triband, equal stripes; same design as the reference. Grid comparison of the rendered drawing against the 400px reference matched on every cell.

era-1934.note: Emblem redrawn by hand on 2026-10-25 and compared by eye with the reference: same layout and colours, emblem simplified (shape and detail reduced).

era-1538.note: Redrawn: Green field with a gold lion carrying a sun, as the Commons Safavid flag (itself a later reconstruction). Earlier drawing differed from the reference.

era-1747.note: Teal field with a gold disc and arc. The caption calls it a generic stand-in, and no khanate banner looks like it: the one Commons khanate flag (Ganja) is green with a red centre band and gold emblems. Left as a labelled stand-in.

era-1813.note: Black, yellow and white horizontal stripes, same as the 1858-1896 Russian imperial flag. That flag only applied from 1858 to 1896; before 1858 and after 1896 (white-blue-red) Russia flew other flags, so the drawing fits only part of the 1813-1918 era.

era-1918.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Stripes (light blue, red, green), white crescent and star as in the reference, but the star has five points and the reference star has eight; the crescent is a thin sliver and the whole emblem sits about 8% of the width too far right (reference crescent centred just under half-way, star at about 57%). Fix: eight-point star, fuller crescent, moved left (the 1918-1920 flag has the same layout). It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1920.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The 1952-1991 flag is red with a wide dark-blue band across the bottom quarter and a gold hammer and sickle with a star in the upper hoist. Ours has a narrow light-blue strip (about 7% of the height) and a plain gold cross in place of the hammer and sickle, with no star. Fix: dark-blue quarter band, hammer and sickle with star (simplified). It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1991.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Stripes (light blue, red, green), white crescent and star as in the reference, but the star has five points and the reference star has eight; the crescent is a thin sliver and the whole emblem sits about 8% of the width too far right (reference crescent centred just under half-way, star at about 57%). Fix: eight-point star, fuller crescent, moved left. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-861.note: Green field with a white crescent, labelled by its caption as an informed representation. I found no Commons flag file for the Shirvanshahs, and the Wikipedia article shows none, so nothing contradicts or supports the colours; the evidence row's one hint (a gold flag in a court poet's divan) points to gold, not green.

era-1718.note: Blue ensign with a Union Flag canton and a badge on a white disc at the fly, as in the Commons Bahamas ensign (1869-1904). The reference badge is a ship scene (the colonial seal: a ship chasing pirate ships); ours shows a gold sun on a blue triangle, which the caption calls a sun and sailing ship and the evidence row says is not what the badge shows. The ensign with a badge is documented only from 1869, so 1718-1869 is not covered.

era-1973.note: Aquamarine, gold, aquamarine horizontal bands with a black triangle at the hoist, as in the reference. The reference triangle reaches slightly further across (its apex about 43% of the flag's length for a 2:1 flag against about 37% in ours) and the aquamarine is a little greener-darker; the design is the same.

era-1204.note: Caption says informed reconstruction. The Commons Husain Shah alam is an ornate gold banner on a long pennant shape; the drawing is a plain maroon field with a white crescent, which is not in that reference.

era-1576.note: Caption says schematic. The Commons Bengal Subah standard is a white and teal pennant and the nautical flag is white with yellow marks; neither shows a green field with a gold sun. Wikipedia lists a moss-green alam, which failed verification (evidence row), so this green/sun design is not supported by the reference images.

era-1757.note: Red and white horizontal stripes with a Union canton as in the references (13 stripes starting with red, canton about seven stripes deep). The canton shows only the cross of St George and a saltire: the 1801 reference adds the Irish saltire and the 1707 reference has the older Union.

era-1858.note: Caption says schematic. The drawing is a dark-blue ensign with a Union canton and a gold star badge in the fly, which matches the layout of the Bengal Presidency ensign (Flag_of_British_Bengal.svg, with a different badge). It is not the Union flag with the Star of India at the centre (Governor-General flag) nor the red ensign (British_Raj_Red_Ensign.svg) that the caption text names.

era-1947.note: Dark green field, white hoist strip (about a fifth against the reference quarter), white crescent and five-pointed star at centre, crescent opening toward the fly: same design as the reference; crescent and star are a little smaller than the reference.

era-1971.note: Green field and red disc as in the 1971 reference. The reference carries a large gold map of Bangladesh filling most of the disc; the drawing has only a small gold blob toward the upper part of the disc, so the map is far smaller and not recognisable as a map.

era-1972.note: Green field with a red disc set slightly toward the hoist: same design as the reference (disc position and size agree).

era-1627.note: Blue Ensign with a Union Flag canton and a badge in the fly matches the 1870-1966 flag in outline (the badge there is a coloured seal with Britannia and a trident; ours is a ring around a white stick trident). The card spans 1627-1966, and the sources give no flag for Barbados before 1833; the Union Jack itself dates from 1801, so the drawing is out of period for roughly the first 240 years. The caption now says which period the drawing fits.

era-1966.note: Ultramarine-gold-ultramarine vertical bands with the black trident head centred on the gold band: matches in layout and size. The broken trident is drawn with straight strokes and a long stem instead of the reference's curved, barbed prongs with a cut-off shaft.

era-1392.note: Red field with a white figure matches the banner's colours. The reference shows a white mounted knight with raised sword and blue-detailed shield; the drawing reduces him to an egg-shaped outline with a block below, not recognisable as a horseman.

era-1795.note: White-blue-red horizontal tricolour matches the Russian civil/merchant flag. The official state flag of 1858-1896 was black-yellow-white (Flag_of_Russia_(1858–1896).svg), not shown; the evidence found no source tying either flag to Belarusian lands.

era-1918.note: White-red-white, as the reference.

era-1919.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: References are plain red (Flag_of_the_Lithuanian-Byelorussian_SSR.svg, 1919-1920) and red with gold Cyrillic letters ССРБ at the hoist (BSSR 1919-1927). The drawing is red with a gold star and a dashed border; neither the star nor the dashed border appears on either reference. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1922.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The 1951-1991 flag has red over green in 2:1, a hoist band that is RED with a white ornament (white edge strips), and a gold hammer-and-sickle under a star in the canton. The drawing has a thin green stripe (about 1/7 instead of 1/3), a plain cream hoist band, and a star over two gold bars instead of hammer and sickle. The 1937-1951 flag (…(1937–1951).svg) was plain red with the emblem and no ornament or green, and the 1919-1937 flags had gold letters on red, so no flag in the era matches the drawing. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1991.note: White-red-white horizontal bands in 5:4:5 proportion (reference proportions), as drawn.

era-1995.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Red over green (2:1) matches. The hoist ornament band is wrong: the reference is a RED band carrying a WHITE rushnyk pattern; the drawing is a cream band with small red squares, i.e. the colours are inverted and the pattern is a grid of squares rather than the diamond chain. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1384.note: Same drawing as the 1581 card: white field with red saltire, straight bars instead of the ragged cross, five dots as badges. Matches the design of the reference, not its ragged detail.

era-1581.note: White field with a red saltire as in the reference, but the saltire is drawn as straight bars with round ends instead of the ragged (knotted-branch) cross, and five small dark dots stand in for the fire-steel badges. The red-white-yellow civil ensign also attested for the period is not drawn.

era-1795.note: Vertical blue-white-red, blue at the hoist, the same as the French tricolour reference. Whether it was the flag of the annexed departments is a text question.

era-1815.note: Red-white-blue horizontal tricolour, same order as the reference; the blue is slightly lighter-cornflower versus the dark reference but the hue is right.

era-1830.note: Drawing shows the vertical black-yellow-red of 23 Jan 1831 onward, matching the reference. The very first 1830 flag was horizontal red-yellow-black (Flag_of_Belgium_(1830).svg), which the caption mentions but the drawing does not show.

era-1914.note: Horizontal black-white-red equal bands, identical to the German Empire flag. Whether this flag flew over occupied Belgium is not established by the sources (text issue, not a drawing issue).

era-1918.note: Vertical black-yellow-red, same as the reference (the 1936 FOTW confirmation describes the same design).

era-1940.note: Redrawn after the Commons Flag of Germany (1935–1945): red field, white disc, black swastika turned on its point.

era-1944.note: Vertical black-yellow-red, black at the hoist, same as the reference.

era-1714.note: Emblem redrawn by hand on 2026-10-25 and compared by eye with the reference: same layout and colours, emblem simplified (shape and detail reduced).

era-1638.note: Redrawn: The 1606 Union Flag: blue field, white St Andrew saltire, red St George cross with white edging. Earlier drawing differed from the reference.

era-1862.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The Commons files for British Honduras are a navy-blue ensign with a Union Flag canton and a white disc badge in the middle of the fly. Ours has a teal-green field, a dark teal canton in place of the blue Union ground, and a plain gold disc that sits low (70% down against the vertical centre). Fix: navy field and canton, badge disc centred in the fly. The Union Flag is simplified (no red St Patrick diagonals) and the badge is a plain disc with a ring and block standing for the arms. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1950.note: Plain blue field with a white central disc holding the arms, as in the 1950-1981 file. The arms are reduced to a brown ring and dark rectangle.

era-1981.note: Blue field with a red stripe at top and bottom (thin white edge lines) and a white central disc, as in the reference. The coat of arms inside the disc (mahogany tree, figures, tools, wreath of leaves) is reduced to a brown ring and a dark rectangle. (The Commons files 1981-2019 and the current one differ only in the wreath and details.)

era-1625.note: A dark red field with a gold disc and a dark shield: an invented stand-in; the caption says no single documented flag and calls it a reconstruction. Wikipedia's Dahomey article shows a white-and-red flag with a war elephant (Dahomey_flag_1889.svg) and a Behanzin banner, neither of which the drawing resembles.

era-1894.note: Vertical blue-white-red tricolour, blue at hoist: matches the French flag.

era-1958.note: Green hoist band (two fifths) with yellow over red on the fly: matches the reference.

era-1960.note: Green hoist band (two fifths) with yellow over red on the fly: matches the reference.

era-1975.note: Plain green field with a red five-pointed star in the canton: matches; our star is about a third larger and set further from the corner than in the reference.

era-1990.note: Green hoist band (two fifths) with yellow over red on the fly: matches the reference.

era-1559.note: White field with a red diagonal saltire, as the Cross of Burgundy reference; straight round-capped bars short of the corners instead of knotted branches.

era-1776.note: White field with a red diagonal saltire, as the Cross of Burgundy reference (the flag Wikipedia's Bolivia gallery uses for the colonial period). The bars are straight, round-capped and stop short of the corners, where the reference has knotted branches reaching the corners.

era-1825.note: Red, yellow, green horizontal triband, same as the civil flag reference (grid match complete). The state flag adds the arms in the centre. The tricolour dates from 1851 per the evidence row; the 1825-1826 civil flag (Civil_flag_of_Bolivia_(1825-1826).svg) was a different design, so the first quarter-century of the era is not what is drawn.

era-1154.note: Redrawn: Dark-blue swallow-tailed banner with a white cross, as the Commons flag attributed to Stjepan II Kotromanic. Earlier drawing differed from the reference.

era-1918.note: Blue-white-red as the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes flag. (The short-lived State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs flag of 1918, File:Flag_of_the_State_of_Slovenes,_Croats_and_Serbs.svg, was red-white-blue; not what this card is about.)

era-1929.note: Blue-white-red horizontal tricolour, bands equal, as the reference.

era-1939.note: Red-white-blue tricolour with a plain chequy shield on the white band, as the Banovina reference (the civil variant, Civil_Flag_of_Banovina_of_Croatia.svg, has no shield).

era-1941.note: Red-white-blue tricolour with the crownless chequy shield (first square white) on the white band matches. The Ustasha U emblem near the hoist is drawn as a plain dark U on the red band; the reference has a white field with a blue U inside a curl.

era-1943.note: Blue-white-red tricolour with a plain red star in the white band (no yellow edge), as the reference.

era-1946.note: Blue-white-red horizontal tricolour with a yellow-bordered red star in the white band; matches the reference. Star is somewhat smaller than the reference.

era-1947.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Reference is the red-white-blue tricolour with ONLY a large yellow-bordered red five-pointed star in the centre; no chequy shield. The drawing keeps the full chequy shield and adds a small star above it, so the emblem and layout differ from the reference (and from the caption in which the star replaces the arms). It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1990.note: Red-white-blue tricolour with the chequy shield (13 red, 12 white, first square red) matches. The crown of five historic shields is reduced to five plain blue/red squares (no star-and-crescent, lions, bars, marten or Istrian goat) and the squares sit lopsided to the left instead of in a symmetrical arc.

era-1991.note: Red over blue over white, equal bands, matches the plain Krajina tricolour. The state-flag version (File:State_Flag_of_Serbian_Krajina_(1991).svg) adds a coat of arms in the centre of the blue band; the drawing omits it.

era-925.note: Checked against the fetched Wikipedia text (no Commons image of the lone shield found): a golden six-pointed star over a silver crescent on a (light) blue shield; the drawing has exactly that, on a blue heater shield. It is an emblem, not a flag, which the caption states.

era-1420.note: Emblem redrawn by hand on 2026-10-25 and compared by eye with the reference: same layout and colours, emblem simplified (shape and detail reduced).

era-1192.note: Caption says reconstructed. Barry of eight, white and blue, matches the Lusignan arms; the red crowned lion rampant is replaced by a plain red shield-shaped blob with a gold edge.

era-1571.note: Redrawn: Ottoman red banner with a single dark crescent (no star), as on the Commons c.1490-1701 flag. Earlier drawing differed from the reference.

era-1878.note: Union Flag, as the reference. The evidence notes a Blue Ensign with a CHC badge (Flag_of_Cyprus_(1881–1922).svg) was also approved in 1881; the card's claim that no badge existed is a text point, the drawing itself matches the Union Flag.

era-1925.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: A Blue Ensign has the Union Jack only in the upper-hoist quarter and a plain blue fly carrying the badge (two red lions, for Cyprus 1922-1960). The drawing spreads the Union Jack across the whole flag and adds a gold disc, so the layout and the badge are both wrong. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1960.note: Emblem redrawn by hand on 2026-10-25 and compared by eye with the reference: same layout and colours, emblem simplified (shape and detail reduced).

era-1489.note: Caption says reconstructed. The reference Venetian flag is a red field with a gold winged lion holding a book; the drawing keeps the red field and a gold lion but reduces it to an ellipse with arcs and a dot, not recognisable as a lion. No source ties this flag to Cyprus. The emblem was redrawn by hand on 2026-10-25.

era-1918.note: Wedge flag, matching the Commons Czechoslovak flag. The wedge dates from 30 March 1920; from October 1918 to 1920 the flag was plain white over red (Commons has Flag_of_Czechoslovakia_(1920_proposal).svg for the design debate), so the first 18 months of the era are not shown.

era-1938.note: Wedge flag, matching the Commons Czechoslovak flag in layout and hue.

era-1939.note: White, red, blue horizontal tricolour in that order, as in the Commons Protectorate flag.

era-1945.note: Wedge flag, matching the Commons Czechoslovak flag in layout and hue.

era-1948.note: Wedge flag without any emblem, matching the Commons Czechoslovak flag in layout and hue.

era-1989.note: Shows the federal wedge flag (white over red, blue triangle), identical to the Commons Czechoslovak flag. The evidence note says the Czech lands also had a plain white-over-red flag in law from 1990; that is not drawn, but the drawing is a correct picture of the federal flag.

era-1993.note: White over red with a blue hoist triangle reaching to the middle, as in the reference; hues and wedge depth match.

era-1526.note: Emblem redrawn by hand on 2026-10-25 and compared by eye with the reference: same layout and colours, emblem simplified (shape and detail reduced).

era-1198.note: Emblem redrawn by hand on 2026-10-25 and compared by eye with the reference: same layout and colours, emblem simplified (shape and detail reduced).

era-1158.note: Ours is a single-tailed white lion pictogram on red. The Commons Banner_of_Přemyslid_family.svg (described as the banner of the Přemyslid dynasty, St Wenceslas and the Duchy of Bohemia, undated) is a black eagle on white, not a lion; Wikipedia's coat-of-arms text gives a lion first shown with one tail but also a black eagle for the early 13th century, and no source read dates either to 1158-1198. No dated reference for this exact period found, so the drawing cannot be called faithful or wrong. The emblem was redrawn by hand on 2026-10-25.

era-1219.note: Red field with a white Nordic cross offset toward the hoist, as in Flag_of_Denmark.svg (proportions slightly different, 3:2 against 37:28). (The 1219 date is the legend; the drawing is the Dannebrog as it looks now.)

era-1397.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The Commons Kalmar Union flag is a gold field with a plain red Nordic cross. Ours adds three white discs (standing for the three crowns) that are not in the reference; the evidence row notes neither source describes the crowns. Cross and gold match. Fix: remove the discs. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1523.note: Red field with a white Nordic cross offset toward the hoist, as in Flag_of_Denmark.svg (proportions slightly different, 3:2 against 37:28).

era-1814.note: Red field with a white Nordic cross offset toward the hoist, as in Flag_of_Denmark.svg (proportions slightly different, 3:2 against 37:28).

era-1896.note: Vertical blue-white-red French tricolour, as the reference; no T.F.A.I. marking is drawn, which agrees with the evidence.

era-1977.note: Light blue over green with a white hoist triangle bearing a red five-pointed star, as the reference (the drawing's blue is a more cyan tint, the star a little smaller).

era-1763.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The Union Jack of 1763 was the Great Britain flag of 1707-1800 (Commons): blue with a white St Andrew's saltire and the red St George's cross with white edging, and no red diagonal. Ours includes St Patrick's red saltire inside the white saltire, which belongs to the 1801 Union Flag, so it is anachronistic for 1763-1801. The evidence row notes the French royal flag (Commons Royal_flag_of_France.svg, blue with gold lilies) flew in 1778-84. fixSvg draws the 1707 Union Flag. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1783.note: Blue ensign with a Union Flag canton and a badge at the fly, as in the Commons colonial ensigns (1961/1965-78). Ours places the badge on a white disc with a green leaf shape and a red dot; the Commons badge is a shield-and-parrot device with no white disc visible. The evidence row notes a Dominica-badge ensign is documented only from 1955, so the picture applies to the last decades of this 1783-1978 era.

era-1978.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Green field, cross of three parallel stripes and a red disc with a parrot ringed by ten green stars, as in the reference. The cross is built wrong: in the Commons flag each arm is three side-by-side stripes, yellow, black and white (yellow on the hoist/top side, white on the other, black in between, equal width). Ours nests them concentrically (a wide yellow bar, a narrower black bar inside it, a thin cream bar at the centre), so the stripe order across each arm is yellow-black-cream-black-yellow. The red disc is also too small (about 30% of the height against half the height in the reference) and the parrot is a simplified shape, as the caption says. fixSvg redraws the cross and disc. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1492.note: White with a red saltire, the Cross of Burgundy flag, as the reference; the reference saltire is made of ragged, knotted staves, ours is two straight bars in a brighter red-orange. Wikipedia assigns the flag to the Captaincy General of Santo Domingo 1492-1795; FOTW dates its use from 1506.

era-1795.note: Blue-white-red vertical tricolour, the same design as the Commons flag of France, used here as a stand-in. The evidence row says no source states which flag flew over Santo Domingo in 1795-1809 and FOTW supports a French tricolour only for Toussaint Louverture's 1801 occupation; the Commons Flag_of_Spanish_Haiti.svg (a yellow, blue, red flag) is a further candidate for 1821 only.

era-1822.note: Blue over red horizontal bicolour with a small light panel at the centre, as in the Commons Haitian flag of 1820-49, whose panel holds the arms (palm tree and trophy of arms). Ours shows the panel as an empty cream rectangle with a gold outline.

era-1844.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The Commons flag of 1844 has both top quarters blue and both bottom quarters red around the white cross (the red and blue were flipped on the fly side only in 1865, when the arms were added, per the evidence row). Ours shows the post-1865 arrangement (top-fly red, bottom-fly blue) with a central disc, so it is the later flag. fixSvg draws blue on top, red below, white cross, no arms. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1861.note: Red-yellow-red horizontal flag with a half-height yellow band, as in the Commons Spanish flag of 1785-1873. The reference carries the Spanish arms on the yellow band near the hoist; ours is plain. The evidence row notes which flag flew in 1861-65 is itself inferred (FOTW lists other candidates).

era-1865.note: White cross with blue and red quarters in the same arrangement as the current flag (blue top-hoist and bottom-fly, red top-fly and bottom-hoist). The reference has the national coat of arms at the crossing; ours replaces it with a plain cream disc with a gold rim and dot.

era-1390.note: A red field with a blue square holding four dots, in a dashed gold frame. The caption calls it a reconstruction after the royal arms; it does not resemble the Commons Afonso I royal banner or the Portuguese-granted arms, and Wikipedia shows an actual banner, so the invented emblem is a stand-in only.

era-1885.note: Single yellow star on blue: matches; ours is about two thirds the size of the reference star (about 24% against 35% of the flag width) and the blue is darker.

era-1908.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Ours has a large star ringed by six small stars; the reference Free State flag (unchanged under Belgium per FOTW) is a single large yellow star on blue. The six small stars belong to the 1960 flag. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1960.note: Blue field with a yellow-bordered red diagonal and a yellow star at the hoist: matches the 1963-66 flag (the caption says so). The earlier 1960-63 flag of this card span (large central star and six small stars, Flag_of_the_Republic_of_the_Congo_(Léopoldville)_(1960–1963).svg) is not drawn.

era-1971.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Light green field and yellow disc with an arm holding a red torch match, but ours puts the disc 35 units left of centre (the reference disc is centred and larger) and draws the arm black and thin; the reference arm is brown. The torch is a loose scribble rather than a hand holding a flame. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1997.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Ours shows the sky-blue flag with a yellow-bordered red diagonal and one star, which is the 2006 flag (reference Flag_of_the_Democratic_Republic_of_the_Congo.svg). The 1997-2006 flag was plain blue with a large central star and six small stars in a column at the hoist. Fix redraws the 1997 flag; the 2006 design belongs to a separate card starting 2006. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1563.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The drawing is a red field with cream bands across the top and bottom and a gold diamond. The Cross of Burgundy reference (the flag the evidence row says flew over Ecuador in the colonial period) is white with a red saltire. fixSvg draws it (straight bars, the reference has knotted branches). It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1809.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The drawing is a teal field with three white dots joined in a triangle. The Commons Quito revolution flag is a red field with a white saltire, which agrees with the evidence row (the Spanish inventory describes a red taffeta flag with a white saltire). fixSvg redraws it. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1822.note: Yellow double-height band over blue and red, as the Gran Colombia reference; the reference has the arms/emblem at the centre, which the drawing omits.

era-1830.note: Yellow band of double height over blue and red bands: identical to the civil flag reference. The state flag also carries the arms in the centre, which the civil flag (and the drawing) omit. (The 1845-1860 blue-and-white flag named in the caption is not drawn.)

era-1517.note: Red field with a white crescent and star, as in the Commons Ottoman flag. The reference crescent sits left of centre and the star is placed in its mouth; ours is centred with a larger star. The evidence row says the red crescent flag is established only from 1793, so this fits the later part of the era only.

era-1805.note: Redrawn: Red field with a large white crescent and three five-pointed stars in its opening, as on the Commons Muhammad Ali flag. Earlier drawing differed from the reference.

era-1922.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Green field with white stars, but there is no crescent: the reference has a white crescent with the stars beside it in its mouth, and ours shows three stars in a triangle on their own. Fix: add the crescent and set the three stars in its opening. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1953.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The red-white-black tricolour is right, but the emblem is two plain black discs in the white stripe. The era's flags carried the Eagle of Saladin (1952-58, Flag_of_Egypt_(1952–1958).svg), two green five-pointed stars (UAR 1958-71) or a gold hawk (1972-84); none is two black dots. Fix: the UAR version with two green stars, the longest-lived of the three; the 1952-58 and 1972-84 flags carry gold emblems too complex to draw. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1984.note: Red, white, black horizontal tricolour as in the reference. The gold Eagle of Saladin is reduced to a gold arc over a short stem, which does not read as an eagle (no wings, head, or shield).

era-1525.note: White field with a red diagonal saltire as the Cross of Burgundy reference, drawn with straight bars where the reference has knotted ragged branches. The evidence row finds no source linking it to the Captaincy General of Guatemala.

era-1821.note: Green, white, red vertical tricolour with a badge in the middle of the white stripe, as in the reference; the crowned eagle on a cactus is reduced to a plain brown disc. (The evidence row doubts the imperial flag flew in San Salvador; the picture itself is the Mexican Empire flag.)

era-1823.note: Blue-white-blue triband with an emblem in the centre of the white stripe, as in the federation reference. The drawing reduces the arms (triangle of volcanoes, rainbow, cap) to an oval with triangles, and uses a dark cobalt where the reference is a light sky blue (about 137,197,227).

era-1841.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The drawing is a plain blue-white-blue triband. That matches 1822-1865 only (Flag_of_El_Salvador_(1822–1865).svg, in a light sky blue rather than the cobalt drawn). From 1865 to 1912, most of this era, the flag was nine alternating blue and white stripes with a red canton of white stars (the 1875-1912 reference shows 14 stars; the evidence row says the plain-flag claim is contradicted). fixSvg draws the 1875-1912 flag. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1912.note: Blue-white-blue horizontal triband in the same cobalt blue as the reference, with the arms centred on the white stripe. The arms are reduced to an oval with five triangles and a red arc (no ribbon, flags, cap or wreath).

era-1471.note: Redrawn: White flag with the crowned Portuguese royal shield, as the Commons Portuguese flag of the period. Earlier drawing differed from the reference.

era-1778.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Red-yellow-red is right, but the Spanish bands are 1:2:1 (yellow twice the width of each red band, with a small arms on the yellow near the hoist); ours uses three equal bands. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1968.note: The drawing is the Wikimedia Commons file 'Flag of Equatorial Guinea.svg' (Public domain), with scripts, text and external links removed so it embeds in the page; its shapes and colours are the file's own.
era-1968.artist: See File history below for details.

era-1890.note: Caption says schematic. The Italian colonial flag was the Italian tricolour with the crowned Savoy shield (reference); the drawing is a vertical green-white-red tricolour with a brown disc in place of the shield, an invented badge.

era-1941.note: Union Flag, as the reference. The "B.M.A." marking in the caption is not drawn, and the evidence finds no source for it.

era-1952.note: The drawing is the Wikimedia Commons file 'Flag of Eritrea (1952-1961).svg' (Public domain), with scripts, text and external links removed so it embeds in the page; its shapes and colours are the file's own.

era-1993.note: Red hoist triangle over green (top) and blue (bottom) triangles matches the layout. The gold olive wreath (with, on the 1995 version, a branch) is replaced by a plain gold rectangle.

era-1227.note: Black cross on white matches, but the atlas cross is centred on the field while the Commons flag of the Teutonic Order state has the cross offset toward the hoist (Nordic cross). The Livonian Order own flag is not documented; the Commons Livonian Order file did not render a usable flag.

era-1561.note: Blue field with a yellow Nordic cross offset toward the hoist, as in the Swedish flag file.

era-1721.note: White, blue, red horizontal tricolour in the same order as the Russian tricolour. Commons also shows a black-yellow-white imperial flag for 1858-1896, so the tricolour is the civil flag, as the caption says.

era-1918.note: Blue, black, white horizontal tricolour, same order and hues.

era-1940.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Red field with a gold star, sickle and hammer top left matches the 1953-1990 flag. The blue band with its white wavy line sits at the very bottom edge in the atlas (white line at 88% of the height, blue 93-100%); in the Commons file the white wave is at 50% of the height, the blue band spans about 56-84%, and red shows below it. The waves are straight here. The 1940-1953 flag (Commons) is plain red with the emblem and no bands, so the drawing fits neither version exactly. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1991.note: Blue, black, white horizontal tricolour, same order and hues.

era-1903.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Ours is a Blue Ensign with a Union Flag canton and a blank white badge disc, captioned as the protectorate's own badge. The evidence row says two publishers agree that Swaziland had no distinctive flag and flew the Union Jack until independence (the High Commissioner's flag was a Union Flag with a lettered roundel). So the reference for the period is the plain Union Flag; the Commons Swaziland flags are 1890-1902 (Flag_of_Swaziland_(1894–1902).svg, a blue field with a black-and-white device). The Union Flag in ours also has a centred rather than counterchanged red saltire. fixSvg draws the plain Union Flag. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1968.note: The drawing is the Wikimedia Commons file 'Flag of Eswatini.svg' (Public domain), with scripts, text and external links removed so it embeds in the page; its shapes and colours are the file's own.

era-100.note: Ours shows four gold bars of different heights on brown, standing for the stelae of Aksum; the caption says no national flag is shown and the evidence row says no source mentions an Aksumite flag. It is an emblematic placeholder, not a flag or banner.

era-1270.note: Green-yellow-red tricolour (green on top) with a central emblem, as in the Commons Empire flag with the Lion of Judah. Ours reduces the lion to a small outlined box and an arc on the yellow band, which is hardly visible and not recognisable as a lion bearing a cross staff. Period: the reference is dated 1897-1974 (the earliest form, 1897-1914, was red-yellow-green with no lion, Flag_of_Ethiopia_(1897–1914).svg), so for 1270-1897 only pennants are recorded and the tricolour is later than most of the era.

era-1974.note: The green-yellow-red tricolour is right, but the emblem matches none of the Commons Derg-era flags: 1974-75 has the Lion of Judah without its crown, the 1975-87 flag is blank (or carries a blue-and-green emblem), and the 1987-91 PDRE flag carries a blue-and-green emblem. Ours has a red star with a gold edge over a navy spearhead shape, which the evidence row says no source describes. No fixSvg because three different emblems apply to different years inside the era. The caption now says which period the drawing fits.

era-1991.note: Green-yellow-red horizontal tricolour with a blue disc and a gold star at the centre, as in the reference. The reference disc is large (diameter two thirds of the flag height) with a gold pentagram whose points are joined by thin gold rays; ours has a disc less than half that size (about 30% of the height) and a plain five-pointed star. Wikipedia says the 1991-96 flag had no emblem, which the page's 1991-present span does not show.

era-1871.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The atlas draws a dark blue field with a Union Flag canton and a white bird shape. The Commons flag of the Kingdom of Fiji is a vertical bicolour, white at the hoist and light blue at the fly, with a red crowned shield bearing a white dove across the middle. There is no Union Flag. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1874.note: Dark blue field with the Union Flag in the canton and a white disc badge in the fly matches the 1877-1924 colonial pattern. The disc shows a generic landscape, not the actual badge (a shield with a mermaid, then a crowned lion, then the colony arms; the disc was dropped in 1924), and the first three years (1874-1877) had only a plain Union Flag.

era-1970.note: Light blue field, Union Flag in the canton, shield on the fly side: layout and colours match. The shield's lion, cocoa pod, sugar cane, palm and dove are reduced to coloured quarters.

era-1150.note: Blue field with a gold Nordic cross offset toward the hoist matches the Swedish flag, including its 16th-century Commons form (which has a swallow-tail fly the card does not draw). The design is documented only from the 1500s while the era starts c. 1150, and no source says Finland flew it (evidence row).

era-1917.note: Blue Nordic cross on white, with the vertical arm off-centre toward the hoist and the cross about one sixth of the height, matches the reference.

era-1809.note: The caption already calls this a reconstruction, and the evidence row says no source describes a dark-field arms flag (Wikipedia has an 1848 flag of the arms in laurel on white). The card also inverts the arms: the Commons Grand Duchy arms are a crowned golden lion on a red shield, while ours is a golden lion on a cream shield set on a dark red field. The emblem was redrawn by hand on 2026-10-25.

era-1589.note: Plain white field, which matches the plain white ensign FOTW describes; the lily-strewn white pavilion royal (Pavillon_royal_de_France.svg) and the blue royal standard are not drawn.

era-1789.note: Draws the blue-white-red order fixed by the 1794 decree (the caption says so); the 1790-1794 file shows the same colours. The 1789-1790 cockade-era and red-white-blue 1790 order is not drawn.

era-1804.note: Vertical blue-white-red tricolour with equal stripes: matches the reference (1794-1815 range); imperial emblems not drawn.

era-1814.note: Plain white field, matching the reference; the Hundred Days tricolour interval and royal arms are not drawn.

era-1830.note: Vertical blue-white-red tricolour: matches the reference file, which is dated 1830-1974 among others.

era-1848.note: Vertical blue-white-red tricolour, blue at hoist: matches the 1848 reference drawing.

era-1852.note: Vertical blue-white-red tricolour: matches the reference; imperial bee not drawn, which FOTW treats as an emblem, not part of the flag.

era-1870.note: Vertical blue-white-red tricolour: matches the reference.

era-1940.note: Plain blue-white-red tricolour, which matches the Vichy national flag; the Free France flag in the reference carries a red Cross of Lorraine on the white stripe and the Vichy head-of-state standard (francisque, seven stars) is not drawn. The caption mentions the cross but the drawing omits it.

era-1944.note: Vertical blue-white-red tricolour, blue at hoist, equal stripes: matches the reference.

era-1958.note: Same blue-white-red vertical tricolour as the reference (blue at hoist); the post-1974 lighter/darker blue shade is not distinguished.

era-987.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Blue field with three gold fleurs-de-lis, but arranged one above, two below; the reference (and the arms after Charles V) put two above and one below. The red oriflamme of the Capetian centuries is not drawn (caption already says the post-Charles V arms). It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1839.note: Vertical blue - white - red tricolour with blue at the hoist, same as the French flag.

era-1959.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: In the reference the yellow band is narrow (about 17 percent of the height) with green and blue bands of about 42 percent each, and the French tricolour canton covers the top half of the hoist (half the length, the full green band). Ours has three equal bands and a much smaller canton (a fifth of the area), so the proportions differ visibly. Colours and the canton order (blue, white, red) match. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1960.note: Green - yellow - blue horizontal tricolour in equal bands, same as the reference.

era-1816.note: Plain British Blue Ensign (Union Flag canton on blue) matches the generic ensign, drawn with an uncounterchanged saltire. No source documents a flag specific to Bathurst in 1816-88; the caption says undifferentiated.

era-1888.note: Blue Ensign with a Union Flag canton and a badge in the fly is right, but the badge is not: the Commons flag shows an elephant in front of a palm tree on a mound (orange, green and yellow) set at mid-height of the fly, while ours is a cream disc with a red rim, a green tree and a blue bar placed low in the fly. The caption admits it is a reconstruction and the sources describe an elephant. It is a labelled reconstruction.

era-1965.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Colours and order match, but the stripe proportions do not: the reference bands are 6:1:4:1:6 (red 33%, white 5.5%, blue 22%, white 5.5%, green 33% of the height) while ours are 28%:4%:36%:4%:28%, so the blue is far too broad. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1970.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Colours and order match, but the stripe proportions do not: the reference bands are 6:1:4:1:6 (red 33%, white 5.5%, blue 22%, white 5.5%, green 33% of the height) while ours are 28%:4%:36%:4%:28%, so the blue is far too broad. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1866.note: Black / white / red horizontal bands match the reference for the North German Confederation (sources date it from 1867; the card starts 1866).

era-1871.note: Black / white / red horizontal bands match the reference.

era-1918.note: Black / red / gold horizontal bands match the reference (the Weimar flag is the same tricolour).

era-1933.note: Redrawn after the Commons Flag of Germany (1935–1945): red field, white disc, black swastika turned on its point.

era-1990.note: Black / red / gold horizontal tricolour in equal bands matches the reference.

era-962.note: Emblem redrawn by hand on 2026-10-25 and compared by eye with the reference: same layout and colours, emblem simplified (shape and detail reduced).

era-1670.note: Caption says it is a stylised motif. No historical Asante national flag is documented; Commons' Flag_of_Ashanti.svg is a different, later design (yellow, white, black with a gold emblem, white, green horizontal bands). The maroon field with a gold frame and disc is an invented stand-in.

era-1821.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The colony's flag was a Blue Ensign (Union Jack only in the upper-hoist canton, blue fly) carrying a landscape badge in the fly, 1877-1957. The drawing spreads the Union Jack across the whole flag with a plain cream disc in the centre. Nothing is documented for 1821-1877, and the fix badge is a simplified landscape disc. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1957.note: Red-gold-green with a black star, identical to the current flag, as the reference.

era-1964.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The 1964-66 flag has a WHITE middle stripe (CPP colours) with the black star; the drawing has a gold middle stripe and adds a black arc under the star that the reference does not have. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1966.note: Red-gold-green horizontal tricolour with a black five-pointed star in the gold band, as the reference (star a little smaller).

era-1261.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The drawing is a black double-headed eagle on gold. The 14th-century Byzantine imperial flag reference (Commons, portolan-based) is a red field with a yellow cross and four fire-steel (B-shaped) emblems, no eagle. The eagle-on-yellow flag is not shown by the reference. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1460.note: Redrawn: Ottoman red banner with a single dark crescent (no star), as on the Commons c.1490-1701 flag. Earlier drawing differed from the reference.

era-1821.note: Plain white cross filling the full flag on a blue field with arms of equal width and the cross centred, as the reference (the reference file is the plain cross flag, dated 1822-1978). Reference blue is darker.

era-1832.note: Nine-stripe flag with cross canton, as in the reference; the 1833-1858 ensign is a light/sky blue and carries the royal arms at the cross centre, and the 1863-1924 version a crown; the drawing has neither and uses a mid blue.

era-1913.note: Nine-stripe flag with cross canton as the reference naval ensign (1863-1924); the reference has a small royal crown at the centre of the cross that the drawing omits.

era-1924.note: Nine-stripe flag with plain white cross canton, no crown: matches the reference and the period when crowns were removed (1924-1935).

era-1935.note: Nine-stripe flag with the cross canton as in the reference (dated 1935-1970); the reference adds a small royal crown at the centre of the cross that the drawing omits.

era-1941.note: Same nine-stripe design as the reference naval ensign without the small royal crown at the cross centre. Nothing here shows an occupation-period or exile-government variant; the drawing is the ordinary pre-war national/sea flag.

era-1944.note: Nine-stripe sea/civil flag with the white-cross canton, as the reference, but the reference (state/naval version) carries a small yellow royal crown at the centre of the cross, which the drawing leaves out. The plain version without crown was also used as the national flag (FOTW per the evidence row).

era-1967.note: Nine-stripe flag with the cross canton, as the junta-era reference (7:12 sole national flag from 1970). The reference blue is a darker navy than the drawing, a shade difference only. The plain-cross land flag also existed until 1969/70.

era-1974.note: Nine blue and white stripes with a white cross on a blue canton five stripes tall, blue stripe first and last: same layout as the reference. Blue is lighter than the dark blue now common.

era-1650.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The atlas draws a white field with a jumble of text glyphs (a club, a heart) and a path that do not form a recognisable fleur-de-lis. The Commons royal French flag is white with several gold fleurs-de-lis. No source names a flag for French Grenada, so the fleur-de-lis itself is also unsupported; the fix only repairs the drawing. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1763.note: Red field with the Union Flag in the canton is the Red Ensign pattern of the period; the atlas canton uses the modern flag with the red St Patrick saltire (1801 and later), whereas the 1707-1801 flag has none. No source documents a Red Ensign over Grenada in 1763-1783.

era-1783.note: Blue Ensign with the Union Flag in the canton and a round badge in the fly matches the colonial pattern. The badge is a generic pale disc with green hills and a sea band; the Commons badges are a sugar mill (1875-1903) and a ship (1903-1967), and the caption calls it a harbour. Nothing documents a Grenada flag before 1875.

era-1974.note: Red border with six gold stars (three top, three bottom), yellow triangles top and bottom, green triangles hoist and fly, a red disc with a gold star at the centre and the nutmeg at the hoist; layout and colours match. The atlas border is thinner than the file's.

era-1524.note: White field with a red saltire, as in the Cross of Burgundy file. The reference saltire is a ragged (knotted) cross and ours is two straight bars.

era-1821.note: Vertical green-white-red, the Empire's national flag as Wikipedia's Flag of Mexico describes it (decreed November 1821, in use from July 1822); the crowned eagle in the centre is replaced by a plain gold disc. Note that the Commons file First_flag_of_the_Mexican_Empire.svg is a different flag, the diagonal white-green-red Regency/Three Guarantees banner with stars.

era-1823.note: Horizontal blue-white-blue as in the 1825-1838 file, with the arms in the white stripe reduced to a brown mound of three triangles (volcanoes) with no cap, rainbow or inscription.

era-1841.note: Horizontal blue-white-blue. Both the 1838-1843 and 1843-1851 files have a small coat of arms in the white stripe, which ours omits; the stripe layout matches.

era-1851.note: Horizontal blue-white-blue with the hoist half of the top stripe red and of the bottom stripe yellow, as in the 1851-1858 file. The arms in the white middle stripe are omitted. The 1858-1871 file is a different layout (Flag_of_Guatemala_(1858–1871).svg) and is not drawn, though the era runs to 1871.

era-1871.note: Vertical blue-white-blue as in the 1871-1968 file. The arms in the white band are reduced to a bare gold ring.

era-1968.note: Vertical blue-white-blue with the arms in the white band, as in the reference. The arms (quetzal on a scroll, crossed rifles and swords, laurel wreath) are reduced to a gold ring with three dark bars; the colours of the bands match.

era-1867.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The 1830-1910 Portuguese flag is a blue and white bicolour split into equal halves (blue at the hoist) with the royal arms on the dividing line. Ours has a blue band only one third wide on a cream field, with a plain gold disc on the line, so the proportions are wrong and the arms are only a disc. The evidence row also says no source shows this flag over Portuguese Guinea. The replacement draws equal halves with a simplified crowned shield. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1911.note: Green hoist (about 40 percent) and red field match the republican flag. The armillary sphere with the shield is reduced to a cream disc with a gold ring and a red centre.

era-1963.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The PAIGC flag has a red hoist band with a black star (and the initials PAIGC underneath), then yellow over green. Ours has a black hoist band with a red star: the two colours are swapped. The evidence row already says the black-band version is contradicted by both sources. The replacement swaps them back and leaves out the initials. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1973.note: Red hoist band with a black five-pointed star, then yellow over green, matches the reference. The hoist band is a little wider than the reference (40 percent of the length vs about 34 percent).

era-1727.note: Redrawn: White pennant with a green inscription, as the Commons flag of the Imamate of Futa Jallon (the inscription here is a stand-in for the original calligraphy). Earlier drawing differed from the reference.

era-1958.note: Vertical red, yellow, green bands, red at the hoist: matches the reference.

era-1616.note: The drawing is the Wikimedia Commons file 'Flag of the Dutch West India Company.svg' (Public domain), with scripts, text and external links removed so it embeds in the page; its shapes and colours are the file's own.

era-1814.note: Blue Ensign with a Union Flag canton and a circular badge in the fly matches the colonial ensign (from 1875). era-1966.note: Green field, white-edged yellow arrowhead, black-edged red arrowhead in the hoist half: same design and colour order as the reference. The yellow arrow reaches only about three quarters of the width where the reference reaches nearly the fly edge.

era-1492.note: White field with a red diagonal saltire matches the Cross of Burgundy; the ragged-staff stubs are left out and the arms are plain bars.

era-1697.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The atlas draws a white field with one gold glyph that is a star-and-crescent (Unicode 9770), not a fleur-de-lis. The Commons royal French flag is white with several gold fleurs-de-lis. No source ties it to Saint-Domingue specifically, but the star-and-crescent is wrong either way. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1803.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The atlas draws horizontal bands, blue over red. The Commons flag for 1803-1804 (and the 1806-1811 file) divides the field vertically, blue at the hoist and red at the fly, and carries white motto lettering. Horizontal bands only came with the 1820 flag. The fix omits the motto. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1820.note: Blue over red horizontal bicolour with a centre white panel bearing arms, as in the reference; the arms are a white oval with a green leaf placeholder.

era-1986.note: Blue over red horizontal bicolour matches. The centre white rectangle bearing the coat of arms (palm, cannons, flags, cap on a pole) is drawn as a white oval with a green leaf and a dot, a placeholder as the caption says.

era-1795.note: The card shows the eight-stripe flag adopted in 1845 and calls it the flag adopted under Kamehameha I. Per the evidence row, Wikipedia says a distinct Hawaiian flag first reached a foreign port in 1817, early versions (1816-1845) varied (nine stripes with a 1:2 canton; seven stripes seen in 1818) and the British Red Ensign was the unofficial flag c. 1793-1816. So for 1795-1845 the drawing is a later design. No replacement is given because the early versions are undocumented in the files found. The caption now says which period the drawing fits.

era-1893.note: Eight stripes in the order white, red, blue, white, red, blue, white, red from the top, with a Union Jack canton, match the reference. The canton is a simplified Union Jack without the offset diagonals and covers about 43 percent of the width and half the height, a little smaller than the reference canton (about half the width). The evidence row says no flag specific to the Provisional Government is described and the US flag flew for part of 1893, so this design is used for a period the sources do not confirm.

era-1894.note: Eight stripes in the order white, red, blue, white, red, blue, white, red from the top, with a Union Jack canton, match the reference. The canton is a simplified Union Jack without the offset diagonals and covers about 43 percent of the width and half the height, a little smaller than the reference canton (about half the width). The Republic reissued the flag with a 1896 diagram (FOTW), which the card does not distinguish.

era-1898.note: Eight stripes in the order white, red, blue, white, red, blue, white, red from the top, with a Union Jack canton, match the reference. The canton is a simplified Union Jack without the offset diagonals and covers about 43 percent of the width and half the height, a little smaller than the reference canton (about half the width). Same drawing as every other Hawaii era; the sources say the territory kept the kingdom flag.

era-1959.note: Eight stripes in the order white, red, blue, white, red, blue, white, red from the top, with a Union Jack canton, match the reference. The canton is a simplified Union Jack without the offset diagonals and covers about 43 percent of the width and half the height, a little smaller than the reference canton (about half the width).

era-1524.note: Red saltire on white matches the Cross of Burgundy. The reference saltire is made of ragged (knotted) staves; ours has straight bars.

era-1821.note: Green - white - red vertical stripes match the First Mexican Empire flag. The crowned eagle on the nopal in the white stripe is reduced to a plain gold disc.

era-1823.note: Light blue - white - light blue matches. The arms on the white stripe (a triangle with volcanoes, rainbow, cap of liberty) are reduced to three plain gold triangles, with no rainbow, sun or cap.

era-1838.note: Plain blue - white - blue in equal stripes; matches the Commons flag for the period (the file starts at 1839).

era-1866.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Blue - white - blue with five blue stars matches in outline, but the stars are drawn as round dots in a zigzag. The Commons 1866-1949 flag has five-pointed stars in an X (four at the corners of a smaller square, one in the centre). It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1949.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Blue - white - blue with five blue stars on the white stripe is right, but the five marks are round dots, not five-pointed stars, and they sit in a W-like zigzag (two high at the sides, one high in the middle, two low inner ones). The reference has the stars in an X: four at the corners of a square and one in the centre, spread widely. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1000.note: Alternating red and silver (white) stripes, red uppermost, as in the Commons reconstruction; the reference is drawn as a pennon, the atlas as a rectangle (style). It is a reconstruction of the Arpad stripes, not a surviving flag.

era-1526.note: Looked for a flag of John Zapolya or Ferdinand I on the Commons file lists for the Zapolya and Ferdinand articles: only coats of arms turned up. The Louis II flag file (an arms banner) is of the previous reign. The Arpad stripes appear on Zapolya seals but no source shows a flag; the dashed border is an invented marker of disputed rule.

era-1541.note: Redrawn: Ottoman red banner with a single dark crescent (no star), as on the Commons c.1490-1701 flag. Earlier drawing differed from the reference.

era-1918.note: Tricolour matches. The Commons drawing carries a small crownless shield at the centre which the atlas leaves out (caption says plain); Wikipedia says unarmed tricolours were also used, so the plain version is a defensible reading.

era-1919.note: Plain red field, as in the reference.

era-1944.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The atlas drawing is a green field with a white star. The reference for the Horthy-era tricolour, which Wikipedia says carried the arms up to 1944-45, is the red-white-green tricolour with the crowned arms at the centre; the Arrow Cross party flag is not the state flag in the sources. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1946.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The Commons drawing for 1946-1949 is the tricolour with a small crownless Kossuth shield (red-white stripes on one side, a double cross on a green mound on the other) at the centre; the atlas drawing is a plain tricolour with no emblem. Wikipedia text agrees with the Commons file. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1949.note: Tricolour matches. The Rakosi arms (wheat-ear wreath round a shield with hammer and star above) are reduced here to one red star with a gold outline. The reference arms apply to 1949-1956 only; the plain tricolour was official from 1957 (see evidence row).

era-1989.note: Red, white, green horizontal tricolour, same order and hues as the civil flag.

era-1920.note: Emblem redrawn by hand on 2026-10-25 and compared by eye with the reference: same layout and colours, emblem simplified (shape and detail reduced).

era-1867.note: Emblem redrawn by hand on 2026-10-25 and compared by eye with the reference: same layout and colours, emblem simplified (shape and detail reduced).

era-1699.note: Emblem redrawn by hand on 2026-10-25 and compared by eye with the reference: same layout and colours, emblem simplified (shape and detail reduced).

era-1397.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The Kalmar Union flag on Commons is a yellow field with a red cross offset to the hoist; the drawing has the right yellow and red cross but adds three white discs for crowns that the flag does not carry (the 1427 captured flag in Wikipedia shows arms, not crowns). Fix: plain yellow field with red cross. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1523.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Same drawing as the 1814 card: red-white-red horizontal stripes with a white vertical bar, not the Dannebrog (red field, white Nordic cross). Fix: red field with a white offset cross. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1814.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The Dannebrog is a red field with a white Nordic cross. The drawing is three horizontal stripes (red, white, red) crossed by a white vertical bar, so it reads as a white band, not a cross on red. Fix: red field with a white offset cross.
