era-1918.note: Same design as the 1918-1944 flag: blue field, white-edged red cross.

era-1944.note: Blue field, white-edged red Nordic cross offset to the hoist, same as the reference. The blue is a brighter shade than the post-1944 dark blue, same hue.

era-1262.note: Emblem redrawn by hand on 2026-10-25 and compared by eye with the reference: same layout and colours, emblem simplified (shape and detail reduced).

era-1206.note: The caption already calls this a reconstruction. The only Commons reference (the Catalan Atlas flag attributed to the Tughlaqs, itself a doubtful attribution per Wikipedia) is a grey field with a black vertical strip; ours is dark red with a gold triangle and ring, which matches no reference.

era-1526.note: Redrawn: Moss-green triangular alam (pennant) with a gold sun, as the Commons Mughal standard. Earlier drawing differed from the reference.

era-1707.note: Redrawn: Moss-green triangular alam (pennant) with a gold sun, as the Commons Mughal standard. Earlier drawing differed from the reference.

era-1757.note: Thirteen red and white stripes with a Union canton, red stripe on top, matches the reference. The canton is the post-1801 Union Jack with St Patrick saltire, drawn without offset diagonals and covering fewer stripes than the reference; the 1707 reference (no St Patrick saltire) would be the design for most of 1757-1800.

era-1858.note: Union Jack canton on a field with the Star of India badge in the fly matches the reference design; the card uses the blue field (the Royal Indian Marine form; the Red Ensign reference is the civil form). The badge is reduced to a plain star with a gold outline, where the reference has the Star of India emblem on a disc. The Union Jack drawing is also simplified (no offset diagonals).

era-1906.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The Commons drawing of the 1906 Calcutta flag has an orange-red top band with eight white lotuses, a yellow middle band with Vande Mataram, and a green bottom band with a sun and a crescent and star. Ours is the reverse: green top with the lotuses, yellow middle, red bottom with the sun and crescent. This agrees with the FOTW order (red, yellow, green top to bottom) in the evidence row and contradicts the Wikipedia prose order (green, yellow, red); the replacement follows the Commons drawing. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1917.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Reference: nine horizontal stripes, red at top and bottom (five red, four green), a Union Jack canton at the hoist, seven stars (Saptarishi) running diagonally down the field and a crescent with a star near the top of the fly, with a swallow-tail notch in the fly edge. Ours has the stripes reversed (five green, four red, green on top), a canton without the red diagonals, the stars in a clump, the crescent at the bottom left and no fly notch. The replacement fixes the stripe order and canton but omits the fly notch. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1921.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The Commons reference for the 1921 Gandhi flag has white on top, green in the middle and red at the bottom, with a navy spinning wheel on the hoist side (circle with three spokes and a frame). Ours is red / white / green from the top, with a small ring at the centre; band order and the wheel position differ. The evidence row notes that sources disagree on band order, so the replacement follows the Commons reference only. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1931.note: The drawing is the Wikimedia Commons file '1931 Flag of India.svg' (Public domain), with scripts, text and external links removed so it embeds in the page; its shapes and colours are the file's own.

era-1947.note: Saffron / white / green bands and a navy wheel match the reference. The wheel is simplified: 16 spokes drawn where the real Ashoka Chakra has 24, and it is smaller than the specified size. Checked by colour-grid comparison with the rendered reference.

era-320.note: No Gupta flag is documented. The caption says reconstructed. Gold wheel (12 spokes) on maroon; the Wikipedia Gupta article describes Garuda on coins and seals, not a wheel, so the emblem is an invention.

era-322bce.note: No Maurya flag survives. The caption says the wheel is reconstructed from the Sarnath pillar; the Ashoka Chakra (24 spokes) is documented on the Lion Capital, here drawn as a 12-spoke white wheel on maroon, so it is a stand-in.

era-1501.note: Green field as in the reference, but the Commons Safavid flag has a gold lion-and-sun emblem in the centre that the drawing omits (the caption says plain green; Wikipedia gives no design for the infobox flag).

era-1736.note: Caption says informed approximation. The Commons Afsharid and Zand flags are triangular pennants (white with green border and gold lion and sun; red, white and blue stripes; red and gold) and none is a maroon rectangle with a gold sun and four ticks; the drawing is not based on any of them.

era-1979.note: Green-white-red horizontal triband with an emblem centred on the white stripe, as in the reference. The reference emblem is the red stylised Allah design (four crescents and a sword) and the white Takbir script runs along the inner edges of the green and red bands; the drawing reduces the emblem to a plain red disc and the script to rows of small green ticks inside the white stripe (the caption says so).

era-224.note: Caption says informed reconstruction. The Commons Derafsh Kaviani is a purple field with a red border carrying a gold star pattern and tassels; the drawing has a maroon field with a thin gold and blue frame and corner dots but no star pattern, so it is a looser reconstruction than the Commons one.

era-651.note: Plain black field, same as the Abbasid black banner reference. The era runs from 651 and the Abbasids only from 750, so the first century (Rashidun and Umayyad) is not covered by this banner.

era-1925.note: Emblem redrawn by hand on 2026-10-25 and compared by eye with the reference: same layout and colours, emblem simplified (shape and detail reduced).

era-1789.note: Emblem redrawn by hand on 2026-10-25 and compared by eye with the reference: same layout and colours, emblem simplified (shape and detail reduced).

era-1534.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Red field with a white crescent matches, but the star in our drawing is a malformed fragment (a half star pointing right, standing clear of the horns); the reference has a full five-pointed star between the horns. The 1844 design is drawn for the whole 1534-1920 span; earlier Ottoman flags are not. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1920.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The 1921-24 reference is black-white-green with a plain red triangle reaching to the middle of the flag and no star; ours has a shorter triangle and a white star. The 1924-32 flag of this card span is the starred trapezoid (Flag_of_Iraq_(1924–1959).svg), not drawn. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1932.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Black-white-green stripes match, but the red hoist shape is a trapezoid (vertical edge halfway across the white stripe) carrying two white seven-pointed stars in the reference; ours is a pointed triangle running to the middle of the flag with one tiny star. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1958.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Wrong layout and emblem: the reference is three vertical stripes, black, white, green, with a red eight-pointed star holding a white ring and yellow disc in the centre. Ours is red-white-black horizontal stripes with a yellow disc and dagger. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1963.note: Red-white-black stripes with three green stars on the white stripe: matches; the reference spaces the stars more widely (about 23%, 50%, 76% of the width) than ours (35%, 50%, 65%).

era-1991.note: The drawing is the Wikimedia Commons file 'Flag of Iraq (1991–2004).svg' (Public domain), with scripts, text and external links removed so it embeds in the page; its shapes and colours are the file's own.
era-1991.artist: See File history below for details.

era-2008.note: Red-white-black horizontal stripes with a green takbir centred on the white stripe, no stars: matches. The Kufic Arabic inscription is replaced by Latin letters 'ALLAHU AKBAR' in a monospace face.

era-637.note: Plain white field. No reference drawing: the Wikipedia pages for the Umayyad and Rashidun Caliphates carry no flag image (only coins and maps), and Commons has none among the files they use.

era-762.note: Plain black field: matches the Commons Abbasid banner.

era-1171.note: Blue with three gold crowns, two over one, as in the Lordship arms file. The arms are drawn as a full blue field rather than a shield, and the crowns are small bowl-and-block shapes. This is arms, not a flag, as the evidence row says.

era-1541.note: Green field with a gold harp, as in the harp-flag file. The harp is built from a few strokes (curved neck, straight pillar, soundbox, four strings) and has no sculpted pillar or winged figure. The evidence row finds no source for this being a flag of the Kingdom itself.

era-1801.note: Union flag layout (blue field, white and red crosses, red diagonals) as in the reference. The red diagonals of St Patrick's cross are drawn centred in the white diagonals; the reference has them offset (counterchanged), and the central cross proportions are a little thin.

era-1919.note: Three equal vertical stripes, green, white, orange from the hoist, as in Flag_of_Ireland.svg. (The evidence row notes the GPO flags of 1916 predate this era; that is a dating point, not a drawing one.)

era-1922.note: Three equal vertical stripes, green, white, orange from the hoist, as in Flag_of_Ireland.svg.

era-1949.note: Three equal vertical stripes, green, white, orange from the hoist, as in Flag_of_Ireland.svg.

era-1099.note: White field with a gold large cross and four small crosses, as in the Jerusalem cross reference. The reference crosses have the T-shaped potent ends and the four small crosses are crosses; the drawing uses a plain square-ended cross and four plain squares as crosslets.

era-1291.note: Gold field with a dark central emblem, as in the Commons Mamluk flags (bright yellow field, dark eagle emblem on the Alexandria flag; others have a white pole-line or plain yellow). The drawing's field is an ochre brown rather than yellow and the eagle is a featureless dark blob. Several Commons Mamluk flags differ from each other, so the exact design for 1291-1517 is not settled.

era-1517.note: Red field with a white crescent and five-pointed star, as the Ottoman Empire 1844-1922 flag that Wikipedia's infobox shows. Before 1793/1844 the Ottoman flags differed (a crescent alone, per Ottoman_flag_c.1490-1701.png), so the star is anachronistic for most of 1517-1844.

era-1917.note: Union Flag in navy, white and red, with a white-edged red cross and diagonals. The diagonals are drawn symmetrically: the reference has the red saltire of St Patrick counterchanged (offset), which the drawing does not show.

era-1948.note: White field, two blue horizontal stripes near the top and bottom edges and a blue hexagram outline at centre: same design as the reference. Proportions are 3:2 against the real 8:11, and the star is drawn a little smaller than the reference.

era-636.note: Plain white field as in the Commons Umayyad flag (and the Fatimid_flag.png, also plain white). The drawing adds a thin pale frame line. The caption's later green Fatimid flag is not what is drawn.

era-1416.note: Red field with a white cross reaching the edges, as the Savoy reference.

era-1720.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Reference for the Savoyard states in the 18th century is a RED field with a white cross (with a small crown). The drawing is a blue field with a white cross, a colour the evidence found no source for in 1720-1798. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1798.note: Vertical blue-white-red French tricolour, as the reference.

era-1814.note: The drawing is the Wikimedia Commons file 'Merchant Flag and War Ensign of the Savoyard States (1814-1816).svg' (Public domain), with scripts, text and external links removed so it embeds in the page; its shapes and colours are the file's own.

era-1848.note: Green-white-red tricolour with the Savoy shield on the white band matches; the reference shield has the blue border and a larger shield, and the drawing's small crown and border are simplified.

era-1861.note: Tricolour with the Savoy shield (red, white cross) and crown matches in layout; the shield's blue border is omitted and the crown is a plain gold bar and arch.

era-1922.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The reference for the Kingdom 1861-1946 is the tricolour with the crowned, blue-bordered Savoy shield only; there are no fasces beside the shield (Wikipedia: the 1926 fasces proposal was blocked). The drawing adds two fasces flanking the shield and omits the blue border. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1943.note: Plain green-white-red tricolour (state flag, Flag_of_Italy.svg) matches. The war ensign carried a large eagle holding fasces on the white band; the drawing has only a small dark mark standing for it.

era-1945.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The Commons flag for 1861-1946 (and its crowned variants) is the tricolour with the Savoy arms: red shield, white cross, blue border, crown above. The drawing shows the shield with no crown and no blue border; the crown removal is a claim the page's sources do not support (evidence: not in either source). Drawn here as the reference, with crown. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1946.note: Vertical green-white-red tricolour with no emblem, as the reference.

era-1509.note: Red saltire on white matches the Cross of Burgundy; the reference saltire is made of ragged staves, ours has straight bars.

era-1655.note: Union Flag layout matches with centred (not counterchanged) red diagonals. It is the post-1801 design with the Irish saltire; for 1655-1801 the Union Flag had no red diagonals (FOTW, per the Canada evidence row), so the earlier part of the span is drawn with a later flag.

era-1875.note: Blue Ensign with the Union Flag in the upper-hoist quarter and a badge in the fly matches the reference layout. The colonial badge is a simplified shield (green with a gold disc) where the Commons badge is a round device; the Union Flag has centred, not counterchanged, red diagonals. The badge changed in 1906 and 1957.

era-1962.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Gold saltire on green and black is right, but the black and green are in the wrong places. In the reference the saltire divides the flag into four triangles: black at the hoist and fly, green at top and bottom. Ours is green all over with only four small black corner triangles, so the left and right triangles are mostly green. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1185.note: Ours is a placard reading NO NATIONAL FLAG YET, a deliberate non-flag stand-in. Commons shows the Nishiki no Mihata as a historical military flag from the 13th century on, and Wikipedia records Minamoto (white with a red disc) and Taira (red with a gold disc) sun-disc banners in the Genpei War; none of these is a national flag, so the placard is consistent only in that sense.

era-1336.note: Ours is a green placard reading NO NATIONAL FLAG YET, a deliberate non-flag stand-in. Commons has an Ashikaga banner file for 1338-1568 (a tall narrow banner, undescribed there), and FOTW describes mon-based daimyo flags from 1467; Wikipedia says both armies raised the Hinomaru in 1575. So the claim that nothing was flown is stronger than the sources; the placard is not a drawing of a flag.

era-1603.note: Ours is a dark placard reading NO NATIONAL FLAG YET. The Commons file Ensign_of_Shogunate_Ships.svg quotes the 1854-1863 shogunate orders: the white flag with a red sun disc as the national ship mark from 1854 and a white-black-white horizontal flag (nakaguro) for shogunate warships; FOTW (per the evidence row) says the shogunate used the sun flag on ships in the early 1600s. So documented flags exist for this era; the placard denies them. fixSvg shows the sun-disc flag (the ship flag the sources attest). The caption now says which period the drawing fits.

era-1868.note: Red sun disc with radiating rays on white, as in the Commons Army war flag and the 1889-1945 naval ensign (naval one has the disc off-centre toward the hoist). The references have sixteen tapering wedge rays running to the edges; ours has eight thick lines (four axes and four diagonals) and a disc of equal size to the plain flag. Colours and concept match.

era-1945.note: The plain Hinomaru, identical to the reference; the dashed outline is the page's marker for restricted display, not part of any flag. The Commons Flag_of_Allied_Occupied_Japan.svg is the Allied occupation ensign (a different, red-and-blue flag) and is not what this card claims to show.

era-1947.note: White field with a centred red disc of diameter three fifths of the height, as in the reference.

era-794.note: Ours is a placard reading NO NATIONAL FLAG YET, not a flag. Wikipedia records a sun-motif court flag in 701 and a Heian imperial Nishiki flag with golden sun and silver moon; Commons has a Nishiki no Mihata drawing labelled 13th century onward, so no Heian-dated drawing was found and the placard cannot be checked against a picture.

era-1115.note: Gold Jerusalem-cross motif on white: the colours match the Kingdom of Jerusalem arms (gold cross potent with four crosslets on silver), but the cross is a plain Greek cross with four small squares instead of crosslets. The arms belong to the kingdom; no banner for the Lordship of Oultrejordain is documented.

era-1189.note: Dark field with a thin gold ring, a placeholder; no Ayyubid flag image on the Wikipedia Ayyubid dynasty article (coin only).

era-1260.note: Gold field with a black eagle silhouette. No reference: Wikipedia's Mamluk Sultanate article carries no Mamluk flag (its only flag image is Egypt's modern one) and Commons has none among the files it uses.

era-1517.note: Redrawn: Ottoman red banner with a single dark crescent (no star), as on the Commons c.1490-1701 flag. Earlier drawing differed from the reference.

era-1921.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Ours is a blue-and-white Union Flag; the Commons Emirate of Transjordan flag is black over white over green with a red hoist triangle (apex one third across) and a white star, and our own evidence says no source has the Union Flag flying over Transjordan. The reference covers 1928 onward; 1921-28 used the Hejaz flag. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1946.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Black-white-green stripes match, but the red triangle in the reference runs halfway across the flag (apex at 50% of the length, ours stops at 43%) and carries a small seven-pointed white star about 12 units across; ours is a five-pointed star roughly three times too large. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-636.note: Plain cream field standing in for an Umayyad banner; no reference image (the Wikipedia Umayyad Caliphate article has no flag, only coins and maps).

era-1465.note: Caption says no fixed flag is documented and the tamga motif is a reconstruction. The Commons alleged flag is white with a red tamga-type mark and a separate Commons Khanate flag is blue with small white symbols, so ours (a gold diamond outline on black) is an invented stand-in that matches neither; fine only because the caption says reconstructed.

era-1731.note: White - blue - red horizontal tricolour in equal thirds, same as the Russian flag. Whether that flag flew over the steppe is a text question, not an art one.

era-1920.note: Plain red field with gold marks in the upper hoist matches the Commons flag of the Kazakh ASSR (1920-36), which has two lines of gold lettering in the canton. Ours replaces the lettering with a small gold L-shaped mark and leaves out the gold border line.

era-1936.note: Red field with a light-blue stripe near the bottom and a gold emblem in the upper hoist matches the 1953-1991 flag. The hammer and sickle is a crude cross-and-ring mark and the gold star above it is missing. This is the 1953 design drawn for a span that starts in 1936; the 1937 and 1940 flags (Commons) differ.

era-1991.note: Sky blue field with a gold sun and steppe eagle under it and a gold ornament band on the hoist matches. Detail left out: the sun is a disc with eight sticks instead of 32 rays, the eagle is a small blob, and the hoist ornament is a plain gold bar with no national pattern.

era-1892.note: Blue Ensign with the Union Flag in the canton and a badge in the fly matches the colonial pattern. The Commons ensigns show the colony shield (frigatebird, sun and waves on a small shield, no white disc) in the fly; the atlas shows a generic white ring with a blue centre and a star, which the evidence row calls schematic.

era-1979.note: Emblem redrawn by hand on 2026-10-25 and compared by eye with the reference: same layout and colours, emblem simplified (shape and detail reduced).

era-1752.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The Commons 1746-1871 flag is red with a white serrated (saw-tooth) band along the hoist edge; ours is plain red. The evidence row records that Wikipedia has the ribbon while FOTW only supposes a plain red flag. Fix: add the serrated white band at the hoist. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1899.note: Red field with the name Kuwait in Arabic in white (system font, near the centre), roughly as the 1914-1921 and 1921-1940 files show it (red with small white Arabic text). It fits about 1914-1961 only; the evidence row finds no support for 1899-1914, and the 1921 and 1940 files add other text or marks.

era-1961.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The current flag is three horizontal stripes, green, white, red, with a black trapezoid at the hoist whose inner edge spans the white stripe. Ours has green and white stripes but a black bottom stripe, a red wedge in the bottom hoist and a black wedge in the top hoist: the red and black are in the wrong places and the trapezoid is not a trapezoid. Fix: green, white, red stripes and one black trapezoid. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1876.note: White-blue-red horizontal tricolour, the Russian civil flag, as the reference (the state flag 1858-83 was black-orange-white per the evidence; the text question is which flew over Turkestan).

era-1876-1.note: Dark field with a gold diamond outline: the caption itself says no single flag is documented and the motif is a reconstruction. No reference exists; the Kyrgyz and Central Asian khanate pages describe no pre-Russian flag.

era-1924.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The 1952-91 Kirghiz SSR flag is red with a broad blue-white-blue band across the middle (about a third of the height) and a hammer, sickle and star in the canton. The drawing has one thin light-blue stripe near the bottom and an L-shaped glyph. Earlier forms (1924-52) had no hammer-and-sickle-with-stripe design. Fix: red with the central blue-white-blue band and a simplified hammer, sickle and star. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1991.note: Red field with a yellow sun and a tunduk (crossed-lath yurt roof) at its centre, as the reference. The sun has no rays: it is a plain yellow disc (the flag has 40 wavy rays) around a red disc crossed by four straight yellow lines. The 2023 redraw is a further change.

era-1201.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The Teutonic Order flag is a black cross on white whose arms run to the edges of the flag (Nordic-style, offset to the hoist). Ours is a small floating Greek cross in the middle of a white field that touches no edge. The black-on-white idea matches; the layout does not. The Order-specific banner for the Livonian branch is a text question. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1561.note: Redrawn: White over red with the arms of Poland (white eagle) and Lithuania (Vytis), as the Commons flag of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth. Earlier drawing differed from the reference.

era-1561-1.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The Commons state flag of the Duchy of Courland and Semigallia is red over white in two equal bands (the civil ensign adds a red and white chequer). Ours is a dark red field with a gold stag-like emblem, which neither Commons file nor the evidence sources show. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1621.note: Yellow Nordic cross on blue, cross offset to the hoist with the same proportions as the Swedish flag. The drawing matches the Swedish flag; that it flew over Riga is a text question.

era-1721.note: White-blue-red horizontal tricolour in equal thirds, same as the Russian flag (civil ensign from 1705 per the evidence row); no separate Livonia Governorate flag was found, so only the Russian ensign can be compared.

era-1795.note: White-blue-red horizontal tricolour in equal thirds, same as the Russian flag. Note the governorate flag on Commons for Courland is different (File:Flag_of_the_Courland_Governorate.svg: green over blue over white), so the design is a faithful Russian civil ensign but not shown to be the provincial flag.

era-1918.note: Carmine red - white - carmine red in 2:1:2, the same as the 1921 law flag on Commons.

era-1940.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The 1940-1953 Latvian SSR flag is plain red with a gold hammer and sickle in the upper hoist and the gold letters LPSR above them; there is no star. Ours draws a gold star merged with the hammer and sickle and leaves out the LPSR lettering. (The 1953-1990 flag, which has an outlined star, is a different design.) It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1941.note: Redrawn after the Commons Flag of Germany (1935–1945): red field, white disc, black swastika turned on its point.

era-1944.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The 1940-1953 Latvian SSR flag is plain red with a gold hammer and sickle in the upper hoist and the gold letters LPSR above them; there is no star. Ours draws a gold star merged with the hammer and sickle and leaves out the LPSR lettering. (The 1953-1990 flag, which has an outlined star, is a different design.) It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1953.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Red field with gold hammer and sickle under an outlined gold star in the upper hoist matches, but the lower edge does not: the reference has a solid blue band across the bottom fifth with white wavy stripes; ours has a thin cream strip with a blue wave line and red below it, so the bottom of the flag is red instead of blue. The star and sickle are also fused into one blob in ours. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1990.note: Carmine red - white - carmine red in 2:1:2, the same as the reference.

era-1109.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The atlas draws a gold Jerusalem cross (four small crosslets) on white, the arms of the Kingdom of Jerusalem. The Commons banner for the County of Tripoli is a red field with a large gold cross reaching the edges (arms of Toulouse-Tripoli). Field colour and cross differ. The fix is a plain version of the cross. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1109-1.note: The drawing is a faint cedar on a dashed maroon placeholder field and the caption says no flag is documented. Wikipedia and the Commons lists for Lebanon, Phoenicia and the early caliphates give no flag image for this span, so there is nothing to compare it with.

era-1289.note: No Commons flag of the Mamluk Sultanate exists. Wikipedia (Mamluk Sultanate) describes yellow sultanic banners and personal blazons, and shows its infobox flag blank. The atlas draws a brown-gold field with a dark eagle-like emblem; no source reads an eagle, so the emblem is a reconstruction.

era-1517.note: Redrawn: Ottoman red banner with a single dark crescent (no star), as on the Commons c.1490-1701 flag. Earlier drawing differed from the reference.

era-1861.note: Red field with a white crescent and star, the Ottoman state flag official from 1844; it fits the Mutasarrifate (1861-1918).

era-1920.note: Vertical blue, white, red bands with a green cedar on the white band, as in the Commons mandate-era flag; the atlas cedar is smaller. The caption mentions a plain French tricolour flown alongside, which is not drawn.

era-1943.note: The drawing is the Wikimedia Commons file 'Flag of Lebanon.svg' (Public domain), with scripts, text and external links removed so it embeds in the page; its shapes and colours are the file's own.

era-1868.note: A Blue Ensign with a Union Jack canton and a round badge in the fly matches the unofficial Basutoland ensign on Commons in layout. The Union Jack is simplified and the badge is a plain cream disc where the reference has a coloured shield. The evidence row says both sources contradict a Blue Ensign for the colonial period as a whole (the Union Jack was the flag from 1884 to 1966; this ensign was unofficial and only used after 1951), so it does not fit 1868-1951.

era-1966.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Reference (current flag, 2006): blue band on top (about 30 percent of the height), a broad white band (about 40 percent) holding the black mokorotlo hat, then green (30 percent). Ours has white on top, a broad blue middle band holding the hat, and green below, so the order of blue and white is swapped and the proportions differ (27 / 47 / 27 percent). The hat is also a rough egg shape without the knob. The evidence row notes the era title covers three flags (1966-87, 1987-2006, 2006-) and the card shows only the 2006 one. The replacement fixes the band order and widths and the hat outline. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1822.note: Thirteen red and white stripes with a blue canton bearing a white cross in place of stars: the same design as the 1827-1847 reference. Canton proportions slightly different.

era-1839.note: Thirteen red and white stripes with a blue canton bearing a white cross in place of stars: the same design as the 1827-1847 reference. Canton proportions slightly different.

era-1847.note: Eleven red and white stripes (red top and bottom), blue canton with one white five-point star: the same design as the reference. The canton is drawn larger than the real one (it covers seven stripes where the flag has five) and the white is cream; style differences only.

era-1980.note: Eleven red and white stripes (red top and bottom), blue canton with one white five-point star: the same design as the reference. The canton is drawn larger than the real one (it covers seven stripes where the flag has five) and the white is cream; style differences only.

era-2003.note: Eleven red and white stripes (red top and bottom), blue canton with one white five-point star: the same design as the reference. The canton is drawn larger than the real one (it covers seven stripes where the flag has five) and the white is cream; style differences only.

era-1911.note: Green / white / red vertical tricolour matches the Italian flag; the reference carries the crowned Savoy arms in the white band, which the card omits.

era-1943.note: The card is a four-quarter blue / cream / cream / blue panel with a dashed gold border, which is not a flag of any administration; the real flags the evidence row names are the Union Flag (British zones) and the French flag (Fezzan). The caption does not say the panel is schematic.

era-1951.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Reference: horizontal red / black / green bands (red and green a quarter each, black half) with a white crescent and star in the black band. Ours has the vertical orientation, red at the hoist, green at the fly. The crescent is a thin arc. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1969.note: Redrawn: Red-white-black horizontal bands with a golden hawk in the white band, as the Commons Libyan flag of 1972-1977 (the 1969-72 flag had no hawk). Earlier drawing differed from the reference.

era-1977.note: Plain green field with no emblem matches the reference. The card green is a lighter hue than the reference dark green.

era-2011.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Reference: horizontal bands, red (quarter of the height) on top, black (half) in the middle, green (quarter) at the bottom, with a white crescent and star in the black band. Ours has the same colours as three vertical bands of near-equal width, so the layout is wrong. The crescent is also only a thin arc in ours. The replacement redraws the bands horizontally. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-900.note: Red field with a white crescent and five-pointed star matches the Ottoman flag in idea, but the card's star sits across the crescent's tips instead of in its mouth, and the crescent is smaller. The reference is dated only from the late 18th century while the era runs from c. 900 (see evidence row), so the design is right for the late Ottoman period only.

era-1815.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The drawing is a cream field with a brown frame, a red disc and a dark vertical bar, which is not a flag design. The Commons Liechtenstein flag for 1719-1852 is a yellow (gold) band over a red band, horizontal (the evidence row agrees). fixSvg draws it. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1866.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The drawing is blue over red (horizontal), which matches the 1921-1937 flag (Flag_of_Liechtenstein_(1921–1937).svg). The Commons flag for 1852-1921 is vertical, red at the hoist and blue at the fly. The evidence row says Wikipedia and FOTW leave the orientation before 1921 unsettled, so the horizontal drawing is firm only for 1921-37. fixSvg draws the vertical Commons version. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1937.note: Blue over red with a gold crown in the blue stripe near the hoist: same layout and colours as the reference. The crown is a tiny abstract gold glyph in the extreme upper corner, much smaller and further from the hoist-centre than the reference crown, and has no arches or cap.

era-1795.note: Ours is a white-blue-red tricolour captioned as the Imperial Russian flag flown over a governorate. White-blue-red is the Russian civil tricolour (Commons Flag_of_Russia.svg), but no source read says which flag the Russian administration flew over the Lithuanian governorates, so the picture cannot be checked as a flag of Lithuania in 1795-1918.

era-1918.note: Yellow-green-red horizontal tricolour in the same order and hues as the Commons interwar flag.

era-1940.note: Red field with a gold hammer and sickle at the hoist, as in the reference. The Commons flag also carries gold lettering (the republic's name) in the top corner, which ours omits (the caption calls it plain); ours adds a gold star above the emblem, which could not be matched against the reference at this resolution.

era-1941.note: The Reich flag (red field, white disc, black swastika turned on its point) drawn as the occupiers' flag; the sources read do not document a flag specific to this territory, so it is a stand-in, not an attested local flag.

era-1944.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Red field with a gold star, sickle and hammer in the upper hoist corner, matching the reference's emblem. The bottom stripes are wrong: the Commons 1953-88 flag has red for about two thirds of the height, then a thin white stripe (about 8%), then a green stripe about a quarter of the height flush with the bottom edge. Ours has two thin stripes (about 5% each) of cream and green with a strip of red still showing below the green. fixSvg keeps ours emblem and corrects the stripes. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1990.note: Yellow-green-red horizontal tricolour in the same order and hues as the reference (ratio differs only by canvas).

era-1569.note: Emblem redrawn by hand on 2026-10-25 and compared by eye with the reference: same layout and colours, emblem simplified (shape and detail reduced).

era-1253.note: Emblem redrawn by hand on 2026-10-25 and compared by eye with the reference: same layout and colours, emblem simplified (shape and detail reduced).

era-1443.note: White field with a red diagonal saltire, as in the Burgundian banner file. The ragged-staff cross is drawn as plain bars with round dots for the stubs, and the small central emblem in the reference is omitted.

era-1581.note: White field with a red diagonal saltire, as in the Cross of Burgundy files. The ragged-staff cross is drawn as plain bars with round dots for the stubs. The caption mentions a Spanish Habsburg crown, which the Commons Spanish Netherlands variant shows at the centre but the atlas omits.

era-1795.note: Vertical blue, white, red tricolour in the same order as the French flag of 1794-1815.

era-1815.note: Looked at the Commons file lists for the Flag of Luxembourg and Duchy of Luxembourg articles: the only Luxembourg flag is the modern tricolour, which Wikipedia says was fixed in 1845 (and says Luxembourg had no flag before about 1830). The atlas draws that tricolour for 1815-1839, so it is likely too early; no drawing of what marked the Grand Duchy 1815-1830 was found.

era-1839.note: Red, white, light blue horizontal tricolour, same as the reference; fixed in 1845 per Wikipedia.

era-1890.note: Red, white, light blue horizontal tricolour, same as the reference; the tricolour was fixed in 1845.

era-1940.note: Redrawn after the Commons Flag of Germany (1935–1945): red field, white disc, black swastika turned on its point.

era-1944.note: Red, white, light blue horizontal tricolour, same order and hues as the reference.

era-1714.note: Emblem redrawn by hand on 2026-10-25 and compared by eye with the reference: same layout and colours, emblem simplified (shape and detail reduced).

era-13.note: Plain red field matches FOTW's description; the Commons drawing of the Kruševo flag is red with a yellow inscription, which ours omits. Wikipedia and FOTW disagree on what flag was flown, and the Commons file is unsourced here.

era-1346.note: Gold field with a red eagle matches the reconstruction in layout and colour; the eagle is reduced to a red shield-and-wings silhouette, not the double-headed eagle of the reference.

era-1392.note: Redrawn: Ottoman red banner with a single dark crescent (no star), as on the Commons c.1490-1701 flag. Earlier drawing differed from the reference.

era-1912.note: Blue-white-red horizontal tricolour matches the Yugoslav flag of 1918-41 but not 1912-18, when the Serbian flag was red-blue-white (Flag_of_Serbia_(1882–1918).svg). The caption says there was no regional flag, so this is a stand-in for the ruling state's flag.

era-1941.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The Bulgarian flag is three horizontal stripes, white over green over red; ours has the same colours as vertical stripes. Evidence for use in Macedonia is a single FOTW line. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1944.note: Red field with a red star outlined in gold in the upper hoist: matches the 1946-92 design; the star is a little smaller and nearer the corner than in the reference. The 1944-46 first flag (a centred gold-outlined star, Flag_of_North_Macedonia_(1944–1946).svg) is not drawn.

era-1992.note: Red field with a sixteen-ray yellow sun around a disc: matches in layout. Rays are plain wedges of nearly equal length, whereas the reference has rounded rays alternating long and short; the gold is a duller shade.

era-1995.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Reference: red field, eight yellow rays widening to the edges (four cardinal, four to the corners) around a yellow disc with a red ring. Ours: eight narrow spikes that stop short of the edges, the horizontal pair stop well short, plus stray extra wedges near the centre, and no ring; it reads as a different, smaller sun. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1810.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Wikipedia (per the evidence) describes Radama's 1810 flag as a white-and-red bicolour, and the Commons Merina flag is white over red horizontal halves. The drawing is a cream field with a red border and a red disc holding a white star, which no source describes (the page labels it its own reconstruction). It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1896.note: Caption says schematic. The French vertical blue-white-red tricolour is right; the brown disc in the white band stands in for a colonial badge and is not on the reference flag (the evidence finds only the plain French flag hoisted in 1896).

era-1958.note: White hoist third with red over green on the fly, as the reference.

era-1891.note: Blue ensign with a Union Flag canton and a badge on the fly, as in the Commons ensigns. Ours shows the badge as a white disc holding a red X; the Commons British Central Africa Protectorate ensign has a tree badge with red fruits (Flag_of_British_Central_Africa_Protectorate.svg) and the Nyasaland ensigns of 1914-64 a leopard, so the red X matches neither. The Union Flag is drawn with a centred red saltire. The evidence row notes the single badge fits 1914-1953 only.

era-1953.note: Blue ensign with a Union Flag canton and a badge on the fly, as in the Commons ensigns. Ours shows the badge as a white disc with a thin brown outline and nothing inside; the Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland badge in the reference is a coloured shield-type device (yellow and black) on the blue field. The Union Flag is drawn with a centred red saltire.

era-1964.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Black-red-green bands as in the reference, but the sun is broken. The Commons flag has a red half-sun rising from the bottom edge of the black band, with 31 long rays across the upper half. Ours draws a quarter arc in orange (not red) at the top of the black band and five scattered round dots, which do not form a rising sun. fixSvg redraws the sun as a half disc with 31 rays. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1826.note: Redrawn: Blue Ensign with a gold crown in the fly, the Straits Settlements flag of 1868-1877. Earlier drawing differed from the reference.

era-1826-1.note: No reference found: Commons file lists for Flag of Malaysia and Flags of Malaysia carry no flag or banner for the Malacca Sultanate or its successor sultanates before the Federated Malay States, and neither Wikipedia nor FOTW (per the evidence) describes one. The plain red field is therefore unsupported; the evidence says FOTW mentions yellow as the Malay royal colour.

era-1942.note: White field with a centred red disc, as the Japanese flag (disc somewhat smaller than the reference). Rests on a single Wikipedia infobox caption per the evidence.

era-1946.note: Redrawn: Red, yellow and black horizontal bands with a tiger in a white oval, as the Commons flag of the Federated Malay States. Earlier drawing differed from the reference.

era-1957.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Eleven red and white stripes match. The canton should hold a yellow crescent and an 11-pointed star on a blue canton about half the flag's length; the drawing has a smaller canton with one five-pointed star and no crescent. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1963.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Fourteen red and white stripes match. The canton is wrong: the reference has a blue canton about half the flag's length holding a yellow CRESCENT and a 14-pointed star; the drawing has a smaller canton with a single five-pointed star and no crescent. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1153.note: Plain red field, as in the earliest-flag file (Wikipedia gives 1117-1796). The caption calls it a reconstruction.

era-1558.note: Redrawn: White flag with the crowned Portuguese royal shield, as the Commons Portuguese flag of 1578. Earlier drawing differed from the reference.

era-1573.note: Plain red field, as in the earliest-flag file. Wikipedia dates the plain red flag to 1117-1796 and a striped-hoist flag from 1796, so the late part of this era is not covered.

era-1887.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The drawing is a red field with a white-bordered black panel carrying the Arabic word for God. No Commons flag of the Maldives has such a panel. The Commons old national flag is red with a black-and-white striped hoist band and a small white crescent opening to the hoist; the older flag (until 1903) has the striped band without the crescent, and the 1926-1953 state flag adds a green rectangle. The fix shows the national flag. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1953.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The drawing is a red field with a white-bordered black panel and a black-on-white crescent. The Commons flag for 1953-1965 (the Wikipedia fifth flag) is red with a black-and-white diagonally striped band at the hoist and a green rectangle holding a white crescent that opens toward the hoist. The badge is a cream box with a star, not the seal. The caption now says which period the drawing fits.

era-1907.note: Red field with the Union Flag in the canton and a badge in the fly, as in the Commons Dominion of Newfoundland Red Ensign. The badge (a round seal with the allegorical scene) is replaced by a cream box with a red star; the canton is slightly simplified (red diagonals not offset).

era-1934.note: Union Flag layout and colours match; the red diagonals are centred on the white ones rather than offset as in the real flag.

era-1949.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The caption and both sources say the Union Flag was the provincial flag from 1949 to 1980, and the drawing is a Red Ensign: red field, Union Flag in the canton and a badge in the fly. The Commons Union Flag is the plain blue, white and red flag; the Red Ensign drawn here is the 1904-1949 Newfoundland flag, not the 1949 one. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1524.note: Red saltire on white matches the Cross of Burgundy in layout, but the reference saltire is ragged (knotted-branch edges) and the drawing's arms are straight smooth bars. From 1785 the Spanish flag (Flag_of_Spain_(1785–1873,_1875–1931).svg: red-yellow-red) replaced it, so the drawing covers only part of the span.

era-1821.note: Vertical green-white-red tricolour matches the First Mexican Empire flag; the crowned eagle on a cactus is reduced to a plain brown disc. Evidence: no source says this flag flew over Nicaragua.

era-1823.note: Blue-white-blue with a central emblem matches the Federal Republic flag. The emblem (triangle of volcanoes, rainbow, cap, rays and ring of text on the reference) is reduced to an oval with five volcano triangles and a red arc.

era-1838.note: Blue-white-blue with a small volcano emblem in the white band matches the 1896-1908 style flag in layout (emblem reduced to an oval outline and one triangle). The span 1838-1908 also saw non-blue-white-blue flags, for example the yellow-white-red tricolour of Flag_of_Nicaragua_(1839-1858).svg and the 1854-58 flags, which the card does not show.

era-1908.note: Blue-white-blue horizontal bands match. The reference emblem is an equilateral triangle holding five volcanoes, a rainbow, a Phrygian cap and rays, ringed by the words REPÚBLICA DE NICARAGUA - AMÉRICA CENTRAL; the drawing shows an oval with five volcano triangles, a red arc and three rays, with no cap and no ring of text.

era-1958.note: Orange - white - green horizontal bands in equal thirds with an orange disc in the centre of the white band, same as the reference (disc a little smaller than the reference).

era-1960.note: Orange - white - green horizontal bands in equal thirds with an orange disc in the centre of the white band, same as the reference (disc a little smaller than the reference).

era-1861.note: Plain Blue Ensign (navy field, Union Jack canton) with no badge. The evidence row says it is a generic stand-in: Lagos flew a badged Blue Ensign only from 1886 and nothing is documented for 1861-1886. The caption says unbadged, so it is flagged as such.

era-1914.note: Blue Ensign with a Union Jack canton and a round badge in the fly matches the layout. The Union Jack is simplified (no offset diagonals) and the badge is a cream disc with a green zigzag and a gold dot, where the reference badge is a red disc with the crown and lettering; the caption already says simplified. The 1952 and 1914 badge designs differ, as the evidence row notes.

era-1960.note: Green / white / green vertical bands in equal thirds match the reference (same flag since 1 October 1960).

era-1963.note: Green / white / green vertical bands in equal thirds match the reference.

era-1392.note: The card is a dashed-border panel reading NO NATIONAL FLAG YET on royal blue, which the caption already presents as having no documented flag. The Commons royal standard of Joseon (1876) is a red field with a dark border and gold emblem, so no blue dynastic flag is supported either.

era-1883.note: The drawing is the Wikimedia Commons file 'Flag of Korea (1882–1910).svg' (Public domain), with scripts, text and external links removed so it embeds in the page; its shapes and colours are the file's own.

era-1897.note: The drawing is the Wikimedia Commons file 'Flag of Korea (1882–1910).svg' (Public domain), with scripts, text and external links removed so it embeds in the page; its shapes and colours are the file's own.

era-1910.note: White field with a centred red disc of diameter three fifths of the height matches the Japanese flag reference.

era-1945.note: The north's 1946-48 provisional flag is a taegukgi: white field, red-and-blue yin-yang disc, black trigram bars in the four corners. Ours keeps the disc but leaves out all four trigrams and adds a dashed navy border that is not in the reference. The evidence row already says the north's flag was a variant of the taegukgi.

era-1948.note: Blue / thin white / wide red / thin white / blue horizontal bands with a white disc and red five-pointed star toward the hoist match the reference layout and colours. Proportions are close (bands 15 / 5 / 60 percent of height vs 17 / 3 / 61 percent); the disc is slightly smaller than the reference (about 17 percent of the height as radius vs 22 percent).

era-676.note: Dashed-border panel reading NO NATIONAL FLAG YET on dark red, not a drawing of a flag. Commons has a reconstructed Silla military banner, noted in the evidence row as a reconstruction.

era-918.note: Dashed-border panel reading NO NATIONAL FLAG YET on maroon, not a drawing of any flag. Wikipedia's Flag of Korea does list three Goryeo royal flags (e.g. the Bong-gi, a yellow field with a phoenix) so the claim of no flag is only true of a state flag.

era-1177.note: Blue field with a gold harp, as in the Commons Royal Standard of Ireland (used 1542-1801); ours draws the harp as a few curved strokes with string lines, and adds a small red star-shaped mark at the lower left (the page's 'red hand for Ulster'), which the reference does not have and no source supports. The standard is dated 1542-1801, so 1177-1542 (the Lordship) has no documented flag.

era-1801.note: Union Flag: blue field, white and red saltires and St George's cross, the same arrangement as the reference. Ours draws St Patrick's red saltire centred on the white St Andrew's saltire; the reference has the red saltire thin and counterchanged (offset within the white), so the diagonals look different. The 1801 design is the same as today's.

era-1921.note: Union Flag: blue field, white and red saltires and St George's cross, the same arrangement as the reference. Ours draws St Patrick's red saltire centred on the white St Andrew's saltire; the reference has the red saltire thin and counterchanged (offset within the white), so the diagonals look different.

era-1953.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: White field with a red St George's cross, a white star bearing a red hand and a crown above, as in the reference. The star is wrong: the Commons banner has a six-pointed star (the vector path has twelve vertices) with a thin dark outline, ours is a five-pointed star. The cross is a brick-red (#9c3b28) where the reference is a plain bright red (#cc0000), the star is oversized and the crown is a gold arc with no detail. fixSvg draws the six-pointed star, red cross and crown. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1972.note: Union Flag: blue field, white and red saltires and St George's cross, the same arrangement as the reference. Ours draws St Patrick's red saltire centred on the white St Andrew's saltire; the reference has the red saltire thin and counterchanged (offset within the white), so the diagonals look different.

era-1507.note: A text card ('CONTESTED / NO SINGLE FLAG') rather than a flag drawing; no Portuguese-period or Nabhani imamate banner appears in the sources read or on the Wikipedia Oman pages.

era-1624.note: Plain red stand-in; the caption calls it an informed reconstruction. The only reference is the later (1856-1970) Muscat red flag; no Ya'ariba-period flag appears in the sources.

era-1744.note: Plain red field. Commons has only the plain red Flag_of_Muscat.svg, which Wikipedia dates 1856-1970; nothing dated 1744-1856 is in the sources or on the Wikipedia Oman pages.

era-1856.note: Plain red field matches the Commons flag of Muscat; ours is a slightly darker red.

era-1970.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Wrong layout: the reference has a red hoist band one third of the width and, on the fly, white over red over green stripes, with a white khanjar-and-swords emblem at the top of the hoist band. Ours has a cream hoist band with a green block and a plain red fly, and a crude grid-like mark instead of the emblem. Fix simplifies the emblem. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1362.note: Looked at the Commons Ottoman flag files (Zulfikar flag, Ottoman flag c.1490-1701 and 1540s-1701, army banners of 1721 and 1788): none is a green standard of 1362-1453. The atlas draws green with a white pole and arc, which the caption calls a plain green standard; the sources describe a horse-tail tugh only in 18th-century records.

era-1453.note: Redrawn: Ottoman red banner with a single dark crescent (no star), as on the Commons c.1490-1701 flag. Earlier drawing differed from the reference.

era-1517.note: Redrawn: Ottoman red banner with a single dark crescent (no star), as on the Commons c.1490-1701 flag. Earlier drawing differed from the reference.

era-1844.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Red field with a white crescent opening to the fly and a star is the right design, but the atlas crescent is a thin sliver (about 38% of the height against 56% in the file) and the star is a malformed half-star arrowhead rather than a five-pointed star set between the horns. The fix uses the file's proportions. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1922.note: The drawing is a dashed maroon text card (SULTANATE ABOLISHED), not a flag; the caption points to the Turkey page. No flag for this one-year span is separately documented, so there is nothing to compare.

era-14.note: Dark green field with a white hoist band a quarter of the length, and a white crescent opening toward the fly with a five-pointed star, match the reference. Crescent and star are a little smaller and less tilted than in the reference.

era-1526.note: Caption says schematic. Ours is a green rectangle with a cream ring and star; the Commons Mughal alam is a green triangular pennant with a gold lion-and-sun, so the ring and star are an invention (the evidence row says the lion and sun are omitted).

era-1857.note: Red field with a Union Jack canton and a star badge in the fly matches the British Indian Red Ensign. The canton is a simplified Union Jack (no offset diagonals) and the Star of India badge is reduced to a plain cream star, where the reference has a gold disc-and-star emblem. As the evidence row notes, the Red Ensign dates only from 1880.

era-1956.note: Dark green field with a white hoist band a quarter of the length, and a white crescent opening toward the fly with a five-pointed star, match the reference. Crescent and star are a little smaller and less tilted than in the reference. The same 1947 flag; the sources say it was retained in 1956.

era-1971.note: Dark green field with a white hoist band a quarter of the length, and a white crescent opening toward the fly with a five-pointed star, match the reference. Crescent and star are a little smaller and less tilted than in the reference.

era-1885.note: Red - yellow - red horizontal flag with the yellow band double width matches the Spanish flag of the period. The royal arms in the yellow band are left out.

era-1899.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The German imperial black - white - red horizontal tricolour is the nearest flag the sources support (FOTW says the Carolines used the Foreign Office service flag or the imperial ensign, with no special colonial flag). Ours is a white field with a black-white-red canton and a black ring-and-star badge in the fly, which no Commons German imperial flag file shows. Replacement is the plain tricolour; the service flag and ensign carried an eagle or cross that is not drawn. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1914.note: Red disc on white, disc three fifths of the height, same as the Japanese flag.

era-1947.note: Thirteen red and white stripes (red top and bottom) with a blue canton about two fifths of the width and seven stripes deep match the US flag. The stars are round dots in a grid rather than five-pointed stars. (The evidence row also names the UN flag and the Trust Territory flag as flown at times; those are not drawn.)

era-1994.note: Light blue field with a gold disc set slightly toward the hoist, same as the reference. The disc is a little larger than the reference (about 66 percent of the height against 60 percent) and the blue is softer, which is style.

era-1519.note: White field with a red saltire as the Cross of Burgundy; the ragged (knotted) branches are plain straight bars. The evidence notes the cross cannot be shown as the colony's banner over the whole 1519-1821 span.

era-1821.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Same layout error: the drawing has yellow on top with blue and red side by side below, instead of the three horizontal bands (yellow, blue, red) of Gran Colombia. Fix: equal horizontal yellow-blue-red bands. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1830.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The caption names Colombia's tricolour from 1861. The drawing is a yellow top half over a blue left and red right quarter, a split bottom half; the real flag has full-width horizontal blue and red bands under the yellow (the earlier New Granada flags 1830-1861 and the Panama state flags are different again). Fix: yellow half, blue quarter, red quarter in horizontal bands. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1903.note: Same quartered design as the reference (white/blue star, red, blue, white/red star); the 1903 flag is the same layout as the current one.

era-1999.note: White top-left with a blue star, red top-right, blue bottom-left, white bottom-right with a red star: the same quartering and star colours as the reference.

era-1537.note: Red saltire on white matches the Cross of Burgundy; the reference saltire is made of ragged staves, ours has straight bars.

era-1811.note: Red - white - blue triband matches the flag from 1842. The span starts in 1811, when the Commons flags are different (File:Flag_of_Paraguay_(1811).svg, a blue flag, and blue-yellow-red stripes, then 1812-1826 and 1826-1842 variants), so only the last part of the span is drawn; the arms are left out.

era-1864.note: Red - white - blue horizontal triband matches the 1842-1954 flag; its arms (the obverse emblem) and the seal on the reverse are left out.

era-1870.note: Red - white - blue horizontal triband in equal bands matches the national flag. The state arms (obverse) are left out, though the caption mentions them.

era-224.note: Both the card and the Commons drawing are artist reconstructions of the derafsh, and the caption says reconstructed. They differ a lot: the Commons reconstruction is a purple field with yellow ornament in a red border with a yellow fringe; ours is a gold trapezoid with four red studs on dark red. Neither is a surviving flag (FOTW: no image survives).

era-247bce.note: Caption says reconstructed. No source read describes a Parthian bow-and-horse standard (evidence row), and the drawing (gold pole, arch, ring and curve on blue) does not clearly show a bow or a horse either; the sourced Persis coin standards are flag-like devices, not this.

era-312bce.note: Caption says reconstructed. A gold disc with a bar and stem (anchor-and-sun idea) on maroon; the sources read mention only flag-like standards on Persis coins, not a Seleucid anchor device. No reference image exists for it.

era-334bce.note: Dashed-border text panel (ALEXANDER'S CONQUEST on dark red), not a drawing of a flag. The sources read cover no Alexander-period flag.

era-550bce.note: Caption says reconstructed. Ours is a crude gold winged-disc figure (the faravahar idea) on blue. Wikipedia describes the faravahar as a relief emblem, not a flag; the Commons Standard of Cyrus is a different design (red field, gold bird emblem, bordered), and Xenophon's golden eagle is the nearest sourced standard. Neither matches the blue field.

era-633.note: The card is a dashed-border text panel (ARAB-ISLAMIC CONQUEST on dark red), not a drawing of any flag; no flag is depicted, which the caption (the empire falls, see Iran page) implies but does not state outright. The only flag event in the sources is the loss of the derafsh at Qadisiyya (c. 636-637).

era-1532.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Same drawing as the 1542 card (red top band and three gold squares on white) matching no flag; the Burgundy cross is the Spanish ensign the sources give for the conquistadors. Fix: white field with red saltire. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1542.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The sources point to the Spanish red-and-white Cross of Burgundy over the viceroyalty. The drawing is a white field with a red band across the top and three gold squares, which matches no flag read. Fix: white field with red saltire (ragged branches simplified to straight bars). It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1821.note: Vertical red-white-red with a gold emblem on the white stripe matches the 1822 triband (Wikipedia, 31 May 1822). The reference carries a wreathed sun emblem; the drawing shows a plain gold five-point star. It does not match San Martin's 1820-22 diagonally quartered flag (Flag_of_Peru_(1821–1822).svg) or the horizontal 1822 flag FOTW gives.

era-1825.note: Vertical red-white-red in equal bands, as the plain civil flag of the reference.

era-1565.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The caption says Cross of Burgundy ensign, and the Commons file is a white field with a red saltire. Ours is a red field cut by white and yellow triangles with a thin red frame, which resembles none of the Spanish flag files (Cross of Burgundy, New Spain, Spain 1785-1873). The evidence row notes no source describes the Spanish-era flag in Manila. Fix: white field with a red saltire (ragged-staff knots simplified to dots). It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1898.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The drawing is a white field with four thin red and blue strips: it matches no flag file. The evidence row finds no source for a stripes-only "insular ensign"; the Wikipedia article on the Philippine flag lists the US flags of the period (45 to 48 stars) for this era. Fix: the US flag (48-star version shown), which is what the sources imply was flown; the star count changed within the era (45, 46, 48). It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1898-1.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Layout and colours match the 1898-1901 file (white triangle, blue over red). The reference sun has a face and eight long rays and the stars are five-pointed; ours is a plain disc with dot stars. Fix: eight-rayed sun (face omitted) and five-pointed stars. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1935.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Layout matches the 1919-1936 and 1936-1985 files (white triangle, blue over red) but the field blue is the modern bright blue, where both files use a dark navy; the sun is a plain disc and the stars are dots. Fix: navy blue, eight-rayed sun, five-pointed stars. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1942.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The caption says it is the same flag, and the 1943-1945 Commons file is the white triangle with blue over red. Ours has an all-red field (no blue half) and discs for stars. Fix: blue over red with the proper sun and stars (the 1943-1945 file uses a mid blue). The evidence row notes the flag may have been flown red-side up in wartime, which neither drawing shows. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1945.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Layout matches the 1936-1985 flag (white triangle, blue over red). The sun is a plain disc with no rays and the three stars are drawn as round dots, not five-pointed stars. Fix: eight-rayed sun (centred nearer the hoist) and three five-pointed stars. Ours also uses the bright modern blue; the 1936-1985 file uses a dark navy, so the fix uses navy. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1946.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Layout and colours match (white hoist triangle, blue over red). The sun is a plain disc with no rays and the three stars are drawn as round dots, not five-pointed stars. Fix: eight-rayed sun (centred nearer the hoist) and three five-pointed stars. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1795.note: Not a flag drawing: a "NO FLAG DOCUMENTED" text card, honest to the evidence (no source gives a Polish banner for 1795-1807). Nothing to compare with.

era-1807.note: Drawing is a plain white-red bicolour. Commons has only the Duchy of Warsaw arms (Grand_Coat_of_Arms_of_Duchy_of_Warsaw.svg, Coat_of_Arms_of_Duchy_of_Warsaw.svg), no flag; the evidence notes Wikipedia says the Duchy had no national flag and FOTW posts conflict. Looked at the Commons file lists of Duchy of Warsaw, Congress Poland, Flag of Poland.

era-1945.note: Plain white over red bicolour matches the national flag of the period; same design as the reference.

era-1947.note: Plain white over red bicolour matches the civil flag; the crownless eagle only appears on the separate state flag/arms. Muted red, same design.

era-1989.note: White over red, two equal horizontal stripes, as the current flag. Red is a duller brick tone than the specified vermilion, hue still correct.
