era-1025.note: Emblem redrawn by hand on 2026-10-25 and compared by eye with the reference: same layout and colours, emblem simplified (shape and detail reduced).

era-1139.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The Commons 1248 flag is a white field with five blue escutcheons in a cross, framed by a red border carrying yellow castles; the 1185 flag is the same without the border. Ours is a single large red-and-blue shield with five dots in the middle of a plain white field, with no border, no castles and no five-shield cross, so it matches neither. The caption says reconstruction. Replacement follows the 1248 design (shields and castles simplified). It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1580.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The Commons Portuguese flags for the end of this period (1578, 1640) are white with the crowned royal arms, and the evidence row says both publishers show Portuguese arms flags in use during the Iberian Union. Ours draws a Cross of Burgundy instead, and badly: the saltire is broken in the middle where the reference saltire is continuous. Replacement is the white arms flag (arms simplified). It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1640.note: Blue hoist half, white fly and crowned royal arms on the seam match the 1830-1910 flag. Only the later part of the span: before 1830 the royal flag was white with the arms (evidence row). The arms are reduced to a red shield with blue inner panel and five dots under a gold crown band.

era-1910.note: Green hoist about 2/5 and red fly 3/5 with the emblem on the seam matches the 1910/1911 republican flag. The emblem is reduced to a gold disc with a red centre and a cross: the armillary sphere is a plain disc and the white shield with the five blue escutcheons is left out.

era-1926.note: The flag is the 1911 flag (Commons: official flag), green hoist about 2/5, red fly 3/5, emblem on the seam; the drawing matches that. The emblem is reduced to a gold disc with a red centre and a cross: the armillary sphere is a plain disc and the white shield with the five blue escutcheons is left out.

era-1974.note: Green hoist and red fly in about 2:3 with the emblem on the seam matches. The emblem is reduced to a gold disc with a red centre and a cross: the armillary sphere is a plain disc and the white shield with the five blue escutcheons is left out.

era-1453.note: Not a flag: an OTTOMAN CONQUEST pointer card (text on a dashed frame); nothing to compare.

era-27bce.note: Redrawn as a legionary aquila (eagle standard) above a vexillum bearing SPQR, as the caption describes; a reconstruction, not a surviving flag.

era-284.note: Dark red banner with gold shapes stands for the labarum, but the reference shows a gold Chi-Rho wreath on top of a pole above a hanging purple-red cloth with medallions; the drawing has a gold T-shaped bar, an arc and a small disc instead of the Chi-Rho. The caption says reconstructed.

era-330.note: Redrawn as the double-headed eagle the caption names, reconstructed from later imperial use; no Byzantine flag of this period is documented.

era-395.note: Invented split card (red West, blue East with gold bars and letters W and E). The caption says reconstructed; no source describes standards for either half and Commons has no flag of the 395 division.

era-509bce.note: Flat red field with a gold SPQR plaque as a stand-in for a Republican vexillum. Wikipedia says a red vexillum with yellow SPQR is only sometimes reported and unsourced, and a real vexillum is a hanging cloth, not a flat flag; the caption already says the inscription is not established.

era-1859.note: Horizontal red-yellow-blue (red top) matches the Commons 1862-66 file and Wikipedia, but the Commons 1859-62 file is blue-yellow-red (blue on top), which FOTW also gives for 1859-62, so the order is right for only part of the span. Ours adds a small red-over-blue badge at the centre that neither Commons file shows; the references are plain horizontal tricolours.

era-1881.note: Vertical blue-yellow-red matches. Wikipedia and FOTW say the arms appear only on army, naval and princely flags (the civil flag is plain), and the evidence row says the caption claim of the king's own arms is unconfirmed; ours reduces any arms to a cream box with a gold arc, which is only a placeholder for an unsourced emblem.

era-1918.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Wikipedia and the evidence row say the civilian tricolour carried no arms, which sit only on army and princely/military flags; the Commons Flag_of_Romania.svg used as the kingdom flag is plain. Ours adds a small cream box with a gold arc at the centre that is neither arms nor sourced. fixSvg is the plain vertical tricolour; not viewed after drawing. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1940.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Wikipedia and the evidence row say the civilian tricolour carried no arms, which sit only on army and princely/military flags; the Commons Flag_of_Romania.svg used as the kingdom flag is plain. Ours adds a small cream box with a gold arc at the centre that is neither arms nor sourced. Antonescu personal standard with arms exists but is not a national flag. fixSvg is the plain vertical tricolour; not viewed after drawing. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1944.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Wikipedia and the evidence row say the civilian tricolour carried no arms, which sit only on army and princely/military flags; the Commons Flag_of_Romania.svg used as the kingdom flag is plain. Ours adds a small cream box with a gold arc at the centre that is neither arms nor sourced. fixSvg is the plain vertical tricolour; not viewed after drawing. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1947.note: Tricolour right. The references (1948-52, 1952-65, 1965-89 Commons files) carry a state emblem at the centre (wheat wreath, forested mountains, oil derrick, sun/red star on top, ribbon); ours has only a red star outlined in gold, so the emblem is reduced to one element. The emblem differed between the three periods and the drawing does not distinguish them.

era-1989.note: Vertical blue-yellow-red equal thirds, blue at hoist, no emblem: same as Flag_of_Romania.svg (ours is a darker, duller shade of each; hue and order match).

era-1600-1.note: Emblem redrawn by hand on 2026-10-25 and compared by eye with the reference: same layout and colours, emblem simplified (shape and detail reduced).

era-1600.note: Emblem redrawn by hand on 2026-10-25 and compared by eye with the reference: same layout and colours, emblem simplified (shape and detail reduced).

era-82bce.note: Caption says reconstructed. Commons shows the draco as a wolf head with open toothed jaws and a long scaled tube tail (modern depiction on a tricolour; Trajan Column scenes are the source). Ours is a maroon field with a gold round head with two antenna strokes and a tail wedge: no jaws or wolf profile, colours invented. Acceptable as a schematic only; attested solely as a military standard. The emblem was redrawn by hand on 2026-10-25.

era-1916.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Wikipedia (per the evidence row) shows the Belgian flag as the flag of Ruanda-Urundi and the Belgian flag is vertical black, yellow, red. Ours has a cream middle band where the reference has yellow, and a gold disc badge that no source documents. Fix: the plain Belgian tricolour. The 1916-1919 years (German then Belgian military occupation) are not covered by the sources. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1962.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The reference is three vertical stripes, red, yellow, green from the hoist, with a black R on the yellow. Ours has the same colours as horizontal stripes. Fix: make them vertical (the R in the reference is a heavy hand-lettered capital, here a system-font R). It was redrawn from the reference.

era-2001.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Three bands with the sun at the upper fly, as in the reference, but the proportions and shade are off: the reference has sky blue over half the height with yellow and dark green a quarter each; ours has a dark royal blue for 65%, only a thin yellow strip (10%) and a bright green quarter. The sun in the reference has 24 rays and is smaller. Fix: sky blue half, yellow quarter, dark-green quarter, 24-ray sun. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1623.note: Red cross on a white field, same as the Flag of England file. The evidence row notes that using the English flag here is the page's own choice: no source states it was flown at Saint Kitts or Nevis.

era-1713.note: Plain Blue Ensign: a Union canton on a dark-blue field. The earliest colonial flag on Commons for these islands is the Leeward Islands flag of 1871 (with a badge); there is no file for 1713-1871 and the evidence row finds no source describing a flag for this period, so nothing to compare it with.

era-1882.note: Ours is a Blue Ensign with a Union canton and a disc badge. That resembles the 1958-1967 St Christopher-Nevis-Anguilla file and the Leeward Islands flag (a Union canton with a badge in the fly), but the 1967-1983 flag (the larger part of the end of this era) is a green, yellow and blue vertical tricolour with a palm (the 1967 file shows it without the palm), which ours does not show. The evidence row says the same. The badge here (white and green discs with a triangle) is not the one in either file. No fix: the palm design is not drawn. The caption now says which period the drawing fits.

era-1983.note: Green upper-hoist triangle, red lower-fly triangle, black diagonal band edged in yellow running from the lower hoist to the upper fly, with two white stars on the band, as in the reference. Band width and star placement are close; the reference stars are slightly tilted.

era-1660.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The drawing is a white field with a gold chess-king glyph (text character), not a fleur-de-lis and not a flag device. The evidence row says Saint Lucia used the Martinique flag under French rule and the drapeau aux serpents from 1766; the Commons Martinique snake flag is a blue field with a white cross and four white snakes in each quadrant. fixSvg draws a simplified version. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1814.note: Dark blue ensign with a Union Jack canton (about half width and height) as in the 1875-1939 and 1939-1967 references. The badge in the fly is a gold triangle with a white edge; the references show a white disc with the island seal (1875-1939) or the arms with Pitons (1939-1967). The Union Jack canton is the old pre-1801 or 1801 style only approximately. The evidence row notes Wikipedia gives a Union Jack-based flag for some of these years.

era-1979.note: Cerulean field with a layered triangle device: white outlined black triangle with a gold triangle in front of it, base near the bottom, apex centred. Same design as the reference (the 1979-2002 variant had a larger gold triangle).

era-1763.note: Redrawn: Blue Ensign with the pre-1801 Union Flag canton. The Union Flag before 1801 had no red diagonal (St Patrick's cross); the drawing's Blue Ensign canton includes the red diagonals of the post-1801 flag. Caption calls it a representative claimant flag (no flag is documented), so the fix is still a stand-in, but with the correct 1707-1800 canton. The caption now says which period the drawing fits.

era-1797.note: Blue Ensign with the Union Jack canton and a disc badge in the fly matches in layout. The badge (a woman figure with an altar and vessels on the reference) is a cream disc with a cross, and the red of the Union Jack is drawn as orange-red. Nothing is documented before 1877.

era-1979.note: Vertical blue, gold, green bands with three green diamonds in a V on the gold band, as the 1985 reference (band widths about 28/44/28 against 25/50/25, diamonds a little smaller). The independence flag of 1979-85 was different, which the era title does not say.

era-1900.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Black-white-red horizontals are right (black on top, as in the reference), but the drawing adds a black rectangle on the hoist side and a gold dome that are not on the flag; the Reichskolonialflagge reference has an eagle in the centre of the white stripe instead, and the plain imperial flag (the evidence row says colonies without arms flew it) has no device. fixSvg gives the plain triband. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1914.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The drawing is a full-field Union Jack (the saltires and cross run corner to corner) with two red stars. The New Zealand ensign reference is a dark blue field with a small Union Jack canton in the upper hoist quarter and four red, white-edged stars in the fly. (The evidence row adds that a Blue Ensign with palms was used under the mandate from 1920.) fixSvg draws the NZ ensign. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1962.note: Same drawing as 1997: red field, blue canton, five white stars as in the reference flag (unchanged from 1949); stars are oversized and not in the exact Southern Cross arrangement.

era-1997.note: Red field with a blue canton covering the upper hoist quarter and a white Southern Cross of five stars: same design as the reference. The stars are drawn about two to three times larger than the reference stars and sit in a different arrangement, so the cross is less recognisable.

era-1600.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Ours is a plain white-over-light-blue bicolour. The oldest attested San Marino flag is the 1465 standard, which the Commons reconstructions show as three vertical bands, yellow/orange, white and violet-red (alessandrino), with the republic's symbol on the white band; the evidence row says the white-and-blue colours begin with the 1797 cockade, not with 1600. fixSvg draws the three vertical bands (without the emblem); the reconstruction is itself an inference from a taffeta receipt. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1862.note: White over light blue with the arms at the centre, as in the reference. The reference arms are a crowned shield showing three towers on three peaks inside a wreath with a ribbon; ours reduces them to a green trapezoid, three grey towers and a gold dot for the crown, with no shield or wreath.

era-301.note: Ours is the white-over-blue bicolour inside a dashed brown frame, which marks it as unverified ('traditional colours'). No source dates white-over-blue before 1797, and the earliest attested flag is the 1465 standard (vertical yellow, white and violet bands in the Commons reconstructions), so for c. 301-1600 the picture is not evidence of anything.

era-1471.note: Green hoist (2/5) and red fly (3/5) as the Portuguese flag of 1910 onward; the armillary sphere and shield are a yellow disc with a white rim. This flag dates only from 1910-11, not from 1471; earlier Portuguese flags are different (see the Cape Verde and Flag of Portugal reference lists).

era-1975.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The flag is green, a wide yellow band across the middle (about 2/4 of the height) and green, with a red triangle at the hoist and two black five-point stars in the yellow band. The drawing has green over 70% of the height with a narrow yellow band at the bottom only, a much larger red triangle, and the two stars are round dots. Fix: 1:2:1 bands, hoist triangle, two black stars in the yellow. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1744.note: Plain green with the white shahada on one line and no sword, as in the Commons file for the First and Second Saudi States (that file shows a white margin on the fly side, which I read as an image border). The calligraphy is replaced by system-font text.

era-1818.note: A dashed-border plaque reading "CONTESTED / NO SINGLE FLAG" on a dark field, a notice and not a flag; the caption already says the period had no single flag. The only Commons file for the period is the First and Second Saudi State green flag (plain green with the shahada), which covers one of the several powers the plaque stands for.

era-1902.note: Green with the shahada and a sword. No Commons flag file or page of the Emirate/Sultanate of Nejd shows a flag for 1902-1926, and the evidence row finds the sword's date disputed (1902 or 1921). The sword is also mirrored compared with the current flag (tip to the right, hilt to the left).

era-1926.note: Plain green with the shahada in two lines and no sword. The evidence row says the dual kingdom's flag in 1926-32 is not established; Commons' pages for the Kingdom of Hejaz and Nejd and the Nejd emirates show only the 1917 Hejaz flag (black, green, white with a red triangle) and the current flag, so there is no period reference to compare against.

era-1932.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Green field with white shahada and sword (the Commons file starts in 1938; the evidence row says Wikipedia has it "by 1938" and FOTW "by 1932"). The sword is mirrored: in the reference (current flag and the 1938-1973 file) the blade tip points toward the hoist and the hilt is at the fly end; ours has the cross-guard at the left and an arrowhead at the right. The shahada is split over two lines where the reference has one line of calligraphy. Fix: sword turned round and the text on one line (system-font Arabic, not calligraphy). It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1973.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Green field with white shahada and sword, but The sword is mirrored: in the reference (current flag and the 1938-1973 file) the blade tip points toward the hoist and the hilt is at the fly end; ours has the cross-guard at the left and an arrowhead at the right. The shahada is split over two lines where the reference has one line of calligraphy. Fix: sword turned round and the text on one line (system-font Arabic, not calligraphy). It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1603.note: Blue field with a white diagonal cross (saltire). Same design as the Commons saltire files; the page uses the sky-blue shade, and the Commons file for 1542-2003 comes in sky blue and navy variants.

era-1707.note: Union Flag layout: white saltire, white-bordered red cross, as in the 1606 Scotland file. The layering differs: in the reference the white saltire lies over the red cross at the centre (the Scottish version), where ours puts the red cross on top. Ours is also sky blue; the reference is the dark navy of the Union Flag.

era-1999.note: Blue field with a white diagonal cross (saltire). Same as the current flag, and the sky blue matches the reference.

era-843.note: Blue field with a white diagonal cross (saltire). Same design as the Commons saltire. The evidence row treats the 843 banner as legend, so this is the later flag projected back.

era-1249.note: Emblem redrawn by hand on 2026-10-25 and compared by eye with the reference: same layout and colours, emblem simplified (shape and detail reduced).

era-1659.note: Vertical blue-white-red tricolour, blue at hoist: matches the French flag, which our own evidence says is the page's assertion for 1659 onward; the tricolour itself dates from 1790-94.

era-1959.note: Green-yellow-red vertical bands with a black kanaga figure on the yellow band: matches. The kanaga is reduced to a stick cross with bent arms and legs, shorter than the reference figure, and has no round head.

era-20.note: Vertical green-yellow-red with a green five-pointed star centred on the yellow band: matches in layout and star size.

era-1371.note: Ours is a dark placard reading NO FLAG DOCUMENTED, consistent with its caption that no banner of Lazar survives. No flag drawing from Commons was found for Moravian Serbia that the sources support; this is a deliberate non-flag.

era-1459.note: Ours is a white crescent and star on red, captioned as the standard Ottoman provincial banner. No flag of the Pashalik of Belgrade is documented in the pages read. The nearest Commons file, Flag_of_Ottoman_Empire_(1517-1793).svg, shows a red field with a crescent device, so the star-and-crescent design is at best a generic Ottoman stand-in and the crescent-with-star form is a later Ottoman design. Looked in: Commons file lists for Flag of Serbia and Sanjak of Smederevo.

era-1804.note: White flag with a red Greek (equal-armed) cross, as in the Commons drawing of the Takovo flag of 1815. Only this flag is drawn for the whole 1804-1878 era; the 1835-78 red-blue-white tricolour with arms and stars is not shown (see Flag_of_Principality_of_Serbia_(1835–1878).svg).

era-1878.note: Plain red-blue-white tricolour, as in the Commons civil flag (the evidence note says the state flag kept the arms in 1878-82; the drawing is the civil flag). Stripe order and hues match.

era-1918.note: Blue-white-red horizontal tricolour, no emblem; matches the reference in order and hue.

era-1941.note: Ours is a faded red-blue-white tricolour with a dashed border, deliberately marked as unconfirmed (the caption says no distinct flag is confirmed). The Commons file for the Nedic government shows a red-blue-white tricolour with arms on the hoist side, but the evidence row notes no source read establishes a state flag for 1941-44, so the ghosted tricolour is a stand-in, not a documented flag.

era-1944.note: Red-blue-white tricolour with a gold-edged red star centred on the blue/white junction, as in the reference. Star point count and placement match; the gold fimbriation is shown.

era-1992.note: Blue-white-red horizontal tricolour with no emblem, as in the reference; stripe order and hues match.

era-2006.note: Emblem redrawn by hand on 2026-10-25 and compared by eye with the reference: same layout and colours, emblem simplified (shape and detail reduced).

era-1166.note: Emblem redrawn by hand on 2026-10-25 and compared by eye with the reference: same layout and colours, emblem simplified (shape and detail reduced).

era-1756.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The drawing is a white left third and a dark blue right two-thirds with the words FLEUR-DE-LIS, which resembles neither the tricolour of 1791 onward (blue, white, red verticals, in the reference) nor the Bourbon royal flags (Royal_flag_of_France.svg is blue with gold fleurs-de-lis). The label is text, not a flag. fixSvg draws the tricolour that the caption names. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1810.note: Dark blue ensign with a Union Jack canton and a badge in the fly, as in the 1903-1961 and 1961-1976 references. The badge is a blank white disc; the references show circular badges with pictorial seals (1903-1961 and 1961-1976; the evidence row describes the 1961 badge as a tortoise, coco-de-mer, boat and fish). Badge-less Union flags used earlier in the era (1810-1903) are not covered.

era-1976.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The drawing is green-white-red horizontal stripes with a gold disc. The Commons independence flag is a white saltire dividing blue triangles at top and bottom from red triangles at hoist and fly. (The evidence row quotes FOTW with the colours the other way round, blue at hoist and fly; the Commons image has red at hoist and fly.) fixSvg redraws it as in the Commons image. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1977.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The drawing is a red field with a green canton holding a gold palm and star. The reference is three horizontal bands, red above, a wavy white band and green below, with no emblem (the evidence row agrees: red, white and green with a wavy white stripe). fixSvg redraws it. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1996.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Colour order is right (blue, yellow, red, white, green fanning from the lower hoist) but the band geometry is not: in the reference the blue/yellow line meets the top edge a third of the way along and yellow/red two thirds along, so the fly edge is only red, white and green in thirds, with green along the bottom. The drawing sends the blue/yellow line to the top fly corner and puts green along the lower hoist, so blue is far too large. fixSvg redraws the bands. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1787.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The Union Flag before 1801 had only the red St George cross and white St Andrew saltire; the red diagonal of St Patrick was added in 1801. The drawing includes the red diagonal stripes of the post-1801 flag, which did not exist in 1787-1801 (and none of the sources says a Union Flag flew at the Province of Freedom). It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1808.note: No reference found: the Commons file list for Flag of Sierra Leone begins with the 1889 Blue Ensign defaced with a badge, and neither Wikipedia nor FOTW (per the evidence) describes any flag for 1808-1889, so the plain undefaced Blue Ensign drawn is not supported.

era-1896.note: Blue Ensign with a Union Jack canton and a disc badge in the fly matches in layout. The Commons badges (1889-1916: elephant, palm, mountains with S.L.; 1916-1961: oil palm and an African figure) are reduced to a cream disc with a brown triangle and a green tree.

era-1961.note: Green over white over blue horizontal bands, as the reference.

era-1975.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Ours is a vertical saffron, cream and green tricolour with a blue disc, i.e. India's flag turned on its side. India's flag is horizontal: saffron over white over green with a navy 24-spoke wheel centred on the white band. The evidence row also notes that neither source says India's flag is Sikkim's state flag. fixSvg draws the horizontal Indian flag. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1947.note: Emblem redrawn by hand on 2026-10-25 and compared by eye with the reference: same layout and colours, emblem simplified (shape and detail reduced).

era-1861.note: Emblem redrawn by hand on 2026-10-25 and compared by eye with the reference: same layout and colours, emblem simplified (shape and detail reduced).

era-1642.note: Ours is a maroon field with a white inner frame and a gold X (crossed dorjes) with four dots. The caption calls it an informed reconstruction of the Namgyal founding banner. Wikipedia's Flag of Sikkim names no Sikkimese flag before 1877 (Nepalese, Bhutanese and Tibetan banners and then the Union Jack are mentioned), so there is no reference to compare; the drawing is an unsupported stand-in. The emblem was redrawn by hand on 2026-10-25.

era-1819.note: Redrawn: Blue Ensign with a gold crown in the fly, the Straits Settlements flag of 1868-1877. Earlier drawing differed from the reference.

era-1942.note: White field with a centred red disc, as the Japanese flag (disc a little smaller than the reference).

era-1946.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Wikipedia's Commons files for the Crown Colony (1946-1952 and 1952-1959) are a Blue Ensign with a badge of a red diamond with one crown on a white disc in the fly. The drawing is a plain Union Flag, which is what FOTW's main page says; the evidence notes FOTW conflicts with its own sub-page and with Wikipedia. The badge in the fix is simplified. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1963.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Same drawing and same fault as the 1965-present card: thin crescent and stars partly lost on the white half. (Whether the 1959 flag flew inside Malaysia is not established by the sources.) It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1965.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Red over white halves match, but the emblem is broken: the crescent is a thin sliver instead of the broad crescent open to the right, and the ring of five stars is spread so that two stars fall on the white half where they are cream on cream and invisible. The reference has a broad white crescent and five white stars in a ring, all within the red half. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1000.note: Eight horizontal stripes, red and silver alternating from the top (Arpad stripes), same as the Commons file. Whether it was flown in 1000 is a dating question, not a drawing one.

era-1918.note: Czechoslovak white-over-red flag with a blue triangle to the middle of the flag, as in Flag_of_Czechoslovakia.svg. The blue triangle was added in March 1920; the 1918-1920 flag was the plain white-red bicolour, so the first two years of the era differ.

era-1938.note: Plain white-blue-red tricolour, no emblem. Wikipedia's List of Slovak flags (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Slovak_flags) uses this one image for 1938-1939 as well as 1939-1945.

era-1939.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The Commons file for 1939-1945 is the plain white-blue-red tricolour with no emblem. Ours adds a blue shield with a white cross at the hoist, which neither the file nor the evidence sources support for 1939 (the arms were added in 1992). Fix: plain tricolour. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1945.note: Czechoslovak white-over-red flag with a blue triangle to the middle of the flag, as in Flag_of_Czechoslovakia.svg.

era-1948.note: Czechoslovak white-over-red flag with a blue triangle to the middle of the flag, as in Flag_of_Czechoslovakia.svg.

era-1990.note: Czechoslovak white-over-red flag with a blue triangle to the middle of the flag, as in Flag_of_Czechoslovakia.svg. It is the federal flag; Slovakia's own plain tricolour of 1990-1992 (Flag_of_Slovakia_(1939–1945).svg is the same design) is not drawn.

era-1993.note: The drawing is the Wikimedia Commons file 'Flag of Slovakia.svg' (Public domain), with scripts, text and external links removed so it embeds in the page; its shapes and colours are the file's own.

era-1699.note: Emblem redrawn by hand on 2026-10-25 and compared by eye with the reference: same layout and colours, emblem simplified (shape and detail reduced).

era-1526.note: Emblem redrawn by hand on 2026-10-25 and compared by eye with the reference: same layout and colours, emblem simplified (shape and detail reduced).

era-1809.note: Vertical blue-white-red French tricolour, blue at hoist: matches the reference.

era-1813.note: A plain red field with no documented flag behind it; the caption says no distinct flag existed for this interval. The Habsburg flag (black over gold) in the reference would be the Austrian authority's colours but no source read says it was used here, so red is an invented stand-in.

era-1816.note: White over red horizontal bicolour with a central arms matches the Commons drawing; the arms are reduced to a black shield with a white star (no eagle; the reference shows the Illyrian arms). Our own evidence says no source describes this flag, so the Commons drawing is unsourced there.

era-1849.note: Black over gold horizontal bicolour matches the Habsburg monarchy flag; but the sources say the Carniolan crownland flag was the white-blue-red tricolour (Flag_of_Krain.svg), so the drawing shows the dynasty, not a crownland. The caption says no single crownland flag existed, so it is a stand-in.

era-1918.note: Horizontal blue-white-red tricolour with equal stripes: matches the reference.

era-1945.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: White-blue-red stripes and a red star with a yellow outline match, but the reference star is centred on the middle of the flag (about 100 of 200, spanning from the white stripe into the red one) and is larger; ours is centred at about 124 and smaller so it sits low in the blue/red stripes. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1991.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Stripes (white, blue, red) and the arms at the hoist straddling white/blue match, but the arms differ: the reference has the three gold stars with two above and one below (ours has one above and two below, and five-pointed), a pointed shield with a red outline and a white Triglav with wavy lines (ours: a square gold-bordered shield and a small arch). Stars of Celje on the real flag are set in an inverted triangle. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-29.note: Horizontal red over white over blue: matches the Commons drawing of this State's flag. The page's own evidence says neither Wikipedia text nor FOTW confirms the order, so this rests on the Commons file alone.

era-658.note: A black panther on gold, drawn as a rough blob. The caption says this is a reconstruction with no period flag. Wikipedia's article image (Carantanian_panther.png) shows a rampant black panther on a white field, so the gold field and the shape are not the published reconstruction.

era-828.note: A plain red field standing in for a period where no flag is attested (the caption says so); no reference drawing exists. Wikipedia's March of Carniola article shows no flag for 828-973.

era-973.note: White-blue-red horizontal tricolour matches the Carniolan flag exactly, but that flag is attested only from 1848; the card spans 973/1364 to 1918, and for the 900 years before 1848 the sources found no Carniolan flag. Correct for 1848-1918 only. The caption now says which period the drawing fits.

era-1285.note: A brown card with the words ADAL & AJURAN SULTANATES; it depicts no flag. Wikipedia's Somalia flag history shows modern drawings of flags for these sultanates (for example the red-and-white Adal flag), which this card does not use.

era-1884.note: Redrawn: British Somaliland (left): Blue Ensign with a white disc badge bearing a kudu; Italian tricolour (right). Earlier drawing differed from the reference.

era-1960.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Ours is the star flag with the extra text 'UNION, 1 JULY 1960' printed across the top of the field; the flag carries no lettering. The design underneath matches the reference. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1969.note: Sky-blue field with one white five-pointed star in the centre: matches; ours is a more cyan, lighter blue than the reference and the star is about the same size.

era-1652.note: Red-white-blue horizontal tricolour, the VOC flag without its white VOC monogram in the middle band (the Commons VOC flag). The caption calls it the Prince's Flag, which is orange-white-blue (Commons Prinsenvlag.svg); the drawing agrees with the VOC and Dutch tricolours that the evidence row says flew at the Cape, so the caption rather than the picture is off. The era runs to 1806 but the British flew their own flag in 1795-1803.

era-1806.note: Blue ensign with a Union Flag canton and a white disc badge at the fly, as in the Commons Cape Colony ensign (1876-1910); ours reduces the badge to an empty white disc and draws the Union Flag with unequal cross arms and a centred red saltire. The evidence row says the card fits only 1875/76-1910: the Cape flew the plain Union flag from 1806, and the Boer republics' flags (e.g. Flag_of_Transvaal.svg, a green hoist band with red, white and blue stripes) are not shown.

era-1910.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: A red ensign with a Union Flag canton and the badge on a white disc at the fly, as in the reference. The canton is wrong in ours: the Union Flag's field is drawn red with a blue cross, i.e. blue and red are swapped; in the reference the field is blue with a red St George's cross and white saltires. The badge is reduced to an empty white disc. fixSvg draws the canton with the correct colours (and equal-width cross arms). It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1928.note: The drawing is the Wikimedia Commons file 'Flag of South Africa (1928–1994, bright colors).svg' (Public domain), with scripts, text and external links removed so it embeds in the page; its shapes and colours are the file's own.

era-1994.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The current flag has a green Y (pall) running from the two hoist corners to the middle and on to the fly edge, edged in white, with a red band above and a blue band below, and a black triangle at the hoist edged in gold. Ours has the red and blue bands but the horizontal part of the Y across the fly is white (not green) and nearly empty, and the arms and triangle are built from overlapping wedges, so the green arms stop at the centre and the white/green/gold edging is wrong. fixSvg redraws the flag from the Commons geometry. era-1392.note: A text card on a dashed frame reading NO NATIONAL FLAG YET; it draws no flag, so there is nothing to compare. Commons has a Joseon royal standard (File:Flag_of_the_king_of_Joseon.svg) for the 1392-1907 period that the card does not show; for Goryeo and Silla no flag file was found in the Wikipedia article image lists searched.

era-1883.note: The drawing is the Wikimedia Commons file 'Flag of Korea (1882–1910).svg' (Public domain), with scripts, text and external links removed so it embeds in the page; its shapes and colours are the file's own.

era-1897.note: The drawing is the Wikimedia Commons file 'Flag of Korea (1899).svg' (Public domain), with scripts, text and external links removed so it embeds in the page; its shapes and colours are the file's own.

era-1910.note: Red disc on white, disc diameter three fifths of the height, same as the Japanese flag the caption names (the Hinomaru). The ground is a warm off-white used across the atlas.

era-1945.note: The drawing is the Wikimedia Commons file 'Flag of South Korea (1945–1948).svg' (Public domain), with scripts, text and external links removed so it embeds in the page; its shapes and colours are the file's own.

era-1948.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: White field, four trigram groups and a red-and-blue taegeuk are the right ingredients, but the drawing is wrong in ways a viewer would see: the taegeuk is turned about 90 degrees (red on the left, blue on the right, no small lobes) where the reference has red on top and blue below on a tilted S; the trigrams are horizontal bars in the four corners where the reference tilts them across the diagonals; and the patterns are wrong: top-right (solid/broken/solid) and bottom-left (broken/solid/broken) are swapped, and the bottom-right has a solid line where all three should be broken. era-918.note: A text card on a dashed frame reading NO NATIONAL FLAG YET; it draws no flag, so there is nothing to compare. No Goryeo or Silla flag file was found in the Wikipedia flag-article image lists or by Commons file-name search.

era-1899.note: Union Flag layout and colours match the British flag in the Commons governor-general flag (which adds a central badge). era-1956.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The atlas draws a green field with a white disc and black star. era-2011.note: Black, red, green bands with white fimbriation between them, a blue triangle at the hoist and a gold five-pointed star; layout and colours match. The atlas green band is taller (about 38% of the height) than the black and red (25% each) while the Commons bands are equal thirds.

era-1230.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Reference is the quartered Castile-Leon banner: gold castle on red in quarters 1 and 4, purple crowned lion on white in quarters 2 and 3. era-1479.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Reference (Catholic Monarchs pennant 1475-92) is quartered: Castile-Leon counterquartered (castles on red, lions on white) in two diagonal quarters and Aragon-Sicily (yellow with red stripes) in the other two. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1516.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Reference is a white field with a continuous red ragged saltire (crossed knotty branches) running corner to corner. Ours has four separate round-capped bars that stop short of the centre, leaving a gap so it reads as two chevrons ">  <", not a saltire; no knots. Colours match. fixSvg draws a continuous saltire with knot stubs; not viewed after drawing. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1716.note: Redrawn: White flag with the crowned royal arms, as the Commons Spanish flag of 1701-1785 (the arms are simplified to four quarters). Earlier drawing differed from the reference.

era-1814.note: Red-yellow-red 1:2:1 with an emblem on the yellow band toward the hoist matches the reference (used 1785-1873). The reference emblem is a crowned oval (castle / lion); ours is a red rectangle with a gold crown bar. Detail omitted only.

era-1873.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Red-yellow-red 1:2:1 is right, but the First Republic reference (Commons file for 1873-74) carries an uncrowned oval shield on the yellow band at the hoist side (castle on red half, lion on white half); ours is a plain bicolour as the caption says, so the drawing and its caption leave out the emblem the reference shows. fixSvg adds a simplified oval shield; not viewed after drawing. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1874.note: Red-yellow-red 1:2:1 with a small emblem on the yellow band at the hoist side is right. Reference viewed as an image.

era-1931.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Wrong colours and order: reference is red / yellow / purple (#630b57) horizontal equal thirds with mural-crowned arms at the centre; ours is purple on top and red at the bottom (order reversed) and the arms are three plain maroon rectangles. fixSvg gives the correct order with simplified arms; not viewed after drawing. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1975.note: Red-yellow-red 1:2:1 with the arms set toward the hoist matches Flag_of_Spain.svg. The arms are reduced to a plain red rectangle with a gold crown bar and two crenels: no quartered shield, no flanking Pillars of Hercules, no ribbon. Reference viewed as an image.

era-1535.note: White field with a red diagonal saltire, as the Cross of Burgundy reference, but with straight bars instead of knotted ragged branches, and a faint gold tint block in the upper hoist that is not on the reference.

era-1808.note: Emblem redrawn by hand on 2026-10-25 and compared by eye with the reference: same layout and colours, emblem simplified (shape and detail reduced).

era-1505.note: White field with the red cross of the Order of Christ with a white inner cross, as in the reference banner. era-1658.note: Red, white, blue horizontal triband with the VOC monogram on the white stripe, as in the reference. The monogram is plain text rather than the interlaced black VOC lettering, and the lower stripe is a dark teal (hue near cyan) where the reference is a clear blue.

era-993.note: No Chola flag for Ceylon found: the Commons images on the Chola dynasty page are coins (a seated tiger) and temples, not flags. The drawing (a tiger on gold) rests on the tiger emblem only.

era-1070.note: No Polonnaruwa-period flag found: Commons files on Kingdom of Polonnaruwa, Flag of Sri Lanka and Kingdom of Anuradhapura pages show none; the drawing is the generic gold lion on maroon reconstruction. The emblem was redrawn by hand on 2026-10-25.

era-377bce.note: Caption says informed reconstruction. The emblem was redrawn by hand on 2026-10-25.

era-1821.note: Red field with a white crescent and a star in the centre. The Commons Muhammad Ali flag is red with the crescent left of centre and a cluster of small stars to its right. No source says the flag was flown in Sudan; ours is an inference from the Egyptian flag.

era-1885.note: A black field with the Latin placeholder words 'ARABIC INSCRIPTION'; the Commons Mahdi movement flag is red with a blue-framed block of four lines of Arabic lettering, and Wikipedia says the state had no uniform flag. Black plus label is a stand-in, not the drawn flag.

era-1899.note: Redrawn: Egyptian flag (green, white crescent and two stars) beside the Union Flag, as the Commons Anglo-Egyptian Sudan flag. Earlier drawing differed from the reference.

era-1956.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Blue-yellow-green stripes in the reference; ours has a cream middle stripe instead of yellow and a small gold crescent in the centre that the flag does not have. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1970.note: Red, white and black horizontal stripes with a green triangle at the hoist reaching about 37% of the width: matches the reference.

era-1667.note: Red, white, blue horizontal tricolour in the same order as the Dutch flag. Wikipedia (evidence row) supports the tricolour for the colony from 1815; the Commons Dutch Guiana colony flag is a separate arms flag that the sources say was not used.

era-1954.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The atlas draws a red oval with five round dots. The Commons 1959-1975 flag has a black ellipse linking five stars (black, brown, yellow, red, white with a dark outline, in the same order as the dots) and the ellipse is larger. Both sources in the evidence row give a black ellipse. The fix draws a black ellipse and stars. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1975.note: Green, white, red (double width), white, green horizontal bands with a gold five-pointed star on the red band, same proportions as the reference (the atlas star is smaller).

era-1397.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Yellow field with a red upright cross matches the Commons Kalmar Union flag (itself a recreation of the red cross on yellow in the 1430 letters). The atlas adds three white discs in the cross quarters that neither the file nor the sources show. The fix removes them. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1523.note: Blue field with a yellow Nordic cross offset toward the hoist, as in the Commons 1562-1650 flag (which is swallow-tailed; style).

era-1814.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The Swedish cross flag with a canton mark is the right idea, but the atlas mark is a red box with a white top band and a blue bottom band. The Commons 1844-1905 ensign has a canton in the upper hoist square: a red field with a white-edged blue vertical bar, and blue triangles with a yellow bar at either side (the combined Norwegian and Swedish colours). The 1815-1844 ensign (Commons) has instead a red canton with a white saltire. The fix shows the 1844-1905 mark. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1905.note: Blue field with a yellow Nordic cross offset toward the hoist, same layout. The atlas blue is darker than today's light blue (the shade was lightened in 1906).

era-995.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The atlas draws three gold five-pointed stars on blue. The Commons Tre Kronor flag and the Three Crowns arms are three gold crowns, two over one, on blue. Stars are not crowns. These are arms rather than a documented flag of the period. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1291.note: Caption says reconstructed. The earliest attested uses are white strips on clothing (Laupen 1339) and the red triangular banner with a long white cross at Arbedo 1422 (Ch-1422a.png); the drawing shows a rectangular red flag with a short thick cross, a later-style stand-in.

era-1648.note: Red field with a white cross matches the Confederate flag in design. The historical cross is thin with arms reaching close to the edges (as in Early_Swiss_cross.svg), while the drawing uses the short, thick modern-style cross.

era-1798.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Helvetic Republic flag is a HORIZONTAL tricolour, green over red over yellow (FOTW: green-red-yellow horizontally). The drawing has the same colours as vertical stripes. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1803.note: No reference found: the Commons file lists for Flag of Switzerland and its history carry nothing for 1803-1815, and FOTW (per the evidence) says the Confederation used no federal flag. The drawing is the red field with white cross under a faint blue wash, which is not any attested flag.

era-1815.note: Red field with a white cross, as the 1815 Bachmann battalion flag and the modern cross; the 1815 cross arms were longer and thinner than drawn.

era-1848.note: Red field with a centred white cross matches. The modern flag is square and the cross arms are a little longer relative to their width than in the drawing (3:2 field, stubbier cross); design and colours are the same.

era-1174.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The atlas draws a near-black field with a gold ring. The Commons drawing of Saladin's flag (the only Zengid/Ayyubid banner Wikipedia describes) is yellow with a red eagle. Colour and emblem both differ. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1260.note: Looked at the Commons files on the Mamluk, Ayyubid and Zengid articles: only the flag of Saladin (yellow with a red eagle) turned up, which is the Ayyubid banner, and no Mamluk banner. Sources describe yellow sultanic banners and personal blazons, and Damascus as yellow with a white crescent in the Book of All Kingdoms. The atlas draws a brown-gold field with a dark eagle-like emblem; the field colour is closer to the sources than the emblem, which no source supports.

era-1517.note: Redrawn: Ottoman red banner with a single dark crescent (no star), as on the Commons c.1490-1701 flag. Earlier drawing differed from the reference.

era-1920.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The atlas draws a plain vertical blue-white-red French tricolour (with a stray pale rectangle). The Commons file for the mandate-era Syrian flag is green-white-green horizontal bands with a French tricolour canton covering about half the width and the top two-fifths. The tricolour appears only as the canton. Other mandate-period flags (1920 blue crescent flag) are not what is drawn either. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1946.note: Green, white, black bands with three red five-pointed stars in the white band, as in the reference (stars smaller here).

era-1958.note: Red, white, black bands with two green five-pointed stars: same design as the UAR flag file (stars smaller here).

era-1972.note: Red-white-black tricolour with a gold hawk at the centre, as in the Commons file. The hawk is a hand-drawn heraldic bird with a plain shield, not the Hawk of Quraish with its scroll and detail; the file itself is 66 KB and too heavy to embed.

era-1963.note: The drawing is the Wikimedia Commons file 'Flag of Syria (1963–1972).svg' (Public domain), with scripts, text and external links removed so it embeds in the page; its shapes and colours are the file's own.

era-1961.note: The drawing (green-white-black, three red stars) matches the restored independence flag, but that flag was replaced in 1963 by a red-white-black flag with three green stars (Flag_of_Syria_(1963–1972).svg) and in 1972 by the Federation of Arab Republics flag with a hawk. The page gives this era as 1961-1980, so for 1963-1980 the picture shows a flag that was no longer in use. The caption now says which period the drawing fits. (The 1963-72 and 1972-80 flags now have their own cards.)

era-1980.note: Red, white, black bands with two green five-pointed stars in the white band, same as the reference (stars smaller here).

era-2024.note: Green, white, black horizontal bands with three red five-pointed stars in the white band, as in the reference; the atlas stars are smaller and closer together (style).

era-636.note: Plain white field. Wikipedia (Umayyad Caliphate) says the Umayyad banners were white; no Commons drawing exists, so this rests on that sentence alone. The page treats it as a colour, not a design.

era-750.note: Plain black field, as in the Abbasid banner file; the gold inner border is decoration. It shows the dynasty's banner, which the page already says is not a flag of Syria.

era-1624.note: Red-white-blue horizontal tricolour: the Commons Dutch East India Company flag (the Dutch Formosa infobox flag) without its white VOC monogram. The caption calls it the Prince's Flag, which is orange-white-blue (Commons Prinsenvlag.svg); the evidence row notes that village leaders were given a Prince's Flag but that the flag over Fort Zeelandia may have been the VOC's, so the picture is acceptable as the VOC flag and the caption is what misnames it.

era-1661.note: Ours is a dark red placard reading NO NATIONAL FLAG YET, not a flag. Wikipedia's Tungning article lists a Ming Cheng flag, drawn on Commons as a white flag with a dark crimson device and black characters (a 1661-dated modern drawing, no source stated in its description). The evidence row found no description of the flag in any text read, so the placard and the Commons picture disagree and neither is confirmed.

era-1895.note: White flag with a centred red disc, the same design as the Commons 1870 Japanese merchant flag that Wikipedia shows for Japanese Taiwan. The evidence row notes that the 1895 Republic of Formosa used a yellow tiger flag (Simplified_Yellow_Tiger_Flag.svg) and that FOTW lists separate Government-General flags; the page's choice rests on the infobox image.

era-1945.note: Red field with a blue canton and a white twelve-rayed sun, as in the Commons flag. Ours draws the rays as twelve thin straight bars and the sun's ring as a plain white-stroked circle, where the reference rays are tapered triangles around a white disc and blue ring; the canton is about 43% x 54% of the field where the reference canton is half the width and half the height.

era-1949.note: Red field with a blue canton and a white twelve-rayed sun, as in the Commons flag. Ours draws the rays as twelve thin straight bars and the sun's ring as a plain white-stroked circle, where the reference rays are tapered triangles around a white disc and blue ring; the canton is about 43% x 54% of the field where the reference canton is half the width and half the height.

era-1683.note: Emblem redrawn by hand on 2026-10-25 and compared by eye with the reference: same layout and colours, emblem simplified (shape and detail reduced).

era-1220.note: Dark field with a brown diamond outline, an invented stand-in for a period with no documented banner (the caption says none is documented). No reference image exists; checked the Chagatai Khanate evidence, nothing describes a banner.

era-1370.note: Reconstruction: blue field with three gold rings. Wikipedia says there is little certainty about the real flag (red banners possibly with a crescent, black or golden dragon banners reported); the three-ring sign of Timur is documented on coins and seals, not as a flag, and the blue field is unsupported. Commons has no Timurid flag file of the period to compare (checked the Timurid Empire article file list).

era-1500.note: Green field with a crescent matches the core of the Emirate of Bukhara flag; the reference also has an orange border, stars and a hand/inscription, and the sources disagree on the exact design. The caption presents it as a plain green field with crescent, and the khanate period before 1785 has no known flag.

era-1920.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: FOTW and Commons give the Bukharan PSR flag of 1921 as green over red with a gold crescent and star (red upper stripe from October 1923); the Tajik ASSR flag of 1929 was red with arms at upper left. The drawing is plain red with a gold L-shaped glyph, matching neither. Fix: the 1921-23 green-over-red flag with crescent and star (lettering omitted). It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1929.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The 1953-91 Tajik SSR flag is Soviet red with a white and a green stripe near the bottom and a gold hammer, sickle and star in the canton. The drawing has a gold stripe instead of white and green (the caption itself flags this) and an L-shaped gold glyph instead of hammer and sickle with a star. The 1929-31 flag was plain red with arms upper left (Flag_of_the_Tajik_Autonomous_Soviet_Socialist_Republic_(1929–1931).svg). Fix draws the 1953-91 design with a simplified hammer, sickle and star. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1991.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Red-white-green with a gold crown and an arc of stars is the right design, but the drawing has five stars (the flag has seven), a crude crown, and a white stripe about 2.3 times a coloured one where the reference is about 1.5 times (2:3:2-ish). Fix: 2:3:2 stripes, gold crown, seven-star arc. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-819.note: Black field is the Abbasid dynastic colour per Wikipedia (Black Standard); no source gives a Samanid flag. The drawing also adds a gold border and a gold Arabic letter sin that no source supports.

era-819-1.note: Plain off-white field with a thin border as a stand-in for the Umayyad white banner mentioned by Wikipedia (Black Standard); nothing ties it to Transoxiana and there is no Commons image of a white Umayyad flag to compare.

era-1921.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Reference (a Commons reconstruction of the 1921-26 flag): a red field with a blue circular emblem containing yellow figures at the centre. The sources (evidence row) give plain red for 1921 and red flags with arms from 1926 (Flag_of_the_Tuvan_People's_Republic_(1926-1930).svg is red with a blue-and-yellow arms disc). Ours is a blue field with a gold canton reading TAR, matching only a doubted 1918-21 report. The replacement is a red field with a simplified blue-and-yellow disc. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1943.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Reference (Commons drawing of the last Tuvan People's Republic flag): a plain red field with gold Cyrillic initials ТАР in the upper hoist corner. Ours has a blue canton with a gold cross-and-sun device on red, which the evidence row says neither source describes. The replacement draws the red flag with the gold initials. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1944.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Ours is a white / blue / red horizontal tricolour. The sources (evidence row) say local flags were abolished in 1944 and the RSFSR flag (red field) was the flag, with the 1992 Tuvan flag (Flag_of_Tuva.svg, a blue field with a yellow-white triangle at the hoist) as the later one. The tricolour is the Russian flag and is documented for neither. The replacement is a simplified RSFSR red flag with its gold lettering; the hammer and sickle are omitted. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1700.note: Plain red field matches the plain red Zanzibar flags on Commons. The card overlays two lines of text (ZANZIBAR SULTANATE, COASTAL & ISLAND INFLUENCE), which are not part of any flag, and the evidence row says the two publishers disagree on whether plain red lasted to 1885.

era-1885.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The caption describes a black field with a black-white-red canton and calls it schematic; the card is a black field with a red canton crossed by white and black diagonals, which is not a canton of those colours. Wikipedia and FOTW (evidence row) both describe a horizontal black / white / red tricolour with the imperial eagle in a white disc, as in the Commons reference. The replacement draws that tricolour with a simplified eagle. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1919.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The 1961 Tanganyika flag (the only one the card draws) has a black band 29 percent of the height edged in gold (the gold band is 42 percent of the height in the SVG, which has 20 and 14 of 48 units).
