As the evidence row says, the flag from 1923 to 1961 was a British Red Ensign with the territory emblem (Flag_of_Tanganyika_(1923–1961).svg) and is not shown. The replacement redraws the 1961 flag with the right widths. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1964.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Reference: green triangle at the top left (hoist), blue triangle at the bottom right, and the black band with yellow edges running from the bottom-left corner to the top-right corner. Ours is mirrored: green bottom-left, blue top-right, with the band running from top-left to bottom-right, which is a different flag. The replacement uses the reference orientation. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1238.note: A plain red field. Wikipedia and FOTW (evidence row) give a plain red flag from about 1680 to 1782; no Commons image of that flag was found, so the match is to the sources' description (the red ground of the Commons Siamese flag is the same colour), not a drawing.

era-1917.note: Red - white - blue - white - red horizontal stripes match the Trirang. The blue stripe is a bit deeper than the reference (40 percent of the height against one third) and the white stripes a little thinner; proportion only.

era-1932.note: Red - white - blue - white - red horizontal stripes match the Trirang. The blue stripe is a bit deeper than the reference (40 percent of the height against one third) and the white stripes a little thinner; proportion only.

era-1782.note: Emblem redrawn by hand on 2026-10-25 and compared by eye with the reference: same layout and colours, emblem simplified (shape and detail reduced).

era-1702.note: Green hoist and red fly with a gold emblem is the Portuguese flag of 1910-75, but the green is half the width (the flag has 2/5 green, 3/5 red) and the armillary sphere with shield is reduced to a gold diamond with a navy disc. Earlier Portuguese flags (1702-07, 1830-1910) are not shown, per the evidence.

era-1975.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The caption says the Indonesian flag, a red band over a white band. The drawing is red-white-blue horizontal bands with a gold star, which is not any Indonesian flag (neither source describes it). Fix: red over white. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1999.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The caption says the United Nations flag, which is light blue with a white emblem of the world map in olive branches. The drawing is a cream card with a navy border and the lettering UN and UNTAET, a placeholder in other colours. Fix: light blue field with a simplified white emblem. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-2002.note: Red field, yellow triangle from the hoist reaching about half the width, shorter black triangle in front, white star in the black triangle: the same design and order as the reference.

era-1884.note: Horizontal black, white, red stripes, the German imperial flag as in the Commons 1867-1918 file. The evidence row notes this was not the only flag in use in Togoland (naval ensign, service flags) and that a colonial badge flag proposed in 1914 was never introduced; the drawing shows none.

era-1960.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The reference has five equal horizontal stripes (green, yellow, green, yellow, green) with a red canton three stripes high holding a white star. Ours has the canton and star but draws eight thin stripes ending in a yellow stripe at the bottom, so the stripe count and the first and last colours are wrong. Fix: five stripes. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1845.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The Tongan flag (Commons, 2:1) is a red field with a white canton set flush in the upper hoist corner (about 42 percent of the length and half the height), and a red couped cross floating in the middle of the canton with white all round it. Ours has the canton inset from the edges by a red margin and the cross arms run right out to the canton edges, cutting it into four white blocks. Replacement follows the reference layout. The span also starts well before the 1875 constitution; the earlier Commons flags (1862-66: white with a red cross, like the Red Cross) differ, so the replacement fits only the post-1875 part. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1900.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The Tongan flag (Commons, 2:1) is a red field with a white canton set flush in the upper hoist corner (about 42 percent of the length and half the height), and a red couped cross floating in the middle of the canton with white all round it. Ours has the canton inset from the edges by a red margin and the cross arms run right out to the canton edges, cutting it into four white blocks. Replacement follows the reference layout. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1970.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The Tongan flag (Commons, 2:1) is a red field with a white canton set flush in the upper hoist corner (about 42 percent of the length and half the height), and a red couped cross floating in the middle of the canton with white all round it. Ours has the canton inset from the edges by a red margin and the cross arms run right out to the canton edges, cutting it into four white blocks. Replacement follows the reference layout. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1574.note: Redrawn: Blue, red, green, red, blue horizontal bands, as on the Commons Tunisian flag of the period before 1831 (its rounded pennant edge is left out). Earlier drawing differed from the reference.

era-1831.note: Same red flag with white disc, crescent and star as the Commons file for 1831-1881.

era-1881.note: Same red flag with white disc, crescent and star as the Commons file for 1831-1959. Ours adds a thin translucent blue frame as the atlas's sign of French protectorate; it is not part of the flag.

era-1956.note: Red field, white disc, red crescent and red five-pointed star inside the disc, as in the reference. The crescent is a little heavier than the reference's.

era-1453.note: Red field with a single crescent and no star agrees with the Commons reconstructions (c. 1490-1701: one crescent; 1540s-1701: three crescents) but the reference crescents are gold/brown, not white, and larger. The reference starts about 1490, so 1453-1490 has no picture, and the evidence row says Wikipedia also shows green and plain red banners.

era-1793.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The red field and crescent are right, but the star is drawn as a small broken six-vertex fragment (about 20 by 30 units) instead of a five-pointed star, and the crescent is too small and too far left. In the reference the crescent has an outer radius of a little more than a quarter of the height and the star (radius about one eighth of the height) sits just right of it with one point toward the hoist. The reference here is the 1844-1922 Ottoman flag, which has a slightly larger crescent and star than the modern one. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1918.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The red field and crescent are right, but the star is drawn as a small broken six-vertex fragment (about 20 by 30 units) instead of a five-pointed star, and the crescent is too small and too far left. In the reference the crescent has an outer radius of a quarter of the height and the star (radius about one eighth of the height) sits just right of it with one point toward the hoist. The evidence row also says no source gives the flag the Ankara government used in 1919-23. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1923.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The red field and crescent are right, but the star is drawn as a small broken six-vertex fragment (about 20 by 30 units) instead of a five-pointed star, and the crescent is too small and too far left. In the reference the crescent has an outer radius of a quarter of the height and the star (radius about one eighth of the height) sits just right of it with one point toward the hoist. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-330.note: Gold cross on red with four small emblems in the quarters matches the Palaiologan banner in layout. The cross is drawn with thin lines where the reference has a broad cross, the four firesteel (beta-shaped) emblems are plain squares, and the red is a darker maroon. The caption already limits the design to the 13th-15th centuries.

era-1040.note: A dark field with a thin ring: a placeholder; no flag is documented for the Seljuk or Mongol period of Merv in the sources read and none exists among Commons files on the Wikipedia Turkmenistan pages.

era-1500.note: A gold diamond outline on dark ground: the caption already calls it a reconstructed tribal-emblem motif. The reference guls (tribal carpet motifs on today's flag) are octagonal medallions, so the diamond is not any of the five.

era-1881.note: White-blue-red horizontal tricolour matches the Russian flag from 1896; for 1881-96 the Commons file for the Russian state flag (Flag_of_Russia_(1858–1896).svg) is black-yellow-white, so the start of the span is not covered. No source says which flag flew over the Transcaspian Oblast.

era-1917.note: Plain red field matches the Commons Turkestan ASSR flags; both reference files carry a vertical column of lettering near the hoist, whereas ours has a gold L-shaped device in the canton. Our own evidence says no source describes this flag.

era-1924.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Red field with a canton emblem matches in broad terms, but the late Soviet-period flag has two turquoise stripes across the middle (about 33-47% and 52-67% of the height) and a gold star above a hammer and sickle in the canton; ours has one thin turquoise stripe near the bottom and a plain gold L-shape. Fix leaves out the hammer and sickle, and covers the 1953-91 design; earlier flags (1926 onward) differ again. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1991.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Green field, carpet stripe, crescent and stars are present, but the reference has the red carpet stripe inset from the hoist (about 12-30% of the width, ours flush with the hoist inside a cream border), five stars beside the crescent in the upper part (ours has three, mid-height) and a smaller crescent. Fix omits the olive branches under the stripe and simplifies the guls. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1892.note: Blue Ensign with the joint colony's arms in the fly in the reference; the drawing has the same cream-and-teal disc stand-in for the arms (and is identical to the 1975 card). Per the evidence, no flag is documented for 1892-1937.

era-1975.note: Dark blue ensign with a Union Flag canton and a badge in the fly, as the reference. The arms shield is a plain cream disc with a teal centre placed in the lower fly (the reference shield is nearer the vertical middle of the fly).

era-1978.note: Light blue field, Union Flag canton, nine gold stars scattered on the fly in the island layout; same design as the reference (the drawing's stars are larger and the Union Flag simplified).

era-1200.note: Red cross on white reaching all four edges, same as the St George's Cross; ours has slightly thicker arms (one quarter of the height against one fifth).

era-1603.note: Same design as the 1606 Union Flag in its English-pattern form: blue field, white saltire, white-edged red cross on top. (A Scottish-pattern 1606 flag also exists on Commons with the saltire on top.)

era-1707.note: Blue field, white saltire and white-edged red cross without the Irish red saltire, same as the Commons Great Britain flag of 1707-1800.

era-1801.note: Blue field with the white saltire, thin red saltire and white-edged red cross is the Union Flag layout and matches. The red diagonals are drawn centred inside the white ones; the real flag counterchanges them (offset to one side of each white diagonal), which gives the pinwheel look. Colours are muted.

era-1922.note: Blue field with the white saltire, thin red saltire and white-edged red cross is the Union Flag layout and matches. The red diagonals are drawn centred inside the white ones; the real flag counterchanges them (offset to one side of each white diagonal), which gives the pinwheel look. Colours are muted.

era-1654.note: Redrawn: Dark-red field with a white cross between a star, two crescents and a sun, as the Commons Zaporozhian Sich banner. Earlier drawing differed from the reference.

era-1795.note: White / blue / red horizontal tricolour matches the Russian flag reference. Whether this civil flag is the right one for a Ukrainian-lands era from 1795 is a text question; the imperial black-yellow-white flag of 1858-1896 is a different design.

era-1917.note: Blue over yellow horizontal bicolour matches the 1917-1921 Commons drawing. The evidence row notes the stripe order was reversed (yellow over blue) in 1918 and under the Hetmanate, a variation the card does not show.

era-1921.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Reference (1919-1929): plain red field with gold Cyrillic initials in the upper hoist; no hammer and sickle until 1937. Ours is red with a gold shield-and-star emblem, which appears in none of the Commons UkrSSR flags. The replacement shows the 1927-29 initials УСРР. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1941.note: Redrawn after the Commons Flag of Germany (1935–1945): red field, white disc, black swastika turned on its point.

era-1944.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Reference (1937-1949): red field with a small gold hammer and sickle above gold Cyrillic УРСР lettering in the upper hoist. Ours has a gold shield with a five-pointed star and no lettering or hammer and sickle. The evidence row already asks for a redraw. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1949.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Reference: red field with a light-blue stripe along the bottom (one third of the width), and a gold hammer and sickle beneath a gold-edged star in the upper hoist. Ours has the red/blue layout but the blue stripe is a quarter of the height, and the emblem is a gold shield with a star, not a hammer and sickle. The replacement fixes the stripe proportion and draws a hammer, sickle and star. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1991.note: Blue over yellow horizontal bicolour, equal halves, matches the reference (the reference uses a deeper blue than the card, which fits the sky-blue / darker-blue variants noted in the evidence).

era-1569.note: Emblem redrawn by hand on 2026-10-25 and compared by eye with the reference: same layout and colours, emblem simplified (shape and detail reduced).

era-1349.note: Emblem redrawn by hand on 2026-10-25 and compared by eye with the reference: same layout and colours, emblem simplified (shape and detail reduced).

era-1240.note: Looked for a drawn lion-on-blue flag of Galicia-Volhynia in the Wikipedia article images for Galicia-Volhynia and Kingdom of Ruthenia (only Belz arms and the modern flag of Ukraine appear) and in Commons search; none found. Ours is a gold lion silhouette on blue, which matches the described golden lion on azure only in colour scheme. The emblem was redrawn by hand on 2026-10-25.

era-1727.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Ours is a plain red field. Wikipedia's Flag of the UAE says the Qawasim had their own green, white and red banner before 1820, with an inscription on the white band (Sharjah's ruler quoted it on restoring the flag in 1975), and the Commons Qasimi standard shows green, white, red horizontal bands with script in the white. Fix: green, white, red bands (the inscription is left out). The caption itself calls the plain red an informed reconstruction. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1820.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Ours is a plain red field. Wikipedia's Flag of the UAE (and the evidence row) say the 1820 treaty had a white segment added to each emirate's flag, the "white pierced red" flag; the Sharjah and Ras al-Khaimah file shows red with a white border. Fix: red with a white border. (Abu Dhabi and Dubai were to fly plain red in war, and Fujairah kept plain red, so plain red was in use by some.) It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1971.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The reference has a red vertical bar at the hoist and three horizontal stripes, green on top, white in the middle, black at the bottom. Ours has the red bar and black bottom stripe but puts white on top and green in the middle. Fix: green, white, black from the top. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1607.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The reference British union flag of this period has a blue field, a white saltire and a red St George cross with white fringe, with no red saltire. The card adds a thin red diagonal on top of the white saltire, which is the St Patrick element added only in 1801, so it is the later Union Jack. It also does not show the Grand Union striped flag the caption mentions. The replacement removes the red diagonals. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1777.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Thirteen stripes starting red match. The star field should be thirteen stars in a ring (the Betsy Ross arrangement the caption names); the card has nine round dots in a diamond plus one stray star at the top left, ten in all. The replacement draws thirteen stars in a circle. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1795.note: Fifteen stripes starting red and fifteen dots in three rows match the 15-star, 15-stripe design; stars are drawn as round dots and the canton covers eight stripes as it should.

era-1818.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The reference 20-star flag (1818) has four rows of five stars (SVG source). The card shows 18 round dots, which is not a count any flag of 1818-1861 had. The replacement draws the 20-star flag that opens the era. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1861.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The reference 34-star flag (1861-63) has rows of 7, 7, 6, 7 and 7 stars (SVG source); the card draws 23 round dots and a narrower canton does not match the 7-stripe canton proportion of the others. The replacement draws the 34-star pattern; the 35-star flag of 1863-65 differs by one star. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1865.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The card covers the 36- to 45-star flags (reference 45-star flag: 8-7-8-7-8-7 staggered rows). The card draws 25 round dots in a regular grid, which matches no flag in the range. The replacement shows the 45-star flag that ends the range (1896-1908); note the 46-star flag of 1908-1912 is not on the page. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1912.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The reference has 48 stars in six rows of eight (checked in the SVG source: eight uses per row, six rows). The card has 33 round dots. The replacement draws 48 stars in a 6 x 8 grid. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1959.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The 49-star flag has seven rows of seven stars; the card has 21 round dots in rows, 28 stars short, and the dots are circles not stars. The replacement draws 49 stars in a 7 x 7 grid. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1960.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Layout is right (13 stripes starting red, canton over 7 stripes, 2/5 of the length) but the canton holds 20 round dots in a 5 x 4 grid, not 50 five-pointed stars in alternating rows of 6 and 5. The card is headlined as the 50-star flag, so the star count matters. The replacement draws 50 stars in nine staggered rows. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1680.note: White field with a red diagonal saltire (Cross of Burgundy), straight bars where the reference has knotted branches. The evidence row finds no source for this flag over the Banda Oriental; the earliest documented flag there is Artigas's 1814 flag (Flag_of_Artigas.svg).

era-1816.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The drawing is two vertical halves (teal and green) with a gold-and-teal disc at the centre line. The Commons Cisplatina flag is horizontal: green above, white in the middle, green below, with a small emblem in the centre (this agrees with the evidence row). The Portuguese and Brazilian flags in the caption are not drawn. fixSvg redraws the green-white-green flag. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1825.note: Light blue, white, crimson horizontal bands with the motto on the white band: same as the Thirty-Three Orientals and 1825-1828 references (grid match 0.91, difference only the hand-lettered motto).

era-1830.note: Nine horizontal stripes, white first and last, with a white canton over the top five and a golden sun: same layout as the reference. The sun is a disc with eight straight rays where the reference has a sixteen-ray alternately straight and wavy sun with a face, and the canton is a bit wider than square.

era-1220.note: Plain black field as in the Abbasid black banner reference. The drawing adds a thin brown frame line. No Samanid-specific flag was found.

era-1370.note: Caption says reconstructed. The Commons Timur banner is a red pennant with a finial, not a blue field with three gold rings; the evidence row notes the sources disagree on colour and the three-ring motif is tentative.

era-1500.note: Caption calls it representative. The Commons Bukhara emirate flag (early 20th century) is a teal field with an orange border, crescent and stars, and the Khanate of Khiva flag (Flag_of_the_Khanate_of_Khiva.svg) is black with a yellow crescent and star; a plain green field with a white crescent matches neither reference.

era-1865.note: White, blue, red horizontal tricolour, same as the Commons Russian flag dated 1896-1918. The reference is dated from 1896, the era starts in 1865; no source seen shows the flag used specifically in Turkestan.

era-1917.note: Plain red field with a small gold mark at the hoist, like the Turkestan ASSR flag (red with gold lettering at the hoist). The drawing reduces the lettering to an L-shaped mark. The Bukharan People's Soviet Republic flag (green over red with crescent and star) and the Khorezm flag (red with a green hoist bar) are different designs and are not shown.

era-1924.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Red field with a gold emblem at the hoist as in the reference, but the light-blue stripe is misplaced: the reference has a white-edged light-blue band across the middle (about 41% to 59% of the height, with a red area below), while the drawing has a thin blue stripe near the bottom (85%-91%). The emblem is an L-shaped stand-in rather than a hammer and sickle with star. The reference is the 1952-1991 flag, so 1924-1952 is not covered (earlier flags such as Flag_of_the_Uzbek_Soviet_Socialist_Republic_(1925–1927).svg were red with lettering). It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1991.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Stripes (light blue, white, green) with thin red fimbriations and a white crescent opening toward the fly in the upper hoist all match. The twelve stars are wrong: the reference has them in a right-aligned triangle of 3, 4 and 5 stars, the drawing has a loose block of three rows of three plus two above and one below. The drawing is 3:2 where the flag is 2:1. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1906.note: Caption says British and French flags side by side. The drawing is one rectangle split down the middle: a cropped Union Jack on the left half and a blue-white-red vertical tricolour on the right. The Commons references show the territory's British Blue Ensign with a badge (1906-1952 and 1952-1980) and the French tricolour as separate flags; no joint flag is drawn on Commons, so this composite is a device of the page.

era-1980.note: Red over green, black hoist triangle with gold edging and a black gold-edged band running to the fly, as in the reference. The emblem in the triangle is reduced to a broken gold ring with a small cross; the reference has a boar's tusk circle with two crossed namele fronds, and the gold Y-shaped fimbriation is drawn only approximately (the reference triangle is a little larger).

era-1825.note: Yellow hoist half and white fly half with a small emblem in the white matches in layout; the emblem (crossed keys under the tiara on the reference) is a small gold smudge.

era-1870.note: No reference found: Commons files for the Papal States end in 1870 (…(1825-1870).svg, with the keys and tiara) and the Vatican City flags start in 1929, with nothing for 1870-1929, and no source read describes a ceremonial papal flag in that period. The drawing shows a plain yellow/white bicolour without keys or tiara, unlike the flags of the periods on either side.

era-1929.note: Yellow hoist half and white fly half with the tiara over crossed gold and silver keys matches. The tiara and keys are much simplified (the tiara is two bands and a ball, the keys plain bars with round bows).

era-756.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The documented pre-1808 flag is a VERTICAL bicolour, red at the hoist and yellow at the fly (Holy See Press Office: red and amaranth/yellow before 1808). The drawing is a horizontal bicolour, gold over red. Nothing is documented for 756 up to the last centuries before 1808, so the fix shows the pre-1808 flag only. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1777.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The caption says a Cross of Burgundy banner, shown schematically. Ours is a cream field with a brown frame, a red band across the top and a gold disc, which has no cross or saltire at all (Commons Cross of Burgundy flag: white with a red ragged saltire). fixSvg draws a white field with a red saltire (straight bars). The evidence row notes the Burgundy cross is inferred for Venezuela, and that the naval ensign became red-yellow-red in 1785. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1810.note: Plain yellow-blue-red tricolour, Miranda's 1806 flag as the caption says. The Commons flag of the First Republic (1811-12) is the same tricolour with a canton at the hoist carrying the arms, which ours omits.

era-1819.note: Yellow-blue-red horizontal tricolour as in the Commons Gran Colombia flags. The references carry the arms (in the canton in 1819-20, at the centre later); ours puts a plain white five-pointed star at the centre, which the evidence row says is unconfirmed.

era-1830.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Yellow-blue-red horizontal tricolour as in the reference. The stars are wrong: ours has five round white dots in a shallow arc, whereas the current flag (the 2006 design, which Wikipedia dates) has eight five-pointed white stars in a tilted arc across the blue band, and the 1930-2006 flag had seven; no era of the flag had five round dots. Earlier forms in this era (1830-36, 1836-59, 1859-63, 1863-1905 and so on) also differ and are on Commons. fixSvg draws the current eight-star flag, with the star positions measured from the Commons image. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1802.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Yellow field with a red band is the right idea, but the Commons first Nguyen flag and the Long tinh flag both have a red horizontal band across the middle half of the flag (from edge to edge); ours is a short vertical red bar in the centre. Wikipedia's Long tinh article also puts its design in the 1920s, so the sources conflict on date. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1887.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Ours is a horizontal red-white-blue flag (the Dutch pattern); the French flag flown over Indochina is the vertical blue-white-red tricolour with blue at the hoist. The sources also mention a yellow protectorate flag with a tricolour canton (Flag_of_Colonial_Annam.svg). It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1976.note: Red field with a large five-pointed gold star centred: matches the reference in layout and star size.

era-938-1.note: Yellow field with the Chinese character for dragon: a placeholder; our own evidence says no source mentions a Chinese imperial dragon standard for 111 BCE-938, and Wikipedia shows no flag for the period.

era-1283.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The caption says England's St George's Cross, but the atlas draws the Union Flag (blue field, diagonals), a flag of 1801 and later. The Commons flag of England is a plain red cross on white. The fix draws that. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1536.note: Union Flag (the 1801 design) drawn for the whole of 1536-1959. The caption says England's flag, then Great Britain's, then the UK's; only the last stage is drawn, and the red diagonals are centred rather than offset as in the real flag. Wales has no part of the Union Flag, as the Commons note on the file shows.

era-1959.note: The drawing is the Wikimedia Commons file 'Flag of Wales.svg' (Public domain), with scripts, text and external links removed so it embeds in the page; its shapes and colours are the file's own.
era-1959.artist: Unknown  Vector graphics by Tobias Jakobs

era-850.note: Reconstruction, as the caption says. The Commons arms of Llywelyn (the Gwynedd arms) are quartered gold and red with four lions; the atlas stands in four brown squares for the lions on a cream field and adds a green dragon, whereas the Welsh dragon in every Commons file is red. The evidence row says no banner is documented for this span. The emblem was redrawn by hand on 2026-10-25.

era-1839.note: Plain red rectangle; the evidence row says it is the page's own placeholder and the caption says reconstructed. The only documented Aden flag found, the 1937-63 Commons drawing, is a Blue Ensign with a badge, so the red field is not supported for Aden either.

era-1918.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Reference: red field with a curved white scimitar across the centre and five white stars, one near each corner and one above the blade. Ours has a straight white line with an arrowhead (a sabre reduced to a stroke) and the five stars in an arc along the top. The evidence row says FOTW describes a red flag with a white sabre and five stars (1927), consistent with the reference. The replacement puts the stars at the corners and top centre and curves the blade. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1990.note: Red / white / black horizontal bands in equal thirds match the reference.

era-897.note: Plain green rectangle labelled reconstructed in the caption. No source read describes any flag for 897-1839 (evidence row); there is no reference image.

era-1891.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The Commons company flag, matching Wikipedia and FOTW in the evidence row, is a full Union Flag with the company badge in the centre. Ours is a Blue Ensign (Union canton on blue) with a gold disc in the fly, a layout the evidence row says probably never flew. Replacement is a Union Flag with a gold badge in the centre (badge simplified). It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1924.note: Blue Ensign layout (Union canton, badge in the fly) matches the Northern Rhodesia flag, but the badge, which is the territory arms on Commons, is a white disc with a black square. Per the evidence row, the Blue Ensign with a badge dates only from 1939; the Union Flag was used 1924-39, so the early part of the span is not shown.

era-1953.note: Blue Ensign layout matches: blue field, Union Flag in the upper-hoist quarter, badge in the fly. The Union Flag has centred red diagonals, and the Federation's arms in the fly are an empty white disc.

era-1964.note: The drawing is the Wikimedia Commons file 'Flag of Zambia.svg' (Public domain), with scripts, text and external links removed so it embeds in the page; its shapes and colours are the file's own.

era-1890.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: FOTW and Commons show a full Union Flag with the Company badge (lion and elephant tusk) in a disc at the centre. The drawing is a Blue Ensign (blue field with a Union Flag canton) with a plain yellow disc in the fly. Fix: full Union Flag with a central badge disc. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1923.note: Dark blue ensign with a Union Flag canton as in the reference. The badge in the fly should be the shield of the colony's arms (Wikipedia, Commons); the drawing uses a plain white disc (one of FOTW's 1923-53 variants). The Union Flag canton is drawn schematically.

era-1965.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: The 1968-79 Rhodesian flag is three vertical stripes, green-white-green, with the coat of arms on the white stripe. The drawing is three horizontal stripes (white, green, white) with a small black leaf shape, so the orientation and the colour of the outer stripes are wrong. It also depicts the 1968 flag; from 1965 to 1968 the flag was the light blue ensign (Flag_of_Rhodesia_(1964–1968).svg). Fix: vertical green-white-green with a simplified shield. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1979.note: Not a flag: a CEASEFIRE TRANSITION text card. The period saw the Union Flag de facto and the Zimbabwe Rhodesia flag (Flag_of_Zimbabwe_Rhodesia_(1979).svg exists on Commons) but neither is drawn.

era-1980.note: Seven horizontal stripes green-yellow-red-black-red-yellow-green and a white hoist triangle with a red star match the reference. The Zimbabwe Bird is reduced to a yellow squiggle, the triangle is a little larger, and the black edge of the triangle is omitted.

era-1632.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Caption says Blue Ensign with the colonial badge. References (1956-1962 Blue Ensign with a white disc holding a shield of hills, building, agave and sea; 1962-1967 same without disc) show a navy field, Union Jack canton and a shield badge. The drawing is not a Blue Ensign: the field is blue with cream and red wedge shapes at the corners and an offset cross, and the badge is a yellow ellipse with green tufts (a pineapple, which the evidence says is wrong for the badge). The earlier 1632-1956 period (Leeward Islands ensigns) is not what either reference shows; the fix draws the 1956-1962 ensign as the representative late-colonial flag. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1967.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Same design as the current flag (adopted 27 Feb 1967 and kept at independence), so the current-flag file is the reference. The drawing is the same garbled black V, sun of two yellow triangles, small blue chevron and cream slivers as the 1981 card; the half-disc sun, full-width V and white point are missing. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1981.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Reference: red field with a downward-pointing red-bordered V enclosing, top to bottom, a black band with a rising yellow sun (half disc and about nine rays), a blue band and a white point. The drawing has the right colours but the layout is garbled: a black V with a sun made of two flat yellow triangles, a small blue chevron and two cream slivers, no half-disc sun and no white point, and the V does not span the full flag width. It does not read as the Antigua flag. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1783.note: Red field with a plain straight-edged white hoist band (about 17% of the length) matches the Commons 1820-1932 flag. The era runs to 1971, so the serrated forms (Commons Flag_of_Bahrain_(1932–1972), about 28 fine points) and the pre-1820 plain red are not shown; the picture is the 1820-1932 phase only.

era-1971.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Same layout, but the 1972-2002 reference has eight white serration points; the drawing has 4 notches (4 teeth), half as many. Wikipedia (28 points, then eight in 1972, five in 2002) and FOTW agree on eight. Fix draws eight teeth. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-2002.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Red field with a white serrated hoist band is right, but the serration is drawn with only 2 notches (3 white points) where the current flag has five white triangles pointing right across the full height. Band base and tip positions are also off (reference base 25%, tips 39% of the length). Fix draws five teeth. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1564.note: Red diagonal cross (saltire) on white, as the Cross of Burgundy reference. Detail left out: the reference arms are knotted and ragged (raguly, with lopped branch stubs); ours are plain straight bars.

era-1821.note: Reference (First Mexican Empire flag): green, white, red vertical bands with a crowned brown eagle on a nopal cactus over water in the white band. Bands match; ours replaces the eagle with a plain brown disc, which is a shapeless stand-in for the emblem. Separately, the Commons Costa Rica flag for September 1821 - June 1823 is light blue over yellow over light blue (Flag_of_Costa_Rica_(1821–1823).svg), matching FOTW, and no source read shows the Mexican flag flown over Costa Rica. Fix draws the crowned eagle on the cactus. (redrawn from the reference) The caption now says no source shows this flag flown in Costa Rica.

era-1823.note: Layout matches the references for the Federal Republic of Central America: equal blue, white, blue bands with a small round arms in the centre showing volcanoes under a rainbow. Ours draws the arms as five dark triangles in an ellipse with a red arc, without the ring of lettering, sun or cap of the reference; the blue is a deeper royal blue than the sky blue of the references.

era-1838.note: Blue, white, blue in equal thirds matches the Commons references for 1838-40 and 1842-48 (light blue, white, light blue) in stripe order. Detail left out: the references carry the round Estado Libre de Costa Rica seal (lower stripe in 1838-40, centre of the white stripe in 1842-48), and the 1840-42 flag was white-blue-white (Flag_of_Costa_Rica_(1840–1842).svg). Ours is also a deeper blue than the sky-blue references (same hue family).

era-1848.note: Blue, white, red (double width), white, blue bands in the 1:1:2:1:1 order of the reference civil flag. The state flag with arms (1906 onwards) is not drawn; the civil flag is correct for the era.

era-1515.note: Red diagonal saltire on a white field matches the Cross of Burgundy in colour and layout; the ragged (raguly) edges of the reference are drawn as smooth straight bars, as the caption says. Wikipedia (Flag of Cuba) dates the cross in Cuba 1521-1843 and gives the red-yellow-red Spanish flag (Commons Flag_of_Spain_(1785–1873,_1875–1931)) for 1843-1898, so the last 25 years of the era had a different flag.

era-1868.note: Wikipedia (Flag of Cuba): Lopez's Lone Star flag (same design as the national flag) was designated the national banner in April 1869; the drawing is the same design as the Commons flag. Not shown: the Cespedes Demajagua flag (Commons Cespedes_flag.svg, red square with star above a blue band) used at the start of the war in 1868.

era-1898.note: Thirteen red and white stripes starting and ending red, blue canton over seven stripes: matches the US flag Wikipedia (Military Government of Cuba) shows for 1898-1902. Detail left out: the stars are plain dots, and only 23 are drawn (rows of 5 and 4) where the 45-star flag has 6 rows of 8 and 7.

era-1902.note: Five stripes (blue, white, blue, white, blue), red hoist triangle reaching to the middle, white five-point star in the triangle: same design and star position as the reference. Colours are close in hue.

era-1008.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Reference (Sakartvelo_-_drosha.svg, reconstructed five-cross flag of the Kingdom of Georgia) and KingDavidtheBuilderFlag.svg (white with a red cross beside a dark panel) are white with red crosses; QueenTamarFlag.svg is a red-and-black quartered field. None is maroon with a gold cross. Ours is a maroon field with a gold cross. Fix: five-cross white flag. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1243.note: Brown field with a white ring: an invented stand-in. The caption already calls it a generic Ilkhanate-era representation. Wikipedia shows Georgian flags of this period as the white five-cross banner (1339 Dulcert and 1367 Pizzigano charts), so the stand-in does not look like anything documented; consider the five-cross drawing instead.

era-1490.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Every reconstructed reference for the kingdoms of this era is white-based: Kartli is a single red cross on white (Kartli_-_drosha_jvari.svg), Imereti plain white (Imereti_-_drosha.svg), Kakheti a white flag with a red fleur-de-lis. Ours is a maroon field with a gold cross; the colours are the reverse of the reference. Fix: single dark-red cross on white. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1801.note: Black over yellow over white in equal horizontal stripes, same as the reference black-yellow-white flag of the Russian Empire (hue match; yellow drawn as gold). Caveat on use: that flag was the Empire state flag only from 1858, with white-blue-red the sole national flag from 1896, so it covers part of 1801-1918, and no source read ties it to Georgia.

era-1918.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Reference: dark red field with a canton at the hoist of only TWO bands, black over white. Ours has three bands (black, white, black) and a small canton set in the top-left; the maroon is also pinker than the reference dark red. Fix: black-over-white canton on dark red. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1921.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Reference (Georgian SSR flag, the long-lived 1951-1990 design): red field, a broad light-blue stripe across the upper part, and a square light-blue canton with red sun rays and a red hammer-and-sickle and star. Ours: red field with a blue-white-blue stripe along the bottom edge and a gold cross-shaped blob at the hoist; the stripe position, the white edging and the gold emblem all differ and the emblem is not a hammer and sickle. Fix redraws the 1951-1990 design. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-2004.note: Five-Cross Flag: white field, large red St George cross, four small red crosses in the quarters; proportions of the central bars match (about 15% of the width). Detail left out: the four small crosses are plain Greek crosses, not the flared bolnur-katskhuri form, and the field is cream. The 1990-2004 wine-red flag now has its own card.

era-1991.note: The drawing is the Wikimedia Commons file 'Flag of Georgia (1990–2004).svg' (Public domain), with scripts, text and external links removed so it embeds in the page; its shapes and colours are the file's own.

era-1293.note: Nine horizontal stripes alternating red and white, red at top and bottom (five red, four white), as the reference.

era-1602.note: Same layout as the reference: Dutch tricolour with the VOC monogram on the white band. Detail left out: the reference monogram is a black interlocked ligature (large V with O and C), ours is the three letters V O C typed in blue serif text.

era-1800.note: Red, white, blue horizontal bands from the top, as the reference Dutch tricolour (Wikipedia: used as the Dutch East Indies flag 1800-1949).

era-1942.note: Red disc on white, disc centred and about 60% of the height as in the reference Flag of Imperial Japan (Wikipedia gives it as the occupation-period flag). White drawn cream; disc a slightly darker red.

era-1945.note: Same red-over-white bicolour as the reference; the flag was the same design from 1945.

era-1949.note: Red over white in two equal horizontal bands, as the reference.

era-1800.note: Fetched Wikipedia Flag of Zanzibar: the Muscat and Oman flag was a plain red flag from 1698, no new flag was adopted by the 1856 Zanzibar sultanate, and the red flag stayed in use under British protection (Commons Flag_of_Muscat.svg and Flag_of_Zanzibar_Under_British_Rule.svg are plain red). The drawing is a plain red field, matching; it is a brick red (hue ok) with two lines of cream caption text (ZANZIBAR SULTANATE / COASTAL INFLUENCE) overlaid, which a real flag would not carry. Whether this flag flew at Kenyan coast posts before 1888 is a text claim not checked here.

era-1895.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Reference (also 1921-1963 file without disc): navy Blue Ensign, Union Jack canton, red lion rampant on a white disc. The drawing has a dark teal-grey field (not ensign blue, clashing with the navy canton), a cream disc with a brown rectangle in place of the lion, and canton diagonals that overshoot the canton edges. Colour and emblem are wrong; the lion badge is the point of the card. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1963.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Stripe order (black, red, green), white fimbriation and colours match. The emblem is wrong: reference has a red Maasai shield (oval, white lens-shaped bars, black side lobes) over two crossed white spears; the drawing has a small cream-and-red pentagon with two crossed brown sticks drawn through it. A pentagon with brown sticks is not a recognisable Maasai shield and spears. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1707.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Same flaw as the 1953 drawing: three separate side-view elephants with a tiny flat gold parasol and gold pedestal blocks. The Commons Luang Phrabang 1707-1893 flag shows a red field with a front-facing three-headed elephant under a round parasol on a stepped pedestal, in white. Fix draws that. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1893.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Drawing is a horizontal red-white-blue tricolour (the Dutch order; the French tricolour is vertical blue-white-red) and has no Lao elements. The Commons 1893-1952 flag (and FOTW la-1893, fetched) is the red Luang Prabang elephant flag with a French tricolour in the canton. Fix draws that. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1953.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Red field with an elephant group under a parasol on a pedestal is the right idea, but the emblem is not the royal emblem: it shows three separate side-view elephants overlapping (only one has a visible head, trunk and eye), a small flat gold triangle for the parasol and gold step blocks for the pedestal. The reference is one three-headed elephant seen from the front, under a nine-tier white parasol on a five-tier pedestal, the whole emblem white on red. Fix draws a front-facing three-headed elephant with stepped parasol and pedestal. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1975.note: Red, blue, red stripes in 1:2:1 with a white disc about 80% of the blue band height, centred: same design as the reference.

era-1885.note: Red, yellow (double width), red horizontal bands, same as the Spanish flag of 1785-1873 that Wikipedia shows for the Spanish East Indies. Detail left out: the reference carries the crowned Castile-Leon arms on the yellow band near the hoist.

era-1899.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Reference (German imperial colonial flag, the infobox flag of German New Guinea, which governed the Carolines; OzOutback also describes black-white-red with the arms on a white disc): full-width horizontal black, white, red bands with the imperial eagle on a white disc in the centre. Ours is a white field with a black-white-red block along the fly edge (a canton on the wrong side and full height) and a black star in a circle instead of the eagle. It does not match the colonial flag, the German New Guinea Company flag (Service_flag_of_German_New_Guinea.svg: white, black-white-red canton at the hoist, black lion at the fly) or the 1914 proposal (Proposed_Flag_of_German_New_Guinea.svg: tricolour with a green shield). Fix draws the colonial flag with a simplified eagle on the disc. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1914.note: White field with a centred red disc about 60% of the height, same as the Flag of Japan that Wikipedia shows for the South Seas Mandate. Caveat: the unsigned OzOutback source gives the Japanese naval ensign (rising sun with rays) for 1914 and a separate mandate emblem flag from 1919; the plain Hinomaru drawn matches Wikipedia, not those.

era-1947.note: Thirteen red and white stripes with a blue canton two fifths of the width and seven stripes deep, as the US flag. Detail left out: the canton carries 20 small white dots in a 5x4 grid instead of 48 (to 1959) or 50 (from 1960) stars. The Trust Territory flag of 1962/65 onward (Flag_of_the_Trust_Territory_of_the_Pacific_Islands.svg: light blue, six white stars in a ring) is not drawn.

era-1986.note: Light blue field with four white five-pointed stars in a diamond (one top, bottom, left, right), as the reference. Blue slightly deeper than the reference light blue; hue matches.

era-1397.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Reference (probable Kalmar Union flag): yellow field with an offset red cross. Ours has that, but adds three white circles standing for crowns; no source and no reference shows crowns, and the circles are conspicuous. Fix: drop the crowns. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1523.note: Dannebrog: red field with an offset white Nordic cross, as the reference (Flag of Denmark, which Norway used 1536/37-1814 per Wikipedia). Brick red instead of bright red; hue matches.

era-1814.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Reference (1844-1899 national flag with the Sweden-Norway union mark): the cross flag with, in the upper hoist canton, a square mark made of two red and two blue triangles split by a yellow horizontal bar and a white-edged blue vertical bar. Ours has only a tiny rectangle of three horizontal bands (white, blue, red) and no yellow, no triangles; it does not read as the union mark. Also note the era starts with the 1814 Dannebrog-with-lion flag and the 1821-44 plain cross flag; the drawing matches only the 1844-99 flag. Fix draws the union mark in the canton. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1905.note: Same plain red flag with the white-bordered navy offset cross as the 1899-present flag, without union mark: correct for 1905-1940.

era-1940.note: Redrawn after the Commons Flag of Germany (1935–1945): red field, white disc, black swastika turned on its point.

era-1945.note: Red field, white-bordered navy Nordic cross, cross centre displaced toward the hoist; stripe order and offset match. Only fine proportions differ (navy band a little narrow).

era-995.note: Reference: red field with a crowned golden lion rampant holding a silver-bladed axe. Ours has a crowned gold lion holding an axe with a white blade, drawn crudely (head, mane and body proportions poor) on a brownish-red field; recognisable as the same emblem, with the detail and the flag-shaped format of the reference left out. Reconstruction in any case (the lion banner dates from about 1280; earlier banners such as the raven banner differed).

era-1884.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Caption: split of German colonial flag (left) and British/Australian ensign (right). German side reference (Reichskolonialflagge 1884-1914; Flag_of_Deutsch-Neuguinea.svg is the unimplemented 1914 proposal): black-white-red horizontal tricolour with a white disc holding the imperial eagle. The drawing has a cream field with only a small black and a small red bar at top-left and a black shapeless blob in place of the eagle, so the tricolour is not there. British side: Territory of Papua / British New Guinea Blue Ensign with a crowned disc lettering; the drawing shows only a canton on a blue half and no badge disc. The split device itself is the page own and is kept in the fix. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1920.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Caption says Australian Blue Ensign. The drawing is a plain blue field with a Union Jack canton and nothing else: the Australian Blue Ensign also has the large seven-point Commonwealth Star under the canton and the five-star Southern Cross on the fly. Commons territorial ensigns (Flag_of_the_Territory_of_New_Guinea.svg, Flag_of_the_Territory_of_Papua.svg) are Blue Ensigns with a crowned white disc lettered T.N.G. / PAPUA, which the drawing also does not show. The canton diagonals overshoot the canton edges. Fix draws the Australian Blue Ensign as captioned. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1975.note: The drawing is the Wikimedia Commons file 'Flag of Papua New Guinea.svg' (Public domain), with scripts, text and external links removed so it embeds in the page; its shapes and colours are the file's own.

era-1783.note: Plain red field matches the Commons plain red flag Wikipedia uses for Qatar, 18th century to 1860 (FOTW: plain red until about 1860). The last years of the era (c.1860-1868) had the narrow serrated white hoist stripe, which is not shown.

era-1868.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Plain red field. Wikipedia lists the plain red flag only for the 18th century to 1860; Commons 1860-1916 and FOTW (qa_his, fetched) give red with a narrow serrated white hoist stripe from about 1860, which covers 1868-1871. Fix draws that striped flag. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1916.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Drawing is a red field with a plain straight-edged white hoist band about 20% wide. The Commons flags for 1860-1916/1916-1932 and for 1932-36, 1936-49, 1949-71 all show a serrated white hoist stripe (the early one has about 10 points, band about 15-20% wide); the 1949-1971 file is the maroon nine-point flag. FOTW (qa_his, fetched) notes some sources claim the stripe was not originally serrated, but no reference image shows a plain straight band. Fix draws the red serrated 1916-32 form. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1971.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Layout, colours and hoist band match (maroon field, white band on the hoist with a serrated edge, about 30% of the length). But the serration is drawn with 7 notches (8 white points) where the reference, and Wikipedia ("nine points"), show nine white triangles; the caption itself says nine-point. Maroon is also much darker than the reference #8A1538. Minor count error. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1547.note: Gold field with a black double-headed eagle matches FOTW's description of the Emperor's vessel standard "yellow with black eagle" (page https://www.crwflags.com/fotw/flags/ru_tzar.html, fetched), which dates from 1699, so it is valid only for the last two decades (1699-1721) of this 1547-1721 era; for 1547-1699 the sources show other flags (1552 Saviour banner: dark red with an icon, stars and crosses; 1696 red armorial banner with a golden eagle; the 1693-99 tricolour with golden eagle). The real standard also has a coat of arms, scrolls and maps in the eagle's claws; ours is the eagle alone. Eagle itself is recognisable. The caption now says the standard is documented from 1699.

era-1721.note: Redrawn as the plain white-blue-red tricolour the sources document for 1721-1917. The earlier drawing added a golden double-headed eagle, which Flags of the World dates to the Tsar's standard of 1693-99 only.

era-1917.note: Reference: red field with the gold letters RSFSR in an ornate Slavic script set in a gold-bordered canton flush with the hoist and top edge. Ours: red field with gold Cyrillic lettering in a plain serif face inside a floating gold outline box; same content and position, lettering style and canton framing simplified.

era-1917-1.note: Plain white-blue-red tricolour as the reference; no eagle or crown, consistent with the Provisional Government use (Wikipedia and FOTW say it kept the tricolour; neither mentions a crown). Cream for white.

era-1922.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Reference (USSR flag): red field, gold-bordered red star above a gold hammer and sickle at the upper hoist. Ours has the star (filled gold rather than red with a gold outline) but the "hammer and sickle" is a horizontal bar, a rotated bar and a dot that does not read as a hammer and sickle. Fix draws a recognisable crossed hammer and sickle. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1991.note: White over blue over red in equal horizontal bands, same order and hues as the reference (white drawn cream).

era-1429.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Same drawing and same problems as the 1609 era: the crest renders as a solid gold disc on rust red, not three commas; the infobox flag for the kingdom is the yellow flame-edged pennant with red disc. Wikipedia also dates the crest to 1467 (Sho Toku), after this era starts. Fix draws the merchant pennant. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1609.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Drawing is a plain gold disc on a rust-red field. The caption says hidari mitsudomoe crest, but the three comma paths overlap into a solid disc, so the emblem is a blob (reference Hidari_mitsudomoe.svg is three commas). The red field is also unsupported: Wikipedia (Flag of Ryukyu) describes a 1798 flag with a white field and black mitsudomoe, and the Ryukyu Kingdom infobox flag (Commons Merchant_flag_of_the_Ryukyu_Kingdom) is a yellow right-triangle pennant with flame-edged red border and a red disc. Fix draws that merchant pennant. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1872.note: Drawing is Japan's sun-disc flag with a dashed gold border. Wikipedia's Ryukyu Domain infobox (wikitext fetched) gives the Hidari mitsudomoe (three-comma crest of the Second Sho family) as the domain's flag/mon and lists no Japanese flag; FOTW found no domain flag. Fix draws that crest (black on white), the only reference image for the domain. The caption now says which period the drawing fits.

era-1879.note: Red disc (diameter about 3/5 of the height) centred on a white field: same design as the Commons 1870-1999 flag of Japan, which the Wikipedia Ryukyu Kingdom infobox lists as the successor flag. Only the design was compared, not when it first flew in Okinawa.

era-1893.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Navy Blue Ensign with Union Jack canton and a badge disc on the fly is the right structure (references: 1906-1947 crown with lettering on a disc, 1947-1956 red turtle shield on a disc, 1956-1966 quartered shield on a disc, 1966-1977 shield without disc; Wikipedia gives a plain Union Jack for 1893-1906). The badge is wrong: a cream disc with a green leaf on a brown stem matches none of them (no crown, turtle or quartered shield). Canton diagonals also overshoot the canton. The era is long and several badges apply; the fix shows the 1956-1966 quartered shield on a disc. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1978.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Layout matches (blue upper-hoist triangle, green lower-fly triangle, yellow diagonal from lower hoist to upper fly, five white stars). The five stars are in the wrong arrangement: reference has a quincunx (four stars at the corners of a square plus one centre) in the hoist corner; the drawing scatters them in a loose pentagon across the triangle, one touching the stripe. Blue and green are lighter/brighter than the reference (cobalt blue, dark green) but the hue is right. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1498.note: Red saltire on white matches the Cross of Burgundy in colour and layout; the ragged edges are drawn as smooth bars. Wikipedia and FOTW date the cross as a Spanish ensign only to the 1670s (Commons Flag_of_Spain_(1701–1760) is royal arms on white) and no source ties it to Trinidad, so it is a stand-in for Spanish rule.

era-1797.note: Plain Blue Ensign with Union Jack canton, no badge. Looked at: Wikipedia Flag of Trinidad and Tobago, History of Trinidad and Tobago and Trinidad and Tobago image lists, Commons file search, FOTW tt_col (fetched: badge on the Blue Ensign dates from 1875 for Trinidad and 1870s for Tobago; no earlier ensign described). No image of a flag for 1797 to c.1870 exists in those sources, and the 1875-1889 part of the era had the round badge, which is not drawn.

era-1889.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Blue ensign with a Union Jack canton and a round badge at the fly is the right layout, but the badge is a teal five-point star on a cream disc. The Commons 1889-1958 badge is a white disc showing ships before a yellow mountain with a motto beneath (FOTW tt_col, fetched: the Trinidad seal badge). A generic star is the wrong emblem. Fix draws a simplified ship-and-mountain badge. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1962.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Colours and order are right (red field, black diagonal band edged in white). Geometry differs: the drawing runs the band along the corner-to-corner diagonal, so the corners cut it, it touches the left and right edges and is thin (black about 15% of the height). In the reference the whole band lies between the top and bottom edges (black at x 6-26% on the top edge, 74-94% on the bottom), steeper than the corner diagonal and wider (black about 21% of the height). Fix redraws the band to those measurements. It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1700.note: Caption calls it a reconstruction (white field, brown border, gold sun and star) but it has no source. The fetched FOTW Buganda page cites Pakenham (Lugard, 1892): the Kabaka flew a flag of two lances and a shield on a red ground, and the current Buganda flag (Commons Flag_of_Buganda.svg) is blue-white-blue with a shield, crossed spears and a lion; neither has a white field or a sun and star. The drawing contradicts the only described flag. The fix shows the described red ground with shield and lances (the only documented flag, 1892, applied here as a stand-in). It is a labelled reconstruction.

era-1894.note: The earlier drawing differed from the reference: Reference: navy Blue Ensign, Union Jack canton, yellow disc badge with the crowned crane among vegetation. The drawing has a dark teal-grey field that is not ensign blue and clashes with the navy canton, a cream (not yellow) disc with brown ring, and canton diagonals overshooting the canton. The crane, as redrawn, is recognisable and faces the right way; the field colour and disc colour are the mismatch. (Wikipedia dates the ensign from 1914.) It was redrawn from the reference.

era-1962.note: The drawing is the Wikimedia Commons file 'Flag of Uganda.svg' (Public domain), with scripts, text and external links removed so it embeds in the page; its shapes and colours are the file's own.

era-1969.note: Emblem redrawn by hand on 2026-10-25 and compared by eye with the reference: same layout and colours, emblem simplified (shape and detail reduced).

era-1949.note: Emblem redrawn by hand on 2026-10-25 and compared by eye with the reference: same layout and colours, emblem simplified (shape and detail reduced).

era-1616.note: Maroon field with a cream dragon line, which the caption calls a reconstructed emblem and not an attested state flag. I found no Commons file or page showing a banner of the Druk Desi state, so there is nothing to compare it with. The emblem was redrawn by hand on 2026-10-25.
